# Cowork sidebar

Plugin `@local/dsh-cowork-shell` (dsh 0.2.2-rc.1). It replaces the app's left sidebar with a MindsHub-style one:

- **Chat / Cowork / Code tabs** at the top. The tabs are the modes of the Modes add-on, in their order, three by default.
- **One New button per tab:** New chat, New task, New code task.
- **Per-tab sections:**
  - **Chat:** Model Arena.
  - **Cowork:** Automation tasks, Connectors, Skills.
  - **Code:** Connectors, Skills.

  Pages no tab claims, such as Plugins, show under every tab, and the **More** menu stays.
- **Your projects and conversations**: the app's own Projects list, unchanged.
- **Settings** at the bottom, unchanged.

It keeps the app's colours, icons, brand, collapse-to-rail, the narrow-window drawer and, on the Mac desktop app, the strip beside the window buttons.

## What a tab does

The tab you pick decides the mode of every **new** conversation, and the Chat / Cowork / Code drop-down disappears from the chat box while this sidebar is on.

- A conversation that has not sent a message yet follows the selected tab. This includes the empty conversation the app re-opens for "New chat", even if it had a different mode chosen on it earlier.
- At its first message, its mode is fixed to that tab's mode.
- Conversations that have already started keep their mode when you change tabs. To change one anyway, type `/mode <id>` in it.

This needs the Modes add-on. Without it, the tabs only switch which sections show. How it works: this add-on provides a small `coworkShell` service, and Modes checks for it. Modes reads a conversation's internal turn counter to tell whether it has started. If a future app version hides that counter, Modes treats every conversation as started, which is the old behaviour.

## Chat tab: no folders

Chat is for a conversation that lives on its own, not for work in a project folder. So on the **Chat** tab:

- **No pickers on the start page.** The "Default workspace" and "Standard mode" buttons above the chat box are hidden. Cowork and Code still show them.
- **New chat always starts in the app's default workspace** (the folder named `default-workspace`), even if a project conversation is open. The suggestion chips and the Mac's hidden-sidebar "new" button follow the same rule.
- **One flat list.** Recent chats show as a single list, pinned first, then newest first, with no project folders. Cowork and Code keep their project groups.
- **Promote.** The `⋯` on a chat offers:
  - **Promote to Cowork / Promote to Code**: the same conversation moves to that tab, and its mode switches from its next message. It stays in the default workspace, because this app version cannot move a conversation to another folder.
  - **Continue in a project…**: pick Cowork or Code (Code by default) and one of your projects. A **new** conversation opens in that project, on that tab, with the chat box filled in with a short line that mentions the chat the app's own way (`@[title](dsh-session:…)`). When you send it, the app attaches a read-only copy of the chat for the model, and the message shows "Referenced session". The original chat stays where it is.

Details:

- The pickers are hidden only while the Chat tab is open **and** the open conversation is in the default workspace (or nothing is open). If you start a conversation in another project while on the Chat tab (the app's own New Session shortcut can do this, or `+` under **Show all**), the pickers show, so you can see where you are.
- If the app has no `default-workspace` project, nothing is hidden and New chat behaves as before.
- The folder picker is hidden with CSS, by the app's seat name (`conversation.hero.workspace`). Switching the add-on off removes it.
- The preset picker (Standard, PTC, Minimal, Creator) is **not** hidden (since 0.20). It was hidden from 0.10 to 0.19, which left a new chat on the app's default preset with no way to see or change it. The preset decides how the model calls tools, and the app fixes it when a conversation starts: the label at the top of a started conversation is text, not a control.
- A conversation now shows in its tab's list right after its first message. Before, it could drop out of the list for up to 10 seconds.

## Conversations per tab

Each tab lists only its own conversations: **Recent chats** under Chat, **Recent tasks** under Cowork, **Code projects** under Code.
- Conversations are grouped under their project; a project appears in a tab when it has at least one conversation of that tab.
- Conversations outside any project come after, under "Other conversations".
- Pinned conversations come first, then newest first. Archived and helper (sub-agent) conversations are hidden, as in the app's own list. An empty new conversation shows only while it is open.

**Which tab a conversation belongs to** is the mode it runs in (recorded by the Modes add-on at its first message). Conversations from before that was recorded are placed by where they live:

| Where it lives | Tab |
| --- | --- |
| no project | Chat |
| the app's `default-workspace` | Cowork |
| any other project folder | Code |

**Moving:** the `⋯` button on a conversation moves it to another tab (on the Chat tab the same entries read "Promote to …", see above). The `⋯` on a project moves all its conversations. Moving also switches the conversation's mode from its next message, so the tab and the mode always agree. The `+` on a project starts a new conversation in it.

**Needs you:** when a conversation waits for you (an approval, a plan review or a question), a **Needs you (n)** block appears at the top of the list, on every tab. It names the conversation and what it waits for; clicking opens it at the question. The conversation's row shows an amber dot instead of the running dot. It reads the app's own status (`uiSession.sessionStatus`), the same one the app's sidebar uses, and shows nothing when that is unavailable. Answering stays in the app's own dialog.

**Archiving:** the same `⋯` on a conversation has **Archive**. It uses the app's own archive: the conversation leaves the list and nothing is deleted. One that is still working asks before it is stopped and archived. Archiving the open conversation starts a new one. Each tab ends with **Archived (n)**; open it to see that tab's archived conversations, each with **Restore**.

**Deleting:** the app has no way to delete a conversation, so this add-on adds one. **Delete** is in the same `⋯` menu and next to **Restore** in the Archived list. It asks first, archives the conversation, then moves its files (and those of its helper conversations) out of the app into `<app data folder>/trash/conversations`. Each tab ends with **Trash (n)**: every deleted conversation, the days it has left, and **Put back**, which returns it to the Archived list. After 30 days a deleted conversation is removed for good; the add-on checks at start and a few times a day.

- A conversation the app still holds in memory (one you used since the app started) leaves the lists at once, but its files move only at the next start of the app. Until then **Put back** simply shows it again.
- Only a folder that holds a stored conversation is ever moved, and only folders inside the trash are ever removed.
- Files the conversation created in your project folders are not touched. The app's search index and its record of which project the conversation belonged to are left to the app.
- Switching this add-on off, or uninstalling Plus, leaves the trash folder where it is; nothing in it is removed while the add-on is off.

Code: `lib/trash.js` (file moves, tested in `test/trash.test.mjs`), the `/dsh-cowork-shell/trash` route in `index.js` (GET lists, POST `{action: 'delete' | 'restore', sessionId, title}`).

**Show all** switches to the app's full list, with its search, rename, pin and archive menus. **<Tab> only** switches back. Each window remembers the choice.

The list reads the app's own project and conversation data in the browser. If that data is not available (a different app version), the sidebar falls back to the app's full list.

## Start page

- **Greeting per tab** instead of "Into the Unknown":
  - Chat and Cowork: "Let's knock something off your list"
  - Code: "What should we build?"

  The greeting sits in the start page's logo seat, and the stock title next to it is hidden only while a greeting shows. A tab with an empty greeting shows the stock title.
- **Suggestion chips** under the chat box, each with an icon: Create slides, Build website, Develop apps, Spreadsheet, Visualization, Wide research, Create games (Cowork and Code tabs). A chip fills the chat box with a starter prompt to finish and send. Chip icons: `slides`, `website`, `app`, `spreadsheet`, `chart`, `research`, `game`, `spark`.
- **New chat / task / code task** is drawn in the scheme's accent colour, with the app's own New Session shortcut as a badge (shown only when the app exposes one).
- In narrow windows the greeting wraps, and the chat-box Search and Deep research buttons shrink to icons.
- The **Search** and **Deep research** buttons in the chat box come from the Modes add-on.

**Logos, date and width.** The sidebar's **More** menu ends with three switches, saved with your settings:

- **Hide DeepSeek logos / Show DeepSeek logos** (`hideLogos`): removes the logo and name at the top of the sidebar and the logo on the start page.
- **Show the date as the title / Show the greeting as the title** (`dateTitle`): the start page title becomes today's date, written like "11 November, 2026" in English and as the language's own long date otherwise. It replaces the greeting on every tab.
- **Wide chat area / Normal chat area** (`wideChat`): the app keeps the conversation and the message box in a centred column about 800 pixels wide. This lets both use the width of the window (with a margin). The start page keeps its own size. It works through two CSS rules on the app's own class names (`_scrollBody` › `_column`, `_composerStack` › `_card`), so a later app version may need them adjusted.

All three are off by default. They do not change the app's icon, its window title or logos drawn by other parts of the app.

Change greetings and chips per tab with `greeting` and `chips` in the tab layout:

```yaml
- id: cowork-shell
  config:
    tabs: '{"cowork":{"greeting":"Hi, what are we doing today?","chips":[{"label":"Plan my week","prompt":"Help me plan my week: "}]}}'
```

Fields you leave out keep their defaults.

## Pages

- **Connectors** lists your MCP servers. In this app version, each server is one `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client` row. For each server the page shows:
  - what it runs or the address it reaches (no keys, tokens or secret-looking arguments)
  - whether it is on
  - how many tools it has registered right now ("Connected · N tools", or "No tools yet" while it starts or if it failed)

  The switch uses the app's own plugin on/off (the same one the Plugins page uses) and applies live. **Add a connector** is a short form that writes out the settings lines for a new server. You paste them at the end of `~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/cordis.patch.yml` and restart; the page does not edit that file itself. Keys never go in the form. Use `${credential:NAME}` in the lines.
- **Skills** is a searchable, read-only list of the skills found for your default folder, read the way the app's own "/" menu reads them for a new conversation ("Standard mode"). A project can add its own skills on top.
- **Model Arena** is the arena's page as a full page. That page comes from the Model arena add-on.

Data comes from two read-only routes, `GET /dsh-cowork-shell/connectors` and `GET /dsh-cowork-shell/skills`, behind the app's login and Host/Origin check, GET only and never cached. They serve names, descriptions, file paths and tool counts, never skill bodies, keys or environment values.

## Switching it off

On the **Plugins** page, switch **Cowork sidebar** off. The normal sidebar comes back at once; no restart is needed. Switching it on again works the same way.

The app must never run both sidebars at once, because it would not load. So the add-on does two things:

1. Its patch switches the app's own sidebar row (`ui-sidebar`) off.
2. The Cowork sidebar row switches itself on **only while** `ui-sidebar` is off.

The app reads `ui-sidebar` before this row, so rule 2 always sees its current state. Turning the app's own "Sidebar" row back on therefore also brings the normal sidebar back, and the Cowork sidebar stays out of the way.

**Do not switch off only the Cowork sidebar's inner row** (on its details page) while leaving the bundle on. The app's sidebar stays off, and you would have no sidebar at all. Use the bundle's main switch. If it happens anyway, run `Uninstall.command`, or remove the `cowork-shell` lines from `~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/cordis.patch.yml`.

## Configuration (optional)

```yaml
- id: cowork-shell
  config:
    # Which pages each tab lists, by page id, and the New button's label. JSON text.
    tabs: '{"chat":{"newLabel":"New chat","pages":["model-arena"]},"cowork":{"newLabel":"New task","pages":["schedules","automations","connectors","skills"]},"code":{"newLabel":"New code task","pages":["connectors","skills"]}}'
    maxTabs: 3        # 1 to 5; the first modes in order. A mode another add-on adds (Finance) gets a tab after these, whatever the limit
```

Page ids: `schedules` (Automation tasks), `automations` (Automation runs, from the Automations add-on), `plugins`, `model-arena` (from the Model arena add-on), `connectors` and `skills`. Pages that no tab lists show under every tab. A page whose add-on is not installed is simply left out.

## How it works

The left sidebar is one replaceable seat (`sidebar`) in the app's layout. This add-on's browser half fills it and declares the same inner seats the app's sidebar declares:

- `sidebar.workspaces`, `sidebar.settings` and `sidebar.footer.action`;
- the brand seats;
- `sidebar.panellist.actions` for the More menu, and the `sidebar.panel.icon` factory.

So the Projects list, Settings and every plugin's page row plug in as before. It uses the app's public services (`uiWorkspace.startSession`, `layout.toggleSidebar` and `layout.selectPanel`) and the app's UI library for icons and the menu. Each of these has a plain fallback. While the sidebar is hidden on the Mac desktop app, it also fills `shell.leading` with "open sidebar" and "new" buttons.

## Checked

In the throwaway web profile only, through the app's browser view:

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Fresh start | Cowork sidebar shown, app's own sidebar off, no errors |
| Tabs | Chat, Cowork and Code show their own New label and sections, with the app's icons and brand |
| A new chat started from the Chat tab | Ran in Chat mode (the model was offered no tools), and its mode was recorded (`sessionModes`) |
| The re-opened empty conversation had Cowork recorded on it | Followed the Chat tab, and Chat replaced Cowork at its first message |
| Chat-box mode drop-down | Hidden while the sidebar is on |
| Rapid tab clicks | The last click wins; a background refresh no longer undoes it |
| Pages per tab | Chat: Model Arena. Cowork: Automation tasks, Connectors, Skills. Code: Connectors, Skills. Plugins and More on every tab |
| Model Arena page | Rounds and blind columns shown, same as Settings → Arena |
| Skills page | Listed a test skill from the user skills folder plus a shared one; search filters. The route answers 401 without login and 405 to POST |
| Conversations per tab | Each tab listed only its own conversations, grouped by project. Moving a conversation from Cowork to Code took it out of Cowork (11 → 10) and put it under the same project in Code, and the move was saved. **Show all** switched to the app's full list and back. Helper (sub-agent) sessions stayed hidden |
| Start page | The greeting replaced the stock title, with the stock title hidden. The Code tab showed its own greeting. The chips sat under the chat box, and "Build website" filled it with "Build a website for:" |
| Connectors page | A local test MCP server (one `echo` tool) showed "Connected · 1 tool". The switch turned it off ("Off") and on again live, with the tool coming back and no restart. The add form produced exactly the row format that loaded the test server |
| Switching to Cowork afterwards | That chat stayed in Chat, and a new task started in Cowork |
| More menu | Showed the app's own items (Browse other plugins, Create your plugin) |
| Projects list, Settings | Plug in as before |
| Collapse | 56 px rail with icons and expand again |
| Narrow window | Drawer |
| Light and dark | Both checked |
| Plugins page switch, off and on live, each followed by a page reload | The right sidebar every time, never both, no "Failed to load plugins" |
| App's own sidebar row forced back on | Cowork sidebar stepped aside, app sidebar shown |

Chat tab changes (throwaway web profile, mock model):

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Chat tab start page | Both pickers hidden. Cowork and Code still show them |
| New chat while a Code project conversation was open | Opened in the default workspace |
| Chat list | One flat list, no project folders. Code and Cowork still grouped by project |
| First message in a new chat | Ran in Chat mode, was recorded as chat, and showed in the list within about 2 seconds |
| Promote to Cowork | The chat left the Chat list and showed under `default-workspace` on the Cowork tab |
| Continue in a project… (as Code) | Switched to the Code tab and opened a new conversation in the picked project with the mention filled in. After sending, it ran in Code mode (all tools, workspace-write), was recorded as code, showed "Referenced session", and its saved log held the chat's text as a read-only snapshot |
| Cowork tab `⋯` | Still reads "Move to Chat / Move to Code" |
| Browser console | No errors |

**Not checked:**

- "Continue in a project…" as Cowork (only Code was run), and with more than a handful of projects
- a chat title with unusual characters in the mention (brackets and backslashes are removed from the label)
- the Chinese wording on screen
- the app's own New Session keyboard shortcut on the Chat tab (it is the app's, so it still uses the current or most recent project)
- the Mac desktop app (window buttons, dragging the window by the sidebar, the hidden-sidebar buttons)
- keyboard-only use beyond the tab arrow keys
- Windows

An earlier Connectors design targeted a newer app's live MCP manager. Your installed version (0.2.2-rc.1) does not have it, so the page was rebuilt on what this version has: one MCP client row per server, and the plugin on/off switch.

An earlier version of the on/off rule failed the live switch-on test: both sidebars ended up on and the app did not load. That rule was replaced by the one above, which passed every case.

# DeepSeek Harness Plus

Extra features for the **DeepSeek Harness** desktop app on the Mac: a MindsHub-style sidebar with Chat, Cowork and Code tabs, colour schemes (including MindsHub's navy and teal), work modes, model tiers, a blind model arena, agent swarms, deep research, a usage counter, benchmarks, syncing between Macs and more. Twenty-six add-ons in all, listed in [docs/ADD-ONS.md](docs/ADD-ONS.md).

The add-ons plug into the normal app. Nothing in the app itself is changed, so app updates do not wipe them, and you can remove them at any time.

You do not need to know how to code to install or use this.

---

## What you need

- A Mac with the **DeepSeek Harness** app in your Applications folder, version **0.2.2 or newer, below 0.3**.
- Open the app **once** before installing, so it creates its settings, then quit it.

## Install

1. Download the newest **`DS-Harness-Plus-<version>.dmg`** from the [Releases page](https://github.com/BLCKHWK60/DS-Harness-Plus/releases/latest) and double-click it. A window opens with everything in it: all the add-ons, the installer and this guide. (If you use git, clone the project instead; it is the same folder.)
2. In that window, double-click **`Install.command`**.
   - The first time, macOS may say it "cannot be opened because it is from an unidentified developer". If it does, **right-click** the file, choose **Open**, then **Open** again. You only do this once.
3. A Terminal window opens and walks you through it. If the app is open, it asks to quit it. When it says **Done**, open DeepSeek Harness.

Installing copies the add-ons into the app's own data folder (`~/.dsh/addons`), so you can eject the disk image and delete the download afterwards. To remove the add-ons later, open the disk image again and double-click **`Uninstall.command`**.

Before it changes anything, the installer saves your current setup under `~/.dsh/backups/deepseek-harness-plus/`. If any step fails, it puts everything back by itself.

**Terminal instead:** if you prefer, run this from the unpacked folder:

```bash
bash scripts/install.sh
```

## First steps

1. **Add your models.** Go to **Settings → Models** in the app. You can paste an API key for a provider there, or add your own server (for example a model server on another computer). No files to edit.
2. **Look at the new pages.** **Settings** now has **Colours, Model Tiers, Modes, Sampling, Usage, Benchmark, Arena** and **Swarm** pages. The chat box (where you type) gets one **model button** beside the send button, with the model list, an effort slider from Off to Ultra Code, tiers and sampling, and, once set up, a model-health dot.
3. **Switch on what you want.** Some add-ons work right away. The others do nothing until you give them a little setup, for example which models the arena should compare. [docs/ADD-ONS.md](docs/ADD-ONS.md) says which is which and how to set each one up.

### What works the moment you install

- **Cowork sidebar:** Chat, Cowork and Code tabs at the top of the left sidebar. Each tab lists only its own conversations and projects, and has its own sections: Model Arena under Chat, and Automation tasks, Connectors (your MCP servers, with on/off switches) and Skills under Cowork and Code. The start page gets a greeting and suggestion chips. A tab picks the mode of new conversations, so the chat box no longer needs a mode drop-down. To get the normal sidebar back, switch **Cowork sidebar** off on the **Plugins** page.
- **Colours:** pick a colour scheme in **Settings → Colours**: DeepSeek Harness (the stock colours, the default), MindsHub Cowork, Graphite or Forest, each in light and dark.
- **Modes:** Chat, Cowork and Code modes, switchable per conversation, plus **Search** and **Deep research** buttons in the chat box.
- **Model Tiers:** one model button in the chat box: pick any model and drag the effort slider. Five starter tiers (Fast, Balanced, Deep, Creative, Code review) work at once on whatever model you use. No model is preconfigured.
- **Code map:** a compact map of the project a conversation works in, so the assistant looks things up instead of reading whole files. Plus four "reverse engineer" skills. Nothing to install.
- **Privacy:** switches off the app's usage reporting and the upload of a conversation when you rate an answer. `/privacy` shows the state.
- **Usage counter:** counts requests and tokens per day and model (never your text).
- **Deep research** and **Code power:** new tools and skills the assistant can use.

Everything else stays switched off until you set it up.

## Changing an add-on's settings

Some add-ons have their own page in **Settings** (Tiers, Modes, Sampling). The rest are set up in the app's settings file. To edit it:

1. Quit DeepSeek Harness.
2. In Finder press **⌘ Shift G**, paste `~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/` and press Return.
3. Make a copy of **`cordis.patch.yml`** first, as your own backup. Then open the original with TextEdit.
4. Paste in the block for the add-on you want, from its section in [docs/ADD-ONS.md](docs/ADD-ONS.md). Fill in the parts in `<ANGLE BRACKETS>`, save, and open the app.

The file is indentation-sensitive: use spaces, never tabs, and keep the lines lined up as in the example. If the app will not start after an edit, put your copy back.

## Updating

Download the newer version and double-click **`Install.command`** again. It replaces the add-ons and keeps your settings.

## Removing

Double-click **`Uninstall.command`**. It removes all twenty-two add-ons and their files. Your conversations and your models are not touched. Any settings you wrote for the add-ons stay in the settings file and do nothing; if you install again, they come back into effect.

## Using it on a second Mac

1. Install the DeepSeek Harness app on the other Mac and open it once.
2. Run **`Install.command`** there too.
3. Add your models in **Settings → Models**.
4. Optional: to keep the same **settings** on both Macs, use iCloud Drive (below).
5. Optional: to see the same **conversations** on both Macs, set up the **Sync** add-on (see [docs/ADD-ONS.md](docs/ADD-ONS.md#sync)). It needs a private git repository that both Macs can reach. Neither Mac has to be switched on for the other to sync.

### Same settings on both Macs, through iCloud Drive

The **Shared settings** add-on keeps the settings you change in the app's own pages in one file, `settings.json`, in a folder in iCloud Drive. Those settings are Modes, Model Tiers, the Cowork tabs, Sampling presets and Colours. Change something on one Mac and the other Mac picks it up within about a minute. The file never holds secrets: API keys, tokens and passwords stay on each Mac.

1. On the first Mac, double-click **`Install.command`** and answer **y** when it asks *"Share settings through iCloud Drive?"*. It uses the folder **iCloud Drive → DeepSeek Harness Plus**.
2. On the second Mac, do the same. When the app opens there, it takes the settings from the file. Its own earlier settings are kept in `~/.dsh/shared-settings/backups`.

To use another folder, or from Terminal: `bash scripts/install.sh --settings "<folder>"`. To stop sharing on one Mac: `bash scripts/install.sh --no-settings`. Type `/shared-settings` in a conversation to see what is shared and when it last synced.

**Good to know:**
- Not shared:
  - which conversation sits in which tab;
  - the tier a conversation uses;
  - which add-ons are switched on;
  - settings written by hand into the settings file rather than in a Settings page.
- If you change the same setting on both Macs at once, the copy in iCloud wins. The other value is kept in the backups folder.
- iCloud sometimes makes a copy such as `settings 2.json` when both Macs write at the same moment. `/shared-settings` tells you if one appears; check it, then delete it.

## Giving it to someone else

Send them the link to this project, https://github.com/BLCKHWK60/DS-Harness-Plus. They follow **Install** above. Nothing in here contains your addresses, keys or personal settings; every add-on starts empty.

## If something goes wrong

- **"DeepSeek Harness is not installed"**: the app must be in `/Applications` or `~/Applications`.
- **"No 'desktop' setup found"**: open the app once, quit it, and run the installer again.
- **"version ... works with version 0.2.2 up to 0.3"**: your app is newer or older than this release supports. Look for a newer DeepSeek Harness Plus.
- **The installer stopped with a problem**: it has already put everything back. The message names a log file; send that file to whoever helps you.
- **The app misbehaves after installing**: run **`Uninstall.command`**. Every install and uninstall also leaves a dated copy of your setup files in `~/.dsh/backups/deepseek-harness-plus/`, in case someone helping you needs them.
- **The app will not start after you edited the settings file**: put back the copy you made before editing.

## What is in this folder

| Folder or file | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `Install.command`, `Uninstall.command` | Double-click to install or remove. |
| `addons/` | The twenty-two add-ons. Each has a `README.md` with its full technical notes. |
| `docs/ADD-ONS.md` | What each add-on does and how to set it up. |

# Deep research

Host plugin `@local/dsh-deep-research` (dsh 0.2.2-rc.1). It adds one tool, `deep_research`, that the model can call for questions that need several sources. It wraps what dsh already has (child agents, the `web_search` / `web_fetch` tools and whichever search backend `dsh-web` uses); the new code is the orchestration and the citation check.

## How a run works

1. **Plan**: a planner child splits the question into 2 to `maxSubquestions` sub-questions (JSON).
2. **Research**: one searcher child per sub-question, in parallel (at most `maxParallel`, and never above the tier's sub-agent cap), each told to fetch every page it cites and to return findings `{claim, url, quote}` as JSON.
3. **Merge**: URLs are normalized (host lower-cased, fragment removed) and de-duplicated into numbered sources, up to `maxSources`.
4. **Write**: a writer child writes the report using only the numbered findings and cites `[n]`.
5. **Check**: the host verifies every `[n]` exists, and marks each source `fetched` (the searcher really called `web_fetch` on it), `search result only`, or `not fetched`. The result ends with a `## Sources` list and a `## Checks` list (unknown citations, unfetched sources, dropped findings, partial run, failures).

`requireFetched: true` drops any finding whose page the searcher did not fetch. If every searcher fails the tool errors; if time runs out the report covers what finished and says so.

**Wide mode** (`mode: "wide"`, with `items` and `columns`): one searcher per item returns one row; the tool returns CSV text (RFC 4180) with `Sources` (only pages that were fetched) and `Notes` columns. It does not write a file: save the text with your own file tool (so the sandbox applies) and use `present`.

## Models

With the Tier plugin, children use the role routes of the parent's tier: planner and writer `plan`, searchers `fast` (configurable `roles`). Without Tier, or when a role has no route, children use the parent's own route. The tool is registered with Tier's sub-agent gate (`registerSubagentTool`), so a tier with sub-agents disabled, or at its cap, refuses it. A research agent cannot call `deep_research` itself.

## Configuration

```yaml
- id: deep-research
  config:
    enabled: true
    toolName: deep_research
    roles: { planner: plan, searcher: fast, writer: plan }
    maxSubquestions: 6
    maxParallel: 4
    maxSources: 40
    maxMinutes: 20          # overall budget; the call may ask for less
    searchToolNames: [web_search]   # use other names for another search backend (for example an MCP one)
    fetchToolNames: [web_fetch]
    requireFetched: false
    wide: { maxRows: 500 }
```

Nothing user-specific is preset. Choose the search backend where it already lives (`dsh-web` settings); this plugin only names the tools whose use it audits.

## Not done

- **A money cap** (`maxCloudUsd`): dsh gives no prices to a plugin; use `maxMinutes`, `maxSources` and your provider's own limits.
- **A Settings page for backends** (the fork's Research settings cards): needs a typed Remote, like the other UI items skipped so far.
- **Quality**: the prompts are short and generic; research quality was not measured.

## Verified (rc.1, scripted mock model, throwaway home)

Plan, two parallel searchers that really called `web_fetch`, merge, writer, and checks: duplicate URLs merged (a URL with another host case and a fragment), a claimed-but-unfetched source marked `not fetched`, an unknown citation `[99]` flagged. `requireFetched` dropped unfetched findings. One junk searcher still gave a report; all junk gave a clear error. Wide mode produced a correct CSV (comma quoting, only fetched sources kept). With Tier: planner and writer ran on the `plan` route, searchers on `fast`; a tier with sub-agents disabled refused the tool. Note: a first run showed a runaway loop caused by my test mock, which led to the recursion guard.

## Not verified

Real web search and real model quality (every model call was scripted); the time budget actually expiring; the recursion guard against a real model calling the tool from a research agent; very large wide runs; Windows paths and proxies.

# DeepSeek Harness Plus

Extra features for the **DeepSeek Harness** desktop app on the Mac: a MindsHub-style sidebar with Chat, Cowork and Code tabs, colour schemes (including MindsHub's navy and teal), work modes, model tiers, a blind model arena, agent swarms, deep research, a usage counter, benchmarks, syncing between Macs and more. Twenty-six add-ons in all, listed in [docs/ADD-ONS.md](docs/ADD-ONS.md).

The add-ons plug into the normal app. Nothing in the app itself is changed, so app updates do not wipe them, and you can remove them at any time.

A window opens with everything in it: all the add-ons, the installer and this guide. (If you use git, clone the project instead; it is the same folder.)
2. In that window, double-click **`Install.command`**.
   - The first time, macOS may say it "cannot be opened because it is from an unidentified developer". If it does, **right-click** the file, choose **Open**, then **Open** again. You only do this once.
3. A Terminal window opens and walks you through it. If the app is open, it asks to quit it. When it says **Done**, open DeepSeek Harness.

Installing copies the add-ons into the app's own data folder (`~/.dsh/addons`), so you can eject the disk image and delete the download afterwards. To remove the add-ons later, open the disk image again and double-click **`Uninstall.command`**.

Before it changes anything, the installer saves your current setup under `~/.dsh/backups/deepseek-harness-plus/`. If any step fails, it puts everything back by itself.

**Terminal instead:** if you prefer, run this from the unpacked folder:

```bash
bash scripts/install.sh
```

## First steps

1. **Add your models.** Go to **Settings → Models** in the app. You can paste an API key for a provider there, or add your own server (for example a model server on another computer). No files to edit.

### What works the moment you install

- **Cowork sidebar:** Chat, Cowork and Code tabs at the top of the left sidebar. Each tab lists only its own conversations and projects, and has its own sections: Model Arena under Chat, and Automation tasks, Connectors (your MCP servers, with on/off switches) and Skills under Cowork and Code. The start page gets a greeting and suggestion chips. A tab picks the mode of new conversations, so the chat box no longer needs a mode drop-down. To get the normal sidebar back, switch **Cowork sidebar** off on the **Plugins** page.
- **Colours:** pick a colour scheme in **Settings → Colours**: DeepSeek Harness (the stock colours, the default), MindsHub Cowork, Graphite or Forest, each in light and dark.
- **Modes:** Chat, Cowork and Code modes, switchable per conversation, plus **Search** and **Deep research** buttons in the chat box.
- **Model Tiers:** one model button in the chat box: pick any model and drag the effort slider. Five starter tiers (Fast, Balanced, Deep, Creative, Code review) work at once on whatever model you use. No model is preconfigured.
- **Code map:** a compact map of the project a conversation works in, so the assistant looks things up instead of reading whole files. Plus four "reverse engineer" skills. Nothing to install.
- **Privacy:** switches off the app's usage reporting and the upload of a conversation when you rate an answer. `/privacy` shows the state.
- **Usage counter:** counts requests and tokens per day and model (never your text).
- **Deep research** and **Code power:** new tools and skills the assistant can use.

Everything else stays switched off until you set it up.

## Changing an add-on's settings

Some add-ons have their own page in **Settings** (Tiers, Modes, Sampling). The rest are set up in the app's settings file. To edit it:

1. Quit DeepSeek Harness.
2. In Finder press **⌘ Shift G**, paste `~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/` and press Return.
3. Make a copy of **`cordis.patch.yml`** first, as your own backup. Then open the original with TextEdit.
4. Paste in the block for the add-on you want, from its section in [docs/ADD-ONS.md](docs/ADD-ONS.md). Fill in the parts in `<ANGLE BRACKETS>`, save, and open the app.

The file is indentation-sensitive: use spaces, never tabs, and keep the lines lined up as in the example. If the app will not start after an edit, put your copy back.

## Updating

Download the newer version and double-click **`Install.command`** again. It replaces the add-ons and keeps your settings.

## Removing

Double-click **`Uninstall.command`**. It removes all twenty-two add-ons and their files. Your conversations and your models are not touched. Any settings you wrote for the add-ons stay in the settings file and do nothing; if you install again, they come back into effect.

## Using it on a second Mac

1. Install the DeepSeek Harness app on the other Mac and open it once.
2. Run **`Install.command`** there too.
3. Add your models in **Settings → Models**.
4. Optional: to keep the same **settings** on both Macs, use iCloud Drive (below).
5. Optional: to see the same **conversations** on both Macs, set up the **Sync** add-on (see [docs/ADD-ONS.md](docs/ADD-ONS.md#sync)). It needs a private git repository that both Macs can reach. Neither Mac has to be switched on for the other to sync.

The **Shared settings** add-on keeps the settings you change in the app's own pages in one file, `settings.json`, in a folder in iCloud Drive. Those settings are Modes, Model Tiers, the Cowork tabs, Sampling presets and Colours. Change something on one Mac and the other Mac picks it up within about a minute. The file never holds secrets: API keys, tokens and passwords stay on each Mac.

1. On the first Mac, double-click **`Install.command`** and answer **y** when it asks *"Share settings through iCloud Drive?"*. It uses the folder **iCloud Drive → DeepSeek Harness Plus**.
2. On the second Mac, do the same. When the app opens there, it takes the settings from the file. Its own earlier settings are kept in `~/.dsh/shared-settings/backups`.

To use another folder, or from Terminal: `bash scripts/install.sh --settings "<folder>"`. To stop sharing on one Mac: `bash scripts/install.sh --no-settings`. Type `/shared-settings` in a conversation to see what is shared and when it last synced.

**Good to know:**
- Not shared:
  - which conversation sits in which tab;
  - the tier a conversation uses;
  - which add-ons are switched on;
  - settings written by hand into the settings file rather than in a Settings page.
- If you change the same setting on both Macs at once, the copy in iCloud wins. The other value is kept in the backups folder.
- iCloud sometimes makes a copy such as `settings 2.json` when both Macs write at the same moment. `/shared-settings` tells you if one appears; check it, then delete it.

## Giving it to someone else

Send them the link to this project, https://github.com/BLCKHWK60/DS-Harness-Plus. They follow **Install** above. Nothing in here contains your addresses, keys or personal settings; every add-on starts empty.

## If something goes wrong

- **"DeepSeek Harness is not installed"**: the app must be in `/Applications` or `~/Applications`.
- **"No 'desktop' setup found"**: open the app once, quit it, and run the installer again.
- **"version ... works with version 0.2.2 up to 0.3"**: your app is newer or older than this release supports. Look for a newer DeepSeek Harness Plus.
- **The installer stopped with a problem**: it has already put everything back. The message names a log file; send that file to whoever helps you.
- **The app misbehaves after installing**: run **`Uninstall.command`**. Every install and uninstall also leaves a dated copy of your setup files in `~/.dsh/backups/deepseek-harness-plus/`, in case someone helping you needs them.
- **The app will not start after you edited the settings file**: put back the copy you made before editing.

## What is in this folder

| Folder or file | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `Install.command`, `Uninstall.command` | Double-click to install or remove. |
| `addons/` | The twenty-two add-ons. Each has a `README.md` with its full technical notes. |
| `docs/ADD-ONS.md` | What each add-on does and how to set it up. |
| `docs/HOW-IT-WORKS.md` | For technical readers: how the install works, how to test, how to change an add-on. |
| `templates/` | Optional ready-to-fill examples: model servers, memory, MCP tool servers, backups. |
| `extras/dsh-intel-mcp/` | Optional Python tools (code map, reverse engineering, context store). Needs Python; not installed automatically. |
| `scripts/` | What the `.command` files run. |
| `VERSION` | This release's version number. |
| `LICENSE` | The MIT licence: anyone may use, change and share this. |

- **Live start:** the app starts with every add-on loaded.
- **Add-ons:** each has its own automated tests, and each settings page was checked in the app's web version.
- **Not yet tested on another person's Mac.** Each add-on's `README.md` lists what was and was not verified for it.

# Diagram builder

Lets a model draw accurate diagrams. The model says what is in the diagram; this add-on does the layout, the drawing and a check. It works the moment it is installed, with nothing to install and nothing leaving the Mac.

## Why it works this way

A model that writes a picture by hand gets positions wrong: text spills out of boxes, boxes overlap, arrows miss. Here the model never writes coordinates. It sends a description (boxes and arrows, branches, messages, events, numbers, formulas), and the add-on:

1. measures the text and sizes every box to fit it;
2. lays the diagram out (layers for flowcharts, with arrows routed around boxes; room per branch for trees; rows for sequences and timelines; axes with round steps for charts);
3. checks the result for anything a reader would stumble over, and tells the model, so it can fix the description and draw again;
4. shows the picture in the chat and saves it as an SVG file.

The drawing is exact. What goes into it is still the model's: a diagram is only as right as the description.

## What it draws

| Kind | For | In the description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `flow` | processes, causes, decisions, how parts connect | `nodes` (id, label, shape, colour, group), `edges` (from, to, label, dashed), `direction` |
| `tree` | hierarchies, outlines, mind maps | `root` with nested `children`, `direction` |
| `sequence` | parties exchanging messages in order | `actors`, `steps` (messages, replies, notes) |
| `timeline` | events in time order | `events` (when, title, text) |
| `chart` | numbers and formulas | bars or lines over `categories`; points or lines over numbers; `functions` to plot formulas in x |

Shapes: box, round, pill, diamond, note. Colours: gray, purple, teal, coral, blue, amber, green.

Formulas are read by a small calculator that never runs code. It knows x, `+ - * / ^`, brackets, `pi`, `e`, and sin, cos, tan, asin, acos, atan, sinh, cosh, tanh, sqrt, cbrt, abs, exp, ln, log, log2, floor, ceil, round, sign. `2x` and `3(x+1)` mean multiplication. A curve is lifted where the formula has no value or leaps across the picture, so `1/x` is drawn as two branches, not joined by a line.

## What the model gets

- Tool `diagram_draw`. Its answer holds the saved file, a text outline of what was drawn (every box, arrow and number, so a model that cannot see pictures can still check its work), and any problems to fix.
- Skill `draw-diagram`, loaded only when used: which kind to pick, to keep diagrams small and labels short, never to invent boxes or numbers, one example per kind, and to read the outline and fix problems.

Mistakes in a description are answered in sentences, for example: `An arrow uses "c", which is not the id of any box. The ids are: a, b.`

## The check

After layout, the add-on looks for: boxes that overlap; text that does not fit its box; an arrow label sitting on a box or on another label; a group's frame covering a box that is not in the group; groups overlapping; many arrows crossing; a picture that is very large; anything outside the picture. It also warns about crowded diagrams, boxes with no arrow, and formulas drawn without a chosen range.

## Where the picture goes

- **In the chat:** as the row for the tool call while the model works, and again under the finished turn, because the app folds tool steps away once a turn is done. If the model drew a diagram, fixed it and drew it again under the same name, only the last version is shown there. The picture in the chat always uses the app's light or dark colours. Click it for full size.
- **As a file:** in a `diagrams` folder inside the conversation's folder, named after the title. A new title that is already taken gets a number; when the model names the file itself, it replaces its own earlier drawing. A file that this add-on did not write is never replaced.

**Settings → Diagrams:** the master switch, save as a file or not, the folder's name, and the colours of the saved file (automatic follows light or dark mode of whatever shows it).

## For developers

- `lib/spec.js` reads and checks a description. `lib/flow.js`, `tree.js`, `sequence.js` (sequences and timelines), `chart.js` lay out one kind each and return `{width, height, body, boxes, labels, crossings, outline}`. `lib/draw.js` ties them together and holds the check. `lib/svg.js` measures text and writes the document. `lib/expr.js` reads formulas.
- Service `diagrams` (apiVersion 1): `draw(description)` returns `{ok, errors}` or `{ok, kind, title, width, height, outline, problems, svg(options)}`. Meant for other add-ons.
- Routes: `GET /dsh-diagram/status`; `GET /dsh-diagram/svg` with header `x-dsh-diagram` (and `x-dsh-theme`); `GET /dsh-diagram/list` with headers `x-dsh-session`, `x-dsh-from`, `x-dsh-to` for the drawings of one turn.
- Client slots: `tool.call.toolview` keyed `diagram_draw`, `conversation.chat.turnTail`, `settings.section`. Pictures are shown as images from a blob, which cannot run scripts.
- A list of drawings (id, conversation, time, file) is kept under the dsh home in `diagrams/index.json`, capped at 600, so pictures still show after a restart if they were saved.

## Checked

- **Unit tests:** 10 (`test/`): formulas (and that names such as `constructor` are refused); text measuring and wrapping; error sentences; flowcharts in both directions with a loop, a decision, a group and a self-arrow; 250 random flowcharts in which no two boxes may overlap and every picture must be well-formed; trees, sequences, timelines; charts placed from the numbers (a bar for 210 on an axis to 250 is exactly 210/250 of the height); the check on a deliberately messy drawing; themes and escaping; file names and never replacing someone else's file; every example in the skill draws without problems.
- **By eye:** all five kinds rendered to pictures and looked at, in light and dark.
- **Live, in the throwaway web profile with a test model server:** the tool reached the model, a flowchart was drawn, and the picture appeared in the chat under the finished turn in the app's dark colours; the settings page saved a change.
- **Not checked:** a real model writing descriptions; saving into a conversation's folder from inside the app (the lab had saving off so as not to write into a real folder; the saving code itself is unit-tested); very large diagrams; right-to-left and non-Latin text (widths are estimated for Latin letters); the Mac desktop app.

## Limits

- Text widths are estimates, set a little wide. Unusual fonts or scripts can still differ.
- Flowchart layout aims for few crossings but does not guarantee the fewest. Dense graphs with many arrows will cross; the check says so.
- Labels on arrows that leave or reach the same box can sit close together.
- No pie charts, no stacked bars, no two vertical axes, no free-form drawings (anatomy, circuits, maps).

- **Privacy:** switches off the app's usage reporting and the upload of a conversation when you rate an answer. `/privacy` shows the state.
- **Usage counter:** counts requests and tokens per day and model (never your text).
- **Deep research** and **Code power:** new tools and skills the assistant can use.

Everything else stays switched off until you set it up.

## Changing an add-on's settings

Some add-ons have their own page in **Settings** (Tiers, Modes, Sampling). The rest are set up in the app's settings file. To edit it:

1. Quit DeepSeek Harness.
2. In Finder press **⌘ Shift G**, paste `~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/` and press Return.
3. Make a copy of **`cordis.patch.yml`** first, as your own backup. Then open the original with TextEdit.
4. Paste in the block for the add-on you want, from its section in [docs/ADD-ONS.md](docs/ADD-ONS.md). Fill in the parts in `<ANGLE BRACKETS>`, save, and open the app.

The file is indentation-sensitive: use spaces, never tabs, and keep the lines lined up as in the example. If the app will not start after an edit, put your copy back.

## Updating

Download the newer version and double-click **`Install.command`** again. It replaces the add-ons and keeps your settings.

## Removing

Double-click **`Uninstall.command`**. It removes all twenty-two add-ons and their files. Your conversations and your models are not touched. Any settings you wrote for the add-ons stay in the settings file and do nothing; if you install again, they come back into effect.

## Using it on a second Mac

1. Install the DeepSeek Harness app on the other Mac and open it once.
2. Run **`Install.command`** there too.
3. Add your models in **Settings → Models**.
4. Optional: to keep the same **settings** on both Macs, use iCloud Drive (below).
5. Optional: to see the same **conversations** on both Macs, set up the **Sync** add-on (see [docs/ADD-ONS.md](docs/ADD-ONS.md#sync)). It needs a private git repository that both Macs can reach. Neither Mac has to be switched on for the other to sync.

### Same settings on both Macs, through iCloud Drive

The **Shared settings** add-on keeps the settings you change in the app's own pages in one file, `settings.json`, in a folder in iCloud Drive. Those settings are Modes, Model Tiers, the Cowork tabs, Sampling presets and Colours. Change something on one Mac and the other Mac picks it up within about a minute. The file never holds secrets: API keys, tokens and passwords stay on each Mac.

1. On the first Mac, double-click **`Install.command`** and answer **y** when it asks *"Share settings through iCloud Drive?"*. It uses the folder **iCloud Drive → DeepSeek Harness Plus**.
2. On the second Mac, do the same. When the app opens there, it takes the settings from the file. Its own earlier settings are kept in `~/.dsh/shared-settings/backups`.

To use another folder, or from Terminal: `bash scripts/install.sh --settings "<folder>"`. To stop sharing on one Mac: `bash scripts/install.sh --no-settings`. Type `/shared-settings` in a conversation to see what is shared and when it last synced.

**Good to know:**
- Not shared:
  - which conversation sits in which tab;
  - the tier a conversation uses;
  - which add-ons are switched on;
  - settings written by hand into the settings file rather than in a Settings page.
- If you change the same setting on both Macs at once, the copy in iCloud wins. The other value is kept in the backups folder.
- iCloud sometimes makes a copy such as `settings 2.json` when both Macs write at the same moment. `/shared-settings` tells you if one appears; check it, then delete it.

## Giving it to someone else

Send them the link to this project, https://github.com/BLCKHWK60/DS-Harness-Plus. They follow **Install** above. Nothing in here contains your addresses, keys or personal settings; every add-on starts empty.

## If something goes wrong

- **"DeepSeek Harness is not installed"**: the app must be in `/Applications` or `~/Applications`.
- **"No 'desktop' setup found"**: open the app once, quit it, and run the installer again.
- **"version ... works with version 0.2.2 up to 0.3"**: your app is newer or older than this release supports. Look for a newer DeepSeek Harness Plus.
- **The installer stopped with a problem**: it has already put everything back. The message names a log file; send that file to whoever helps you.
- **The app misbehaves after installing**: run **`Uninstall.command`**. Every install and uninstall also leaves a dated copy of your setup files in `~/.dsh/backups/deepseek-harness-plus/`, in case someone helping you needs them.
- **The app will not start after you edited the settings file**: put back the copy you made before editing.

## What is in this folder

| Folder or file | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `Install.command`, `Uninstall.command` | Double-click to install or remove. |
| `addons/` | The twenty-two add-ons. Each has a `README.md` with its full technical notes. |
| `docs/ADD-ONS.md` | What each add-on does and how to set it up. |
| `docs/HOW-IT-WORKS.md` | For technical readers: how the install works, how to test, how to change an add-on. |
| `templates/` | Optional ready-to-fill examples: model servers, memory, MCP tool servers, backups. |
| `extras/dsh-intel-mcp/` | Optional Python tools (code map, reverse engineering, context store). Needs Python; not installed automatically. |
| `scripts/` | What the `.command` files run. |
| `VERSION` | This release's version number. |
| `LICENSE` | The MIT licence: anyone may use, change and share this. |

## Status

Release 0.29.2 (the version in `VERSION`). Tested so far:

- **Install, update and uninstall:** run on a fresh setup and on a copy of a real, long-used setup.
- **Live start:** the app starts with every add-on loaded.
- **Add-ons:** each has its own automated tests, and each settings page was checked in the app's web version.
- **Not yet tested on another person's Mac.** Each add-on's `README.md` lists what was and was not verified for it.

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# Self-improvement

Plugin `@local/dsh-evolve` (dsh 0.2.2-rc.1). It makes a model better at your kind of work by improving the **instructions it is given**, never the model itself.

- You supply **test tasks** and how to tell a good result.
- A **reviewer model** studies what goes wrong and proposes small changes.
- Each change is tested on tasks the reviewer never saw. It only reaches you if it measurably helps and breaks nothing.
- **You approve every change.** Every version is kept and can be put back with one click.

Nothing is preconfigured: it does nothing until you pick a model and add tasks on **Settings → Self-improvement**.

## One set of lessons per model version (0.13)

**What to improve** on the page is either a plain model or a saved **model version** from Model Tiers. Each version has its own tasks, lessons, scores and history (kept in `versions/<id>/` inside the data folder), so "Qwen – Coding" and "Qwen – Writing" improve separately.

- Test runs use the version's model, its temperature and max tokens, and its own instructions in front of the lessons under test.
- Approved lessons for a version are used only in conversations that are on that version. The plain model's lessons are used in every conversation, unless the version in use says "Use only these".
- This is how the loop tunes a version's instructions for a job: write the starting instructions on the version, add tasks for that job, and let the loop add lessons on top.

Checked live with the mock model: choosing a version gave an empty task list of its own; a cycle ran on the version's model; the approved lesson was stored for that version and arrived in a conversation on it. Not checked: two versions improved side by side.

## How to use it

1. **Setup.** Pick the model to improve (usually a local one) and a stronger model as reviewer. Both come from your model list in Settings → Models.
2. **Tasks.** Add tasks from your real work, or press **Add example tasks** and tick the sets you want (see "Example tasks" below). Each task has a prompt, a "kind of work" name, one or more checks, and a group:

   | Group | What it is for | Does the reviewer see it? |
   | --- | --- | --- |
   | Learn | The reviewer studies what fails here | Yes: the prompt, an answer and why it failed |
   | Check | Proves that a change helps | Never |
   | Guard | Things that work today and must keep working | Never |

3. **Measure** runs every task several times and shows the score.
4. **Run a cycle** measures, asks the reviewer, and tests each proposed change. Changes that clear every gate appear under **Changes waiting for you** with the reason and each gate's result. **Approve and use** makes a new version; **Decline** drops it.

`/evolve` in a chat shows the state; `/evolve measure`, `/evolve improve` and `/evolve stop` do the same as the buttons.

### Checks

Every check of a task must pass. A check that cannot be decided never counts as a pass.

| Check | Passes when |
| --- | --- |
| `contains` / `notContains` | the answer contains / does not contain a text |
| `noneOf` | the answer contains none of a list of words or marks, written as `delve \| tapestry \| **` |
| `equals` | the answer is exactly a text |
| `regex` | the answer matches a pattern |
| `json` | the answer is valid JSON, optionally with the listed keys |
| `wordCount`, `lineCount` | the answer has a number of words / non-empty lines: one number (`12`) or a range (`150-220`) |
| `fileExists`, `fileContains` | a file exists / contains a text in the task's folder (tasks with tools) |
| `judge` | the judge model gives 4 or 5 out of 5 against your description |

### Example tasks

**Add example tasks** opens a list of ready-made sets. Tick any of them and press **Add ticked**; **Select all** ticks every set; **Remove ticked** takes a set's tasks out again. Tasks you already have are left alone. Each set is spread over Learn, Check and Guard.

| Set | Tasks | What it tests | Needs |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Reasoning and exact calculation | 16 | counting, long arithmetic, dates, logic puzzles, state tracking | |
| Reading and tracing code | 16 | what JavaScript, Python and SQL snippets print, with the usual traps | |
| Structured output and extraction | 12 | exact JSON from messy text: totals, dates, phone numbers, units, versions | |
| Following exact instructions | 12 | several formatting rules at once | |
| General knowledge, two steps | 14 | two facts combined into one exact answer | |
| Writing | 14 | technical writing, blog, web copy, fiction, literary description, e-mail, news, poem | a judge model |
| Tool use | 10 | create files, run code, leave an exact result in a file | an open Cowork or Code conversation |
| Agentic coding | 10 | write a program, run it, leave the result and a README | an open Cowork or Code conversation |

Every answer with one right value was worked out by code, and `test/packs.test.mjs` works each one out again. A writing task passes only when the text is inside its length, contains none of a list of machine-sounding phrases and marks (`AI_ISMS` in `lib/packs.js`: "delve", "tapestry", em dashes, bold, headings and so on), and the judge model gives it 4 or 5. Without a judge model, writing tasks are never counted as passed.

Lessons learned on a set are used in every real conversation, like lessons for "general" work.

The sets live in `lib/packs.js`. They are meant to be hard for local models; how hard they are for a given model is only known after you press Measure.

### Two ways a task can run

- **Answer only:** the model answers in one go, without tools. Fast, and enough for most checks.
- **With tools:** a fresh helper agent does the task with the app's tools. It needs an open Cowork or Code conversation, because helpers belong to a conversation. The app's sandbox only lets a helper write inside that conversation's folder, so each run gets an empty temporary folder there (`.dsh-evolve-test/…`), removed when the run ends. Runs are one at a time, with a five-minute limit each.

## What it can and cannot change

It can change one thing: the **policy**, which is
- a **playbook** of short lessons (at most 600 characters each, at most 60), each for one kind of work or for all;
- up to six **sections** of standing instructions (at most 2,000 characters each).

A change is one bounded edit: add, reword or remove one lesson, or replace one section. The whole text is never rewritten. A change that says almost the same as what is already there is refused.

It cannot change the model, the tasks, the checks, the gates or its own settings. The reviewer's answer is only ever read as a list of edits; nothing in it is run.

## The gates

A proposed change is tested on the Check and Guard tasks, the same number of runs as before, and compared task by task (`lib/gates.js`):

1. **Does not carry a test answer.** It may not name a task or contain an expected answer of any task.
2. **Helps on the Check tasks.** More runs pass than before.
3. **Breaks nothing on the Guard tasks.** No task that passed in at least two thirds of its runs now passes in one third or fewer.
4. **Does not make answers much longer.** Typical answer length stays under 150% of before (`costCeiling`).
5. **You approve it.**

Without at least one Check task and one Guard task, a cycle does not start: an improvement could not be proven.

## Where the approved instructions are used

With "Use approved instructions in real conversations" on (the default), every conversation gets the lessons for `all` and `general` work, plus those whose kind of work is named like its mode (`chat`, `cowork`, `code`), as one prompt section (`evolve:notes`, order 72). The text is in a fixed order, so it stays the same between requests and a model server can keep it cached. Switch it off to try the loop without changing how the app behaves.

## What leaves this Mac

Only what the reviewer needs: for up to 12 Learn tasks that do not pass reliably, the prompt, one answer the model gave and why it failed, plus the current policy and the outcome of earlier proposals. API keys, bearer tokens, private keys, e-mail addresses and home-folder paths are replaced before sending. If the reviewer is a cloud model, that text goes to its provider through the app's own model service; this add-on holds no keys. Conversations, Check tasks and Guard tasks are never sent.

## What changed from the research spec

The spec ("DSH Self-Improvement Loop Plugin — Research & Spec") was checked against the installed app. What holds: the harness is the right place to improve; a strong model must own the reviewing; the evaluation must be out of the loop's reach; `agent/turn-stopping` can keep a turn open (a listener steers the agent); helper agents accept their own folder and model.

| Spec | This build | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Separate Anthropic client, Batch API, prompt caching | The reviewer is any model from the app's model list | No keys to handle, nothing to install; works with a local or cloud reviewer. Batch and cache discounts are not available through the app |
| Python SDK / headless eval runner on another Mac | Test runs inside the app: direct model calls, or helper agents | Nothing to install. The cost: runs share the app with you |
| Train / held-in / held-out / canary | Learn / Check / Guard | Same idea in plain words. No public canary set |
| Seven gates | Four automatic gates plus your approval, always | Sandbox and plugin-test gates belong to levels that are not built. No live canary with automatic rollback yet |
| Every candidate is a git-tracked folder | Every version is a JSON file that is never overwritten | No git dependency; same guarantee |
| Nightly outer loop, monthly meta loop | You press Run a cycle | Keeps it predictable. A schedule can call `/evolve improve` later |
| Levels 0–6 | Levels 1 and 2: instruction sections and the playbook | See below |

**Not built, on purpose:** reviewer-written tools, skills and plugins (levels 3–4), the loop improving its own reviewer prompt (level 5), and weight training (level 6). They run or train on model-written output, which needs a real sandbox and, for training, a licence answer. They also only make sense once this measuring loop has proven itself on your tasks. Also not built: mining your real conversations for failures (only test tasks are used), verify-before-stop in live conversations, best-of-N, helpful/harmful counters per lesson, and a Pareto archive.

**Its honest limit:** it cannot make a small model reason like a large one on work it has never seen. Gains show on kinds of work you repeat and can check. With few tasks, a lucky run can pass the gates; ten or more tasks per kind of work and three runs each make that unlikely.

## Configuration

```yaml
- id: evolve
  config:
    enabled: true
    studentProvider: <ROUTE>        # the model to improve; set on the page
    studentModel: <MODEL ID>
    reviewerProvider: <ROUTE>       # the reviewer; set on the page
    reviewerModel: <MODEL ID>
    judgeProvider: <ROUTE>          # optional, for "judge" checks
    judgeModel: <MODEL ID>
    repeats: 3                      # runs per task, 1 to 5
    maxEdits: 3                     # changes tried per cycle, 1 to 5
    tokenBudget: 400000             # tokens per run, all models; 0 = no limit. A run that reaches it stops and changes nothing
    costCeiling: 1.5                # how much longer answers may get
    applyLive: true                 # use approved instructions in real conversations
    dataDir: <ABSOLUTE_DIR>         # optional; default is `evolve` in the dsh home
    commandName: evolve
```

All but `dataDir` and `commandName` are edited on the page and apply at once.

## Files

`index.js` wires the app: the prompt section, model calls, helper agents, jobs, the `evolve` service (`active()`, `notes(family)`, `status()`), the command and two fenced routes (`GET /dsh-evolve/status`, `POST /dsh-evolve/action`; login and Host/Origin check, a required header, a 64 KB JSON body, listed actions only). The logic is in `lib/` and has no app dependency: `verify.js` (checks), `policy.js` (the policy and its edits), `gates.js`, `review.js` (what the reviewer is sent and how its answer is read), `store.js` (files), `engine.js` (measure, improve, approve).

Data folder (`$DSH_HOME/evolve`): `tasks.json`, `policies/v0001.json …`, `active.json`, `results/<version>.json`, `candidates.json`, `history.json`.

## Checked

- **Unit tests:** 29 (`test/`): the example sets (every expected answer and file worked out again, a wrong answer fails, 10 to 30 tasks per set), every check type, path escapes in file checks, the policy and its limits, leak detection, each gate, redaction, the reviewer packet (it contains no Check or Guard task), strict reading of the reviewer's answer, storage, a full simulated cycle with approval and going back, budget stop, refusals.
- **Live, in the throwaway web profile with a scripted mock model:**
  - Set up entirely on the page: both models picked, example tasks added (0.15: the tick-box list; adding two sets, then removing one, changed the task count as expected).
  - A cycle from a 33% score: the reviewer proposed two lessons; the useful one cleared all four gates and waited; the useless one was stopped by "helps on the check tasks"; nothing changed until Approve.
  - After Approve: version v0002 in use, measured 100%; both versions listed with their scores; going back to v0001 and forward again worked.
  - The approved lesson was in the request of a normal Code conversation (read from the request the mock received).
  - A task with tools: the helper agent wrote a file in its temporary folder, the file check passed 3 of 3, and the folder was gone afterwards. The first attempt, with a folder outside the conversation's folder, was refused by the app's sandbox; that is why the folder is where it is.
  - The action route answered 400 without its header, 405 to GET, 400 to an unknown action and to a task id with `../`.
  - No page errors; the page follows `docs/UI-STYLE.md` (seen in the Forest scheme, light and dark).
  - `/evolve` typed in a chat printed the version in use and the last score.

**Not checked:** a real local model and a real reviewer (the gains shown are from a scripted mock, so they prove the machinery, not an improvement); `judge` checks with a real judge; the token allowance stopping a real run (unit-tested); `/evolve measure` and `/evolve improve` typed in a chat; the page in other colour schemes; the Mac desktop app.

# DeepSeek Harness Plus

Extra features for the **DeepSeek Harness** desktop app on the Mac: a MindsHub-style sidebar with Chat, Cowork and Code tabs, colour schemes (including MindsHub's navy and teal), work modes, model tiers, a blind model arena, agent swarms, deep research, a usage counter, benchmarks, syncing between Macs and more. Twenty-six add-ons in all, listed in [docs/ADD-ONS.md](docs/ADD-ONS.md).

The add-ons plug into the normal app. Nothing in the app itself is changed, so app updates do not wipe them, and you can remove them at any time.

You do not need to know how to code to install or use this.

---

## What you need

- A Mac with the **DeepSeek Harness** app in your Applications folder, version **0.2.2 or newer, below 0.3**.
- Open the app **once** before installing, so it creates its settings, then quit it.

## Install

1. Download the newest **`DS-Harness-Plus-<version>.dmg`** from the [Releases page](https://github.com/BLCKHWK60/DS-Harness-Plus/releases/latest) and double-click it. A window opens with everything in it: all the add-ons, the installer and this guide. (If you use git, clone the project instead; it is the same folder.)
2. In that window, double-click **`Install.command`**.
   - The first time, macOS may say it "cannot be opened because it is from an unidentified developer". If it does, **right-click** the file, choose **Open**, then **Open** again. You only do this once.
3. A Terminal window opens and walks you through it. If the app is open, it asks to quit it. When it says **Done**, open DeepSeek Harness.

Installing copies the add-ons into the app's own data folder (`~/.dsh/addons`), so you can eject the disk image and delete the download afterwards. To remove the add-ons later, open the disk image again and double-click **`Uninstall.command`**.

Before it changes anything, the installer saves your current setup under `~/.dsh/backups/deepseek-harness-plus/`. If any step fails, it puts everything back by itself.

**Terminal instead:** if you prefer, run this from the unpacked folder:

```bash
bash scripts/install.sh
```

## First steps

1. **Add your models.** Go to **Settings → Models** in the app. You can paste an API key for a provider there, or add your own server (for example a model server on another computer). No files to edit.
2. **Look at the new pages.** **Settings** now has **Colours, Model Tiers, Modes, Sampling, Usage, Benchmark, Arena** and **Swarm** pages. The chat box (where you type) gets one **model button** beside the send button, with the model list, an effort slider from Off to Ultra Code, tiers and sampling, and, once set up, a model-health dot.
3. **Switch on what you want.** Some add-ons work right away. The others do nothing until you give them a little setup, for example which models the arena should compare. [docs/ADD-ONS.md](docs/ADD-ONS.md) says which is which and how to set each one up.

### What works the moment you install

- **Cowork sidebar:** Chat, Cowork and Code tabs at the top of the left sidebar. Each tab lists only its own conversations and projects, and has its own sections: Model Arena under Chat, and Automation tasks, Connectors (your MCP servers, with on/off switches) and Skills under Cowork and Code. The start page gets a greeting and suggestion chips. A tab picks the mode of new conversations, so the chat box no longer needs a mode drop-down. To get the normal sidebar back, switch **Cowork sidebar** off on the **Plugins** page.
- **Colours:** pick a colour scheme in **Settings → Colours**: DeepSeek Harness (the stock colours, the default), MindsHub Cowork, Graphite or Forest, each in light and dark.
- **Modes:** Chat, Cowork and Code modes, switchable per conversation, plus **Search** and **Deep research** buttons in the chat box.
- **Model Tiers:** one model button in the chat box: pick any model and drag the effort slider. Five starter tiers (Fast, Balanced, Deep, Creative, Code review) work at once on whatever model you use. No model is preconfigured.
- **Code map:** a compact map of the project a conversation works in, so the assistant looks things up instead of reading whole files. Plus four "reverse engineer" skills. Nothing to install.
- **Privacy:** switches off the app's usage reporting and the upload of a conversation when you rate an answer. `/privacy` shows the state.
- **Usage counter:** counts requests and tokens per day and model (never your text).
- **Deep research** and **Code power:** new tools and skills the assistant can use.

Everything else stays switched off until you set it up.

## Changing an add-on's settings

Some add-ons have their own page in **Settings** (Tiers, Modes, Sampling). The rest are set up in the app's settings file. To edit it:

1. Quit DeepSeek Harness.
2. In Finder press **⌘ Shift G**, paste `~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/` and press Return.
3. Make a copy of **`cordis.patch.yml`** first, as your own backup. Then open the original with TextEdit.
4. Paste in the block for the add-on you want, from its section in [docs/ADD-ONS.md](docs/ADD-ONS.md). Fill in the parts in `<ANGLE BRACKETS>`, save, and open the app.

The file is indentation-sensitive: use spaces, never tabs, and keep the lines lined up as in the example. If the app will not start after an edit, put your copy back.

## Updating

Download the newer version and double-click **`Install.command`** again. It replaces the add-ons and keeps your settings.

## Removing

Double-click **`Uninstall.command`**. It removes all twenty-two add-ons and their files. Your conversations and your models are not touched. Any settings you wrote for the add-ons stay in the settings file and do nothing; if you install again, they come back into effect.

## Using it on a second Mac

1. Install the DeepSeek Harness app on the other Mac and open it once.
2. Run **`Install.command`** there too.
3. Add your models in **Settings → Models**.
4. Optional: to keep the same **settings** on both Macs, use iCloud Drive (below).
5. Optional: to see the same **conversations** on both Macs, set up the **Sync** add-on (see [docs/ADD-ONS.md](docs/ADD-ONS.md#sync)). It needs a private git repository that both Macs can reach. Neither Mac has to be switched on for the other to sync.

### Same settings on both Macs, through iCloud Drive

The **Shared settings** add-on keeps the settings you change in the app's own pages in one file, `settings.json`, in a folder in iCloud Drive. Those settings are Modes, Model Tiers, the Cowork tabs, Sampling presets and Colours. Change something on one Mac and the other Mac picks it up within about a minute. The file never holds secrets: API keys, tokens and passwords stay on each Mac.

1. On the first Mac, double-click **`Install.command`** and answer **y** when it asks *"Share settings through iCloud Drive?"*. It uses the folder **iCloud Drive → DeepSeek Harness Plus**.
2. On the second Mac, do the same. When the app opens there, it takes the settings from the file. Its own earlier settings are kept in `~/.dsh/shared-settings/backups`.

To use another folder, or from Terminal: `bash scripts/install.sh --settings "<folder>"`. To stop sharing on one Mac: `bash scripts/install.sh --no-settings`. Type `/shared-settings` in a conversation to see what is shared and when it last synced.

**Good to know:**
- Not shared:
  - which conversation sits in which tab;
  - the tier a conversation uses;
  - which add-ons are switched on;
  - settings written by hand into the settings file rather than in a Settings page.
- If you change the same setting on both Macs at once, the copy in iCloud wins. The other value is kept in the backups folder.
- iCloud sometimes makes a copy such as `settings 2.json` when both Macs write at the same moment. `/shared-settings` tells you if one appears; check it, then delete it.

## Giving it to someone else

Send them the link to this project, https://github.com/BLCKHWK60/DS-Harness-Plus. They follow **Install** above. Nothing in here contains your addresses, keys or personal settings; every add-on starts empty.

## If something goes wrong

- **"DeepSeek Harness is not installed"**: the app must be in `/Applications` or `~/Applications`.
- **"No 'desktop' setup found"**: open the app once, quit it, and run the installer again.
- **"version ... works with version 0.2.2 up to 0.3"**: your app is newer or older than this release supports. Look for a newer DeepSeek Harness Plus.
- **The installer stopped with a problem**: it has already put everything back. The message names a log file; send that file to whoever helps you.
- **The app misbehaves after installing**: run **`Uninstall.command`**. Every install and uninstall also leaves a dated copy of your setup files in `~/.dsh/backups/deepseek-harness-plus/`, in case someone helping you needs them.
- **The app will not start after you edited the settings file**: put back the copy you made before editing.

## What is in this folder

| Folder or file | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `Install.command`, `Uninstall.command` | Double-click to install or remove. |
| `addons/` | The twenty-two add-ons. Each has a `README.md` with its full technical notes. |
| `docs/ADD-ONS.md` | What each add-on does and how to set it up. |
| `docs/HOW-IT-WORKS.md` | For technical readers: how the install works, how to test, how to change an add-on. |
| `templates/` | Optional ready-to-fill examples: model servers, memory, MCP tool servers, backups. |
| `extras/dsh-intel-mcp/` | Optional Python tools (code map, reverse engineering, context store). Needs Python; not installed automatically. |
| `scripts/` | What the `.command` files run. |
| `VERSION` | This release's version number. |
| `LICENSE` | The MIT licence: anyone may use, change and share this. |

## Status

Release 0.29.2 (the version in `VERSION`). Tested so far:

- **Install, update and uninstall:** run on a fresh setup and on a copy of a real, long-used setup.
- **Live start:** the app starts with every add-on loaded.
- **Add-ons:** each has its own automated tests, and each settings page was checked in the app's web version.
- **Not yet tested on another person's Mac.** Each add-on's `README.md` lists what was and was not verified for it.
