# Model arena

Host plugin `@local/dsh-model-arena` (dsh 0.2.2-rc.1). Ask **one prompt to several models at once**, read the answers under **shuffled labels** (A, B, C, D) with no model name anywhere, let a **blind judge** and **you** pick, then **reveal** who wrote what, with latency and token counts. **Nothing is configured by default**: until you pick at least two models (Settings > Arena, or `candidates` in the config) the arena only shows its setup page.

Everything can be done on the page: **Settings > Arena** (or **Model Arena** in the sidebar) has the setup form, an Ask box, and Judge, Pick and Reveal buttons. The `/arena` commands and the `modelArena` service work as before. Live streaming columns are deliberately not built.

## Configuration

```yaml
- id: model-arena
  config:
    candidates:                       # list at least two, or none to leave the arena off
      - { id: <ID>, provider: <ROUTE>, model: <MODEL ID>, reasoningEffort: <EFFORT> }
    maxContestants: 4                 # 2 to 4 answers per round; a longer list is sampled at random
    blindByDefault: true              # false = show names at once (same as always using --open)
    redactNames: true                 # hide candidate ids and model names if an answer says them
    judge: { provider: <ROUTE>, model: <MODEL ID> }   # only needed for `/arena judge`
    criteria: []                      # empty = accuracy, completeness, clarity, relevance
    consistencyCheck: true            # judge twice, second time in reversed order
    limits: { timeoutMs: 120000, maxTokens: 0 }       # per contestant; maxTokens 0 = not set
    storeDays: 30                     # rounds older than this are deleted
    dataDir: <ABSOLUTE_DIR>           # optional; default is a folder in the dsh home
    commandName: arena
```

## Use

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `/arena ask [--with id,id] [--open] [--blind] <prompt>` | Asks the contestants in parallel and prints the answers under labels only. `--with` picks exact candidates (2 to `maxContestants`). |
| `/arena judge [round]` | A blind judge compares the answers and names a winner by label, with average scores. |
| `/arena pick <label> [round]` | Records your own choice. |
| `/arena reveal [round]` | Shows label to candidate (provider/model), latency, tokens, the judge's and your pick, and whether you agree. |
| `/arena show [round]`, `list`, `delete <round>` | Re-read a round (blind until revealed), list rounds, delete one. |

Without a round id, a command uses the latest round. Service `modelArena`: `candidates`, `run`, `view`, `judge`, `pick`, `reveal`, `list`, `delete`.

## How blindness is kept

- Labels are assigned by a **fair random shuffle** (`crypto.randomInt`) per round; the order is saved and shown only on reveal.
- Output before reveal has **no model, provider, candidate id, latency or token count**.
- A contestant failing shows `(no answer: timed out | route unavailable | request failed)`, a generic word, never the error text.
- If an answer names a candidate id or model (for example "I am ..."), the name is replaced by `[model]` in what you and the judge see (`redactNames`).
- The judge shuffles again on its own labels, so it never sees your labels either. Its own reasoning is not shown, because it would use its own letters.
- **Same-family note**: if the judge's provider or model equals a contestant's, the result carries a warning, without saying which contestant.

## Judge

The judge is the **same one as in Code power** (`candidateJudge` service: shuffled labels, reversed-order consistency check, the owner's Arena judge prompt), so the project has one judge. Load `dsh-code-power` to use `/arena judge`. The judge is called through `ctx.llm.stream` on `judge.provider/model` at temperature 0, with no sub-agent and no tools. If the two rounds disagree the result is a tie flagged as split.

## Settings page

The same page also opens as a full page from the sidebar (**Model Arena**). The Cowork sidebar lists it under the Chat tab.

**Setup** (saved as you change it, applied at once, no restart):

| On the page | Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Models to compare | `candidates` | Add models from the app's model list, set an effort for each, remove them. At least two are needed. The id is made from the model's name |
| Judge model | `judge` | Optional. A model that compares the answers blind |
| Judge twice | `consistencyCheck` | A second reading in reverse order; a different result is a tie |
| What the judge looks at | `criteria` | Words separated by commas; empty uses accuracy, completeness, clarity, relevance |
| Answers per round | `maxContestants` | 2 to 4; with more models, each round draws that many at random |
| Hide the names until I reveal | `blindByDefault` | Off shows names at once for `/arena ask` in a chat. Rounds asked on the page are always blind until you press Reveal |
| Remove model names from answers | `redactNames` | Replaces a model's own name by `[model]` |
| Time limit per answer, Longest answer | `limits` | Seconds (stored as `timeoutMs`), and max output tokens (0 = no limit) |
| Keep rounds for | `storeDays` | Days |

Until two models are picked, Setup sits at the top of the page; after that, Ask and the rounds come first and Setup moves below.

**Ask and the rounds:** type a question, press **Ask the models**; the round shows "N of M answers in" while it runs, then one column per label. **Pick this answer** on a column records your choice, **Ask the judge** runs the judge, **Reveal the models** shows who wrote what with speed and tokens, **Delete round** asks once more first. A refused action says why in plain words (no judge set, the judge gave no usable verdict, and so on).

**How it is wired:**

- The form reads and writes the add-on's own settings through the app's settings channel (`remote.settings.describe` / `mutate`, namespace `model-arena`; on a `settings/conflict` it reloads and retries once). The fields above are `.volatile()` in the Config schema, and the host half reads them at every use (`readSettings`), so nothing is captured at load. The YAML shape is unchanged; existing config files keep working.
- A config with one contestant, or none, now loads (it used to stop the add-on at start): it is a setup in progress. A repeated id in a hand-written file still stops it.
- Buttons go to one write route, `POST /dsh-model-arena/action`, body `{ action: ask | judge | pick | reveal | delete, id?, prompt?, label? }`. It sits behind the same fence as the read routes (login cookie and Host/Origin check), accepts POST only, reads at most 64 KB of JSON, accepts only those five actions, and checks the round id (`20261110120000-a1b`) and label (A to D). `ask` answers with the round id as soon as the models are being asked; the page then follows the round through the read routes. Its answers never name a model: names come only from the read route, and only after reveal.
- The read routes are unchanged and GET-only: `GET /dsh-model-arena/rounds` (now also says whether a judge is set and whether the judge service is loaded) and `GET /dsh-model-arena/round?id=<id>`. Before reveal they carry no model, provider, candidate id, latency or token count.
- The Setup area shows which models are in the arena, because you chose them. It never shows which model wrote which answer.

## Data

One file per round, `arena-<id>.json`, written atomically with mode 0600, holding the prompt, the answers, the label order, timings, tokens, the judge result and your pick. It holds **no key and no setting**. Old rounds are deleted at startup and after each round.

## Routes and failures

A route that Route health reports as down is skipped (shown as `route unavailable`) instead of waiting for a timeout. One contestant failing never stops the others. A round with fewer than two answers cannot be judged.

## Checked

21 unit tests (shuffle, redaction, no leak of names in output, failure and timeout isolation, parallelism, sampling, route-down skip, judge wiring and same-family note, pick/reveal, persistence, pruning, file mode) and a mock run in a real dsh headless profile (3 contestants with one unreachable, judge consistent and split, reveal, command registered). Not tested: real models (do they reveal themselves in ways the redaction misses), long answers, the cost of many rounds.

## Checked (0.10 setup page, throwaway web profile, mock models)

- **Unit tests:** 31 (7 new): settings read live, unusable entries dropped, the write route's refusals (no login, wrong method, unknown action, bad or missing id, unknown round, broken JSON, oversize body, empty prompt, fewer than two models), ask / pick / reveal / delete through the route with no name in any answer, the judge through the route with a stand-in judge service.
- **Live, starting from an empty config:** picked two models and a judge on the page; asked a round; picked an answer; revealed; the settings landed in the profile's `cordis.patch.yml` in the shape documented above and were still there after a restart. Every option (effort, answers per round, both switches, criteria, time limit, longest answer, days) was changed on the page and checked in the file.
- **`/arena list`** in a chat and the sidebar **Model Arena** page still work.
- **Look:** checked in the stock scheme (dark) and Forest (dark and light), and at a 900 px wide window; no sideways scrolling.

**Not checked:** a judge verdict with a real model (the mock model does not answer the judge's question in the needed form, so the page showed the plain "could not give a verdict" message; the success path is covered by a unit test with a stand-in judge); a long-running round on the page (the mock answers at once); the Chinese strings (new texts fall back to English); the Mac desktop app.

# DeepSeek Harness Plus

Extra features for the **DeepSeek Harness** desktop app on the Mac: a MindsHub-style sidebar with Chat, Cowork and Code tabs, colour schemes (including MindsHub's navy and teal), work modes, model tiers, a blind model arena, agent swarms, deep research, a usage counter, benchmarks, syncing between Macs and more. Twenty-six add-ons in all, listed in [docs/ADD-ONS.md](docs/ADD-ONS.md).

The add-ons plug into the normal app. Nothing in the app itself is changed, so app updates do not wipe them, and you can remove them at any time.

You do not need to know how to code to install or use this.

---

## What you need

- A Mac with the **DeepSeek Harness** app in your Applications folder, version **0.2.2 or newer, below 0.3**.
- Open the app **once** before installing, so it creates its settings, then quit it.

## Install

1. Download the newest **`DS-Harness-Plus-<version>.dmg`** from the [Releases page](https://github.com/BLCKHWK60/DS-Harness-Plus/releases/latest) and double-click it. A window opens with everything in it: all the add-ons, the installer and this guide. (If you use git, clone the project instead; it is the same folder.)
2. In that window, double-click **`Install.command`**.
   - The first time, macOS may say it "cannot be opened because it is from an unidentified developer". If it does, **right-click** the file, choose **Open**, then **Open** again. You only do this once.
3. A Terminal window opens and walks you through it. If the app is open, it asks to quit it. When it says **Done**, open DeepSeek Harness.

Installing copies the add-ons into the app's own data folder (`~/.dsh/addons`), so you can eject the disk image and delete the download afterwards. To remove the add-ons later, open the disk image again and double-click **`Uninstall.command`**.

Before it changes anything, the installer saves your current setup under `~/.dsh/backups/deepseek-harness-plus/`. If any step fails, it puts everything back by itself.

**Terminal instead:** if you prefer, run this from the unpacked folder:

```bash
bash scripts/install.sh
```

## First steps

1. **Add your models.** Go to **Settings → Models** in the app. You can paste an API key for a provider there, or add your own server (for example a model server on another computer). No files to edit.
2. **Look at the new pages.** **Settings** now has **Colours, Model Tiers, Modes, Sampling, Usage, Benchmark, Arena** and **Swarm** pages. The chat box (where you type) gets one **model button** beside the send button, with the model list, an effort slider from Off to Ultra Code, tiers and sampling, and, once set up, a model-health dot.
3. **Switch on what you want.** Some add-ons work right away. The others do nothing until you give them a little setup, for example which models the arena should compare. [docs/ADD-ONS.md](docs/ADD-ONS.md) says which is which and how to set each one up.

### What works the moment you install

- **Cowork sidebar:** Chat, Cowork and Code tabs at the top of the left sidebar. Each tab lists only its own conversations and projects, and has its own sections: Model Arena under Chat, and Automation tasks, Connectors (your MCP servers, with on/off switches) and Skills under Cowork and Code. The start page gets a greeting and suggestion chips. A tab picks the mode of new conversations, so the chat box no longer needs a mode drop-down. To get the normal sidebar back, switch **Cowork sidebar** off on the **Plugins** page.
- **Colours:** pick a colour scheme in **Settings → Colours**: DeepSeek Harness (the stock colours, the default), MindsHub Cowork, Graphite or Forest, each in light and dark.
- **Modes:** Chat, Cowork and Code modes, switchable per conversation, plus **Search** and **Deep research** buttons in the chat box.
- **Model Tiers:** one model button in the chat box: pick any model and drag the effort slider. Five starter tiers (Fast, Balanced, Deep, Creative, Code review) work at once on whatever model you use. No model is preconfigured.
- **Code map:** a compact map of the project a conversation works in, so the assistant looks things up instead of reading whole files. Plus four "reverse engineer" skills. Nothing to install.
- **Privacy:** switches off the app's usage reporting and the upload of a conversation when you rate an answer. `/privacy` shows the state.
- **Usage counter:** counts requests and tokens per day and model (never your text).
- **Deep research** and **Code power:** new tools and skills the assistant can use.

Everything else stays switched off until you set it up.

## Changing an add-on's settings

Some add-ons have their own page in **Settings** (Tiers, Modes, Sampling). The rest are set up in the app's settings file. To edit it:

1. Quit DeepSeek Harness.
2. In Finder press **⌘ Shift G**, paste `~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/` and press Return.
3. Make a copy of **`cordis.patch.yml`** first, as your own backup. Then open the original with TextEdit.
4. Paste in the block for the add-on you want, from its section in [docs/ADD-ONS.md](docs/ADD-ONS.md). Fill in the parts in `<ANGLE BRACKETS>`, save, and open the app.

The file is indentation-sensitive: use spaces, never tabs, and keep the lines lined up as in the example. If the app will not start after an edit, put your copy back.

## Updating

Download the newer version and double-click **`Install.command`** again. It replaces the add-ons and keeps your settings.

## Removing

Double-click **`Uninstall.command`**. It removes all twenty-two add-ons and their files. Your conversations and your models are not touched. Any settings you wrote for the add-ons stay in the settings file and do nothing; if you install again, they come back into effect.

## Using it on a second Mac

1. Install the DeepSeek Harness app on the other Mac and open it once.
2. Run **`Install.command`** there too.
3. Add your models in **Settings → Models**.
4. Optional: to keep the same **settings** on both Macs, use iCloud Drive (below).
5. Optional: to see the same **conversations** on both Macs, set up the **Sync** add-on (see [docs/ADD-ONS.md](docs/ADD-ONS.md#sync)). It needs a private git repository that both Macs can reach. Neither Mac has to be switched on for the other to sync.

### Same settings on both Macs, through iCloud Drive

The **Shared settings** add-on keeps the settings you change in the app's own pages in one file, `settings.json`, in a folder in iCloud Drive. Those settings are Modes, Model Tiers, the Cowork tabs, Sampling presets and Colours. Change something on one Mac and the other Mac picks it up within about a minute. The file never holds secrets: API keys, tokens and passwords stay on each Mac.

1. On the first Mac, double-click **`Install.command`** and answer **y** when it asks *"Share settings through iCloud Drive?"*. It uses the folder **iCloud Drive → DeepSeek Harness Plus**.
2. On the second Mac, do the same. When the app opens there, it takes the settings from the file. Its own earlier settings are kept in `~/.dsh/shared-settings/backups`.

To use another folder, or from Terminal: `bash scripts/install.sh --settings "<folder>"`. To stop sharing on one Mac: `bash scripts/install.sh --no-settings`. Type `/shared-settings` in a conversation to see what is shared and when it last synced.

**Good to know:**
- Not shared:
  - which conversation sits in which tab;
  - the tier a conversation uses;
  - which add-ons are switched on;
  - settings written by hand into the settings file rather than in a Settings page.
- If you change the same setting on both Macs at once, the copy in iCloud wins. The other value is kept in the backups folder.
- iCloud sometimes makes a copy such as `settings 2.json` when both Macs write at the same moment. `/shared-settings` tells you if one appears; check it, then delete it.

## Giving it to someone else

Send them the link to this project, https://github.com/BLCKHWK60/DS-Harness-Plus. They follow **Install** above. Nothing in here contains your addresses, keys or personal settings; every add-on starts empty.

## If something goes wrong

- **"DeepSeek Harness is not installed"**: the app must be in `/Applications` or `~/Applications`.
- **"No 'desktop' setup found"**: open the app once, quit it, and run the installer again.
- **"version ... works with version 0.2.2 up to 0.3"**: your app is newer or older than this release supports. Look for a newer DeepSeek Harness Plus.
- **The installer stopped with a problem**: it has already put everything back. The message names a log file; send that file to whoever helps you.
- **The app misbehaves after installing**: run **`Uninstall.command`**. Every install and uninstall also leaves a dated copy of your setup files in `~/.dsh/backups/deepseek-harness-plus/`, in case someone helping you needs them.
- **The app will not start after you edited the settings file**: put back the copy you made before editing.

## What is in this folder

| Folder or file | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `Install.command`, `Uninstall.command` | Double-click to install or remove. |
| `addons/` | The twenty-two add-ons. Each has a `README.md` with its full technical notes. |
| `docs/ADD-ONS.md` | What each add-on does and how to set it up. |
| `docs/HOW-IT-WORKS.md` | For technical readers: how the install works, how to test, how to change an add-on. |
| `templates/` | Optional ready-to-fill examples: model servers, memory, MCP tool servers, backups. |
| `extras/dsh-intel-mcp/` | Optional Python tools (code map, reverse engineering, context store). Needs Python; not installed automatically. |
| `scripts/` | What the `.command` files run. |
| `VERSION` | This release's version number. |
| `LICENSE` | The MIT licence: anyone may use, change and share this. |

## Status

Release 0.29.2 (the version in `VERSION`). Tested so far:

- **Install, update and uninstall:** run on a fresh setup and on a copy of a real, long-used setup.
- **Live start:** the app starts with every add-on loaded.
- **Add-ons:** each has its own automated tests, and each settings page was checked in the app's web version.
- **Not yet tested on another person's Mac.** Each add-on's `README.md` lists what was and was not verified for it.

# Model router

Host plugin `@local/dsh-model-router` (dsh 0.2.2-rc.1). A small routing model picks, for each turn, one of **2 to 5 candidate models** for the user's request. **Nothing is configured by default**: with no candidates the plugin does nothing, and with 1 or more than 5 it fails at load.

## When the choice takes effect (important)

On rc.1 a plugin cannot change the model of the step that is about to run: the route is fixed before any plugin sees the step, and `agent.model.select()` applies to the next step. Selecting and then rejecting the first step was tried: the turn just ends with no answer and the message is not retried. So, as agreed:

> The routing model decides at the **first** step of a turn (adds up to `routingModel.timeoutMs`, default 4 s); the chosen model runs from the **second** step. A turn that needs only one step still runs on the current route.

The spec's statement that `agent/pre-step` is the only legal place to route is therefore true but incomplete: it is legal, and it is one step late.

## How a decision is made

1. Skip the turn when routing is off for the Session, or when the current route is not a candidate and the router already chose one earlier (someone else, for example you in the composer, changed the route: the router **stands down** and `/router on` resumes it). A route that moved because route health saw the chosen route go down is **not** treated as manual.
2. **Stickiness**: for `policy.stickyTurns` turns after a switch the current candidate stays and the routing model is not called.
3. Ask the routing model (`ctx.llm.stream`, temperature 0, small token cap) with the candidates' `strengths`, the last `prompt.includeLastN` requests and the current one; it answers JSON `{route, reason, confidence}`.
4. **Fail safe**: a timeout, an error, unparsable JSON, an unknown or unusable route, or `confidence < policy.minConfidence` keeps the current candidate (or `policy.defaultCandidate` when set).
5. **Health**: with the route-health plugin loaded and `respectHealth` on, candidates on a `down` route are not offered and cannot be chosen.
6. Apply: a Tier candidate goes through `modelTiers.setSessionTier` (route, effort, persisted like a composer choice); an explicit route uses `agent.model.select()` (with its optional `reasoningEffort`).

Every decision is kept in memory (last 20 per Session): `/router` prints the state and the last five (turn, from, to, reason); `/router off` leaves the model alone, `/router on` resumes. Service `modelRouter`: `status(sessionId)`, `setEnabled(sessionId, on)`, `onDecision(handler)`.

## Configuration

```yaml
- id: model-router
  config:
    candidates:                         # 2 to 5
      - { id: <ID>, tier: <TIER_ID>, strengths: '<WHAT IT IS GOOD AT>' }
      - { id: <ID>, provider: <ROUTE>, model: <MODEL_ID>, reasoningEffort: <EFFORT>, strengths: '...' }
    routingModel: { provider: <ROUTE>, model: <MODEL_ID>, timeoutMs: 4000, maxTokens: 200 }
    policy: { stickyTurns: 2, minConfidence: 0.6, defaultCandidate: '', respectHealth: true }
    prompt: { systemText: '', includeLastN: 3 }
    commandName: router
```

No route, model or address is preset. `localOnly` on a candidate is accepted but not enforced yet (Tier has no private-tier flag).

## Costs to know

Each routed turn adds one small model call and up to the timeout in latency at the first step. Every switch changes the model mid-conversation, which discards the inference server's KV cache for that session (hence the stickiness default). Candidates share one conversation history; dsh adds its model-switch notice.

## Verified (rc.1, scripted mock model, throwaway home)

A refactor request on the small route: step 1 on the small model, step 2 on the large one. A trivial request stays small; on a large default route it moves **down** to small. A 0.2-confidence answer keeps the current route. An unreachable routing model keeps the current route. One candidate fails at load with a clear message. The pure decision logic (stickiness, confidence, unusable route, default) has unit checks. Select-then-reject was probed and does not work.

## Not verified

Routing quality with a real small model (all answers were scripted; the spec's 8-of-10 scripted-prompt target needs real models); the median added latency; `stickyTurns` across several turns in one session and the stand-down rule (needs a long session; covered by unit checks only for stickiness); Tier candidates (`setSessionTier` path); the route-health interplay; the spec's `allowEscalation`, `localOnly` and benchmark replay.

To get the normal sidebar back, switch **Cowork sidebar** off on the **Plugins** page.
- **Colours:** pick a colour scheme in **Settings → Colours**: DeepSeek Harness (the stock colours, the default), MindsHub Cowork, Graphite or Forest, each in light and dark.
- **Modes:** Chat, Cowork and Code modes, switchable per conversation, plus **Search** and **Deep research** buttons in the chat box.
- **Model Tiers:** one model button in the chat box: pick any model and drag the effort slider. Five starter tiers (Fast, Balanced, Deep, Creative, Code review) work at once on whatever model you use. No model is preconfigured.
- **Code map:** a compact map of the project a conversation works in, so the assistant looks things up instead of reading whole files. Plus four "reverse engineer" skills. Nothing to install.
- **Privacy:** switches off the app's usage reporting and the upload of a conversation when you rate an answer. `/privacy` shows the state.
- **Usage counter:** counts requests and tokens per day and model (never your text).
- **Deep research** and **Code power:** new tools and skills the assistant can use.

Everything else stays switched off until you set it up.

## Changing an add-on's settings

Some add-ons have their own page in **Settings** (Tiers, Modes, Sampling). The rest are set up in the app's settings file. To edit it:

1. Quit DeepSeek Harness.
2. In Finder press **⌘ Shift G**, paste `~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/` and press Return.
3. Make a copy of **`cordis.patch.yml`** first, as your own backup. Then open the original with TextEdit.
4. Paste in the block for the add-on you want, from its section in [docs/ADD-ONS.md](docs/ADD-ONS.md). Fill in the parts in `<ANGLE BRACKETS>`, save, and open the app.

The file is indentation-sensitive: use spaces, never tabs, and keep the lines lined up as in the example. If the app will not start after an edit, put your copy back.

## Updating

Download the newer version and double-click **`Install.command`** again. It replaces the add-ons and keeps your settings.

## Removing

Double-click **`Uninstall.command`**. It removes all twenty-two add-ons and their files. Your conversations and your models are not touched. Any settings you wrote for the add-ons stay in the settings file and do nothing; if you install again, they come back into effect.

## Using it on a second Mac

1. Install the DeepSeek Harness app on the other Mac and open it once.
2. Run **`Install.command`** there too.
3. Add your models in **Settings → Models**.
4. Optional: to keep the same **settings** on both Macs, use iCloud Drive (below).
5. Optional: to see the same **conversations** on both Macs, set up the **Sync** add-on (see [docs/ADD-ONS.md](docs/ADD-ONS.md#sync)). It needs a private git repository that both Macs can reach. Neither Mac has to be switched on for the other to sync.

### Same settings on both Macs, through iCloud Drive

The **Shared settings** add-on keeps the settings you change in the app's own pages in one file, `settings.json`, in a folder in iCloud Drive. Those settings are Modes, Model Tiers, the Cowork tabs, Sampling presets and Colours. Change something on one Mac and the other Mac picks it up within about a minute. The file never holds secrets: API keys, tokens and passwords stay on each Mac.

1. On the first Mac, double-click **`Install.command`** and answer **y** when it asks *"Share settings through iCloud Drive?"*. It uses the folder **iCloud Drive → DeepSeek Harness Plus**.
2. On the second Mac, do the same. When the app opens there, it takes the settings from the file. Its own earlier settings are kept in `~/.dsh/shared-settings/backups`.

To use another folder, or from Terminal: `bash scripts/install.sh --settings "<folder>"`. To stop sharing on one Mac: `bash scripts/install.sh --no-settings`. Type `/shared-settings` in a conversation to see what is shared and when it last synced.

**Good to know:**
- Not shared:
  - which conversation sits in which tab;
  - the tier a conversation uses;
  - which add-ons are switched on;
  - settings written by hand into the settings file rather than in a Settings page.
- If you change the same setting on both Macs at once, the copy in iCloud wins. The other value is kept in the backups folder.
- iCloud sometimes makes a copy such as `settings 2.json` when both Macs write at the same moment. `/shared-settings` tells you if one appears; check it, then delete it.

## Giving it to someone else

Send them the link to this project, https://github.com/BLCKHWK60/DS-Harness-Plus. They follow **Install** above. Nothing in here contains your addresses, keys or personal settings; every add-on starts empty.

## If something goes wrong

- **"DeepSeek Harness is not installed"**: the app must be in `/Applications` or `~/Applications`.
- **"No 'desktop' setup found"**: open the app once, quit it, and run the installer again.
- **"version ... works with version 0.2.2 up to 0.3"**: your app is newer or older than this release supports. Look for a newer DeepSeek Harness Plus.
- **The installer stopped with a problem**: it has already put everything back. The message names a log file; send that file to whoever helps you.
- **The app misbehaves after installing**: run **`Uninstall.command`**. Every install and uninstall also leaves a dated copy of your setup files in `~/.dsh/backups/deepseek-harness-plus/`, in case someone helping you needs them.
- **The app will not start after you edited the settings file**: put back the copy you made before editing.

## What is in this folder

| Folder or file | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `Install.command`, `Uninstall.command` | Double-click to install or remove. |
| `addons/` | The twenty-two add-ons. Each has a `README.md` with its full technical notes. |
| `docs/ADD-ONS.md` | What each add-on does and how to set it up. |
| `docs/HOW-IT-WORKS.md` | For technical readers: how the install works, how to test, how to change an add-on. |
| `templates/` | Optional ready-to-fill examples: model servers, memory, MCP tool servers, backups. |
| `extras/dsh-intel-mcp/` | Optional Python tools (code map, reverse engineering, context store). Needs Python; not installed automatically. |
| `scripts/` | What the `.command` files run. |
| `VERSION` | This release's version number. |
| `LICENSE` | The MIT licence: anyone may use, change and share this. |

## Status

Release 0.29.2 (the version in `VERSION`). Tested so far:

- **Install, update and uninstall:** run on a fresh setup and on a copy of a real, long-used setup.
- **Live start:** the app starts with every add-on loaded.
- **Add-ons:** each has its own automated tests, and each settings page was checked in the app's web version.
- **Not yet tested on another person's Mac.** Each add-on's `README.md` lists what was and was not verified for it.

# Model Tiers

Two lists that work together, plus the one model control of the chat box:

- **Tiers** are ways of working. A tier sets how hard the model thinks (effort), what it may reach (web search, web fetch, browser, sub-agents), how many sub-agents it runs, its own instructions, the skills it loads and the connectors it may use. Five **starter tiers** ship: Fast, Balanced, Deep, Creative and Code review. You can add your own.
- **Model versions** are named copies of a model with their own effort, temperature and max output tokens, for example "Qwen – Writing" and "Qwen – Coding". The plain model always stays available with default settings.
- A tier can point at a model version, at a plain model, or at no model at all. A tier with no model applies its rules to whatever model the conversation is on.

**No models are preconfigured.** A fresh install has five starter tiers with no model.

## The chat box control

One button beside the send button shows the model (or version) and the effort. It opens one panel:

- **Search and list:** saved versions first, then every model by provider. Picking a plain model always gives default settings.
- **Effort slider:** Off, Low, Medium, High, Extra high, Ultra Code. It applies when you let go.
- **Tier:** one chip per tier. "Reset" forgets this conversation's tier and settings; the model stays.
- **Sampling:** temperature and max output tokens for this conversation. **Save as new version…** keeps the settings in use under a name; **Update "name"** writes changes back into the version in use.

The panel fits the window: it opens above the button when there is room, otherwise beside it on the left, centred on the button, and the model list shrinks before anything else scrolls. A click anywhere outside closes it, including on the part of the Mac window that drags the window (a clear sheet behind the panel catches the click).

The app's own model menu is hidden while this add-on is on (it comes back when the add-on is switched off). The control uses the app's own model directory, so `/model` and the button always agree.

## Starter tiers and your tiers

**Settings → Model Tiers → Starter tiers** has one card per starter:

| Field | What it does |
|---|---|
| Name | Your own name for the starter. Empty uses the built-in name |
| Instructions | Given to the model whenever the tier is active. Empty uses the starter's built-in guidance |
| Model | Optional. One list; its first entry is "No model: keep the model the conversation is on". A search box shows only when there are more than 12 models. "Type a model by hand" opens two fields for a provider and model id that are not in the list |
| Effort, Access | As before: effort level, web search, web fetch, browser, sub-agents |
| Model version | A saved version that supplies the tier's model and sampling |
| Sub-agents | "Ask for at least" (an instruction to the model) and "allow at most" (enforced; empty uses the app-wide cap) |
| Skills loaded with this tier | Up to 6 skills whose text is added to the model's instructions while the tier is active (8,000 characters each; longer text is cut with a note) |
| Connectors | All, or only the MCP servers you tick. Tools of the others are hidden from the model, and refused if called anyway |

**Your tiers** adds tiers without changing the starters: **New tier**, **Copy** on a starter, **Duplicate**, **Move up/down** and **Delete**. They have the same fields, plus a two-character badge, a role line and model variants. Ids are stable (`custom-…`). A conversation on a deleted tier falls back to normal matching.

A model that belongs to a tier (its own model, a variant, a fallback or a role model) gets that tier's rules even when you only picked the model.

## Model versions

**Settings → Model Tiers → Model versions**: "New version of…" a model, then set a name, effort, temperature (0–2) and max output tokens. Empty fields mean "default". Each row says which tiers use it. Versions can also be saved from the chat box.

What applies, strongest first: a value set in the chat box for this conversation → the saved version in use → the adapter default. The **Sampling presets** add-on never overrides the first two.

The app sends only `temperature` and `maxTokens`. `top_p`, `top_k`, `min_p` and the penalties cannot be sent by this app version: they stay on the model server (verified in the installed app's `llm-pi-ai` adapter).

### Instructions on a version (0.13)

A version can carry its own instructions, so one model can be set up for different jobs:

- **Instructions for this version** are given to the model whenever the version is in use, in any mode.
- **Use only these** leaves out the other *added* instructions while the version is in use: the tier's own instructions and effort wording, the Chat / Cowork / Code mode's prompt, and the role prompts. The app's own text about its tools always stays, and so do the tier's limits (internet access, sub-agent cap), because they describe what will actually work.
- **Instructions per app mode**: the app's modes are its agent presets, picked above the chat box of a new conversation (Standard, PTC, Minimal, Creator), plus any you add in Settings → Agent presets. Each can have its own text for this version, either **added** to the version's instructions or **used alone** (which replaces the version's instructions and the other added instructions for that mode).

How it is decided, for the mode a conversation is in: a mode text marked "use only this" stands alone; otherwise the version's text and the mode's text are both used, and "Use only these" on the version decides whether the tier, mode and role instructions are left out. A switch with no text replaces nothing.

Stored on the version as `instructions`, `replace` and `presets: { <preset id>: { text, replace } }` (at most 4,000 characters per text). The service gains `sessionVersion(sessionId)` and `instructionsReplaced(sessionId)`; Modes, Role prompts and Self-improvement ask the second one before adding their own text.

Checked live with the mock model, read from the requests it received: the version's text and the Standard-mode text both arrived; with "Use only these" off, the tier's instructions were there too; with it on, they were gone while the version's text stayed. The preset of a conversation is read with `agentPresets.presetForSession`. Not checked: the PTC, Minimal and Creator modes, a mode of your own, and the mode prompt and role prompts being left out (both add-ons call the same switch; neither had text set in the lab).

## Carry-over from before 0.10

On the first start after an update, once:

- a starter tier that already has a model keeps the name it had (Haiku, Sonnet, Opus, Fable, Code), stored as its Name;
- old per-model defaults ("model profiles") that set something become model versions named "… (saved settings)", and the tiers on that model point at the new version. Empty profiles are left alone and no longer shown.

The marker is `startersMigrated`. Old per-model defaults that remain still apply to conversations that use no version.

## Project profiles

**Settings → Model Tiers → Project profiles** defines named tier decks and assigns them to DSH Workspaces:

- Each profile selects a subset of built-in/custom tiers and a default tier.
- A project assignment makes that profile the project default.
- The composer profile selector can override the project default for one Session.
- New Sessions in a profiled project inherit the profile's default tier once.
- Existing pinned Sessions keep their tier; changing profile does not rewrite tier definitions.
- Deleting a profile clears its project assignments and falls back to all tiers.

Profiles only filter the selector and supply defaults. They do not change Host routing, tier definitions, or model profiles.

## Fallback chains

Each built-in or custom tier can have an ordered fallback chain in **Settings → Model Tiers**. Fallbacks are attempted only after normal request recovery (including `llm-retry`) declines:

- Primary/variant route first.
- Fallback routes in order on request failure.
- Each fallback uses its own model-profile sampling where available.
- The tier's access, sub-agent, effort, and prompt rules stay in force.
- The cursor resets on the next step or turn.

Fallbacks are stored separately in `fallbackChains`; an empty chain preserves the previous single-route behavior.

## Role models

Each tier can bind optional **Plan**, **Implement**, **Review**, and **Fast** role routes in Settings. The `delegate_role` tool starts one child Agent on the selected role model:

- The child keeps the parent tier's access, sub-agent cap, effort, and prompt rules.
- Role routes are matched back to their owning tier, so a child on the Review route still gets the tier's review policy.
- The tool returns the child's final text, stop reason, and child id.
- No automatic role routing happens; the model chooses `delegate_role` when it fits the task.
- Empty role slots do not change primary/variant or fallback behavior.

Role routes are stored separately in `roleModels`. Configured roles also appear as one-click **Role lanes** in the composer, applying that role route to the current Session while keeping the tier policy.

## Multi-lane review

When the active tier has a **Review** role configured, `review_lanes` starts up to three independent review children in parallel:

- Angles: correctness/regressions, security, tests/edge cases, performance.
- Defaults to correctness, security, and tests.
- Each child runs on the tier's Review role model and keeps the tier's access policy.
- Availability respects the current sub-agent cap and already-running children.
- The tool returns one consolidated report with per-lane findings, child ids, and failures.
- The parent still owns synthesis and verification.

Empty Review role routes leave `review_lanes` unavailable; no existing tier behavior changes.

## Pipeline orchestration

`run_pipeline` sequences three role children on the active tier:

1. **Plan** — investigate and return an implementation plan without edits.
2. **Implement** — make scoped changes in the current workspace and report checks.
3. **Review** — inspect the result and report findings; skipped when review is disabled or no Review role exists.

It requires Plan and Implement role routes. Stages run sequentially, respect the tier's sub-agent policy and cap, and return each stage's text plus child ids. The parent still owns final synthesis, verification, and any fixes.

## Health diagnostics

**Settings → Model Tiers → Health** is a read-only view of:

- tier, role-route, fallback, project-profile, and active-session counts;
- primary/variant/fallback/role routes missing from the current model catalog;
- fallback chains that repeat the primary route;
- active sessions pinned to deleted tiers;
- project assignments pointing at missing profiles;
- profile defaults pointing at missing tiers.

It can copy a plain-text report and never mutates configuration.

## Backup & restore

**Settings → Model Tiers → Backup** exports and imports the portable configuration:

- Built-in tier models, effort, and access flags.
- Custom tiers.
- Model profiles and sampling.
- Project profiles and assignments.
- Fallback chains.
- Role routes.
- Sub-agent cap and Ultra auto-delegation.

Exports exclude session pins and per-session profile overrides. Imports are **merge-only**: choose the sections to apply, matching entries are updated, and entries absent from the file are preserved. A live preview validates the JSON and shows how many setting updates will be written.

## Where things are stored

Tier settings are saved through the app's settings service into the active profile. Starters are `tiers.<id>` (ids `haiku, sonnet, opus, fable, code` are kept for existing installs; people see the names). Your tiers are the JSON list `customTiers`, versions the JSON list `modelVersions`. What each conversation picked is `activeTiers`: `{ tier, version?, provider, model, effort, temperature?, maxTokens? }`.

## Effort mapping

The slider has six plugin levels: **Off, Low, Medium, High, Extra high, Ultra Code**.

DSH only accepts reasoning efforts an adapter advertises. The plugin maps each level onto the nearest advertised effort (`off`/`none`/`minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`/`max`, `ultra`). When the model advertises no reasoning metadata, the level still controls the injected behavior prompt but no `reasoningEffort` is sent.

**Ultra Code** additionally tells the model to decompose the task, start independent sub-agents in one message, keep working while they run, avoid busywork, own the final synthesis, run the narrowest proving checks, review the final diff, and state which checks it ran. The sub-agent cap is enforced in flight; the delegation push itself is prompt-driven, because DSH cannot force a model to call a tool.

Each tier also carries a short behavior prompt: Haiku favors fast, narrow changes; Sonnet balances planning and implementation; Opus takes the harder reasoning path; Fable explores and synthesizes broadly; Code restricts itself to review, check, and fix.

## Code tier

The Code tier's prompt restricts it to review, check, and fix work: start from the diff or named files, run the narrowest checks that prove the change, report findings by severity with `file:line`, then fix and re-run. It does not plan new product scope.

## Access gating

Enforced on the Host before dispatch:

- `web_search` requires the tier's Web search toggle.
- `web_fetch` requires the tier's Web fetch toggle.
- Browser tool names and `bash` commands that invoke `ego-browser` require the tier's Browser toggle.
- `subagent`, `subagent_fork`, `workflow`, and `spawn_teammate` require the tier's Sub-agents toggle; direct child starts also enforce the global concurrent cap (default 4, range 1–8).

## How routing works

The selected model is applied through the existing `session.selectModel` Remote. The Host derives the effective selection from the requested provider/model plus the Session's recorded override. An override records `{ tier, provider, model, effort, temperature?, maxTokens? }`: the tier supplies internet/sub-agent defaults, while the route and request controls can differ from that tier's defaults. If the Session's actual route no longer matches the override, the Host falls back to a configured tier that matches the route, or applies no tier rules. When two tiers share the same provider/model, the recorded tier wins; otherwise the first matching tier in Haiku → Code order wins.

## Install

From this profile:

```text
plugin_manager install_bundle target=/absolute/path/to/model-tiers
```

The bundle vendors its two runtime schema packages under `node_modules/` so the Host half can load from a workspace directory without network access.

## dsh 0.2.2-rc.1 compatibility (T1)

This copy differs from the linked original in how it applies routes:

- Reasoning effort is recorded with `agent.model.select()` when an Agent is created or resumed and before each step. It takes effect at the next step prepared; the first step of a new Session is covered by the `agent/created` call.
- The deprecated `agent/request` hook no longer changes provider, model or effort (rc.1 throws if it does). It only sets `temperature` and `maxTokens` from model profiles and per-Session overrides.
- Fallback chains (T2) work at the next message: rc.1 fixes the route for a step and its retries, so a failed step cannot retry on another route. When a step fails terminally on a tier's route, Tier records the next route of the tier's chain with `agent.model.select()`; the failed step ends with the provider error and your next message uses the fallback. A route listed only in a tier's fallback chain keeps that tier (prompt, access gates, effort). There is no automatic return to the primary route and no user-visible banner yet (route-health, spec 4.3). Headless `--session-id` resume re-records the configured route, so it discards the switch; the web app keeps it.

## `modelTiers` service (T3)

Other plugins read tiers and change a session's tier through the service `modelTiers`, provided with `ctx.provide('modelTiers', ...)`. Get it lazily with `ctx.get('modelTiers')`; it is absent when Tier is not loaded. All returned objects are frozen. The existing remotes are unchanged.

| Member | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `apiVersion` | `1` |
| `listTiers()` | `TierInfo[]` in deck order: `id, label, provider, model, effort, webSearch, webFetch, browser, subagents, maxSubagents, minSubagents, version, skills, connectors, custom`. `provider` and `model` are empty for a tier with no model |
| `listVersions()` | the saved model versions: `id, name, provider, model` and the settings each one sets |
| `resolveTier(sessionId)` | the tier the Agent is on (session choice, current route, or a fallback route of a tier), or `null` |
| `setSessionTier(sessionId, tierId)` | the single write path: records the per-session choice (same entry the composer writes), selects the tier's route and effort with `agent.model.select()` for the next step, emits `tier/changed`. A tier with no model keeps the session's current model. The tier's version sampling applies. Throws for an unknown tier or session. If Settings refuses the write (for example the Tier row comes from a `--patch` overlay) the choice is kept in memory for this run and a warning is logged |
| `roleRoute(tierId, role)` | `{provider, model}` for `plan`, `implement`, `review` or `fast`, or `null`; throws for another role |
| `fallbackChain(tierId)` | `{provider, model}[]` in order, empty when none |
| `sessionSampling(sessionId)` | the `temperature` and `maxTokens` the user chose for this Session: values set in the chat box, and those of the saved version the Session is on (never the old per-model defaults), so other plugins do not override a choice |
| `advanceFallback(sessionId, {skip?})` | moves a Session to the next usable route of its tier's fallback chain for the next step; `skip(route)` passes over routes (route health uses it for routes known to be down); returns `{tierId, from, to}` or `null` |
| `restorePrimary(sessionId, tierId)` | moves a Session back to the tier's primary route (its composer choice when it selected that tier); returns `{from, to}` or `null` when already there |
| `registerSubagentTool(name)` | subjects a tool that starts child Agents to the tier's sub-agent switch and concurrency cap; returns a disposer |
| `on('tier/changed', (sessionId, from, to) => void)` | fires for service calls and for changes made in the composer (detected at the next step); returns a disposer; throws for another event name |

Listener errors are logged and do not reach the caller. The per-session override held in memory is cleared when the Agent is disposed.

## Housekeeping (T4, part 1)

- `engines.dsh` is `>=0.2.2-rc.1 <0.3.0`. dsh refuses an incompatible bundle at profile start and skips it, so on a dsh bump Tier stays off until this range is updated after re-reading the upgrade guides.
- `pruneStaleSessions` (default on): when the first Agent exists after start, Tier removes `activeTiers` and `sessionProfiles` entries whose Session is no longer stored (`sessionPersistence.stat` returns nothing). Live Agents and Sessions whose existence cannot be confirmed are kept. It writes once through Settings.
- `registerSubagentTool` (the tool-gate registration API) shipped with the T3 service.
- Decision (owner): per-session state (`activeTiers`, `sessionProfiles`) stays in Settings, written through the revision-checked Settings API. It is not moved to `dsh-storage`; pruning bounds its growth. Revisit only if write races are observed.

## Per-tier sub-agent cap (T5)

A tier may set `maxSubagents` (1 to 8) to override the global `maxSubagents` for that tier; leave it unset to use the global value. In `cordis.patch.yml` it is a field of `tiers.<id>`; custom tiers take it in their `customTiers` JSON entry. The effective cap is used by the tier prompt text, the concurrency gate (`subagent`, `subagent_fork`, `delegate_role`, `review_lanes`, `run_pipeline` and tools added with `registerSubagentTool`), and `TierInfo.maxSubagents` in the `modelTiers` service. The tier cards have a field for it ("allow at most").

A new Session's tier prompt section is now resolved from the Agent's current route, so the first step carries it. Before, it appeared only from the second step.

A composer-selected tier is now matched to its fallback and role routes by its tier id (before, `selection.tierId` was read where only `selection.id` exists, so those matches never succeeded for composer-selected tiers).

## Checked (0.10, throwaway web profile, mock model)

- **Unit tests:** 12 in `test/tiers.test.mjs` (starters without a model, versions, the plain model keeping defaults, tier rules on any model, prompt text, no model names in the bundle patch).
- **Chat box:** the panel opens above the button inside the window; the slider set High and the button showed it; picking a tier with a version switched model, effort and temperature; a failed switch shows its error and puts the earlier choice back.
- **Save as new version:** created a version from a temperature set in the chat box; the plain model stayed in the list with default settings.
- **End to end**, read from the exact request the model received: model and temperature (0.9) of the tier's version, effort Low, the tier's instructions, the text of the chosen skill, "Connectors are switched off", and the "at least 2 sub-agents" line. A Sampling preset (0.1) did not override the version's temperature.
- **Carry-over:** a profile that already had tier models kept the names Haiku … Code.
- **Settings:** every tab renders; version create, rename, effort and temperature edits were saved; the skills list came from the app.

The Settings page follows `docs/UI-STYLE.md` (the app's own fonts, fields, cards, switches and tabs; colours only from the app's variables). Checked in the Forest scheme, dark and light.

**Not checked:** hiding the tools of a real connector (the lab has no MCP server running; only the "none allowed" prompt line and the code path were exercised); project profiles and role lanes in the new panel beyond rendering; the Chinese strings; the Mac desktop app; a model with real thinking levels beyond the mock's.

# DeepSeek Harness Plus

# Modes

Host and client plugin `@local/dsh-modes` (dsh 0.2.2-rc.1): Chat, Cowork and Code modes you can switch **per session, at any time**. A dsh agent preset is fixed when a session is created, so a mode is applied to the live Agent instead: it never needs a new session.

A mode sets:

| Field | Values | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `label` | text | name in the selector |
| `tools` | `"all"`, `"none"`, or a list of tool names | the tools the model sees (a restriction on that Agent; unknown names are ignored) |
| `sandbox` | `inherit`, `read-only`, `workspace-write` | the session's file sandbox mode. `inherit` restores what the session had before a mode changed it. `danger-full-access` cannot be set by a mode |
| `defaultTier` | a Tier id or empty | on a switch to this mode, the session moves to that tier (needs the Tier plugin) |
| `prompt` | text | a prompt section `modes:mode` (order 58) while the mode is active |

Built in (until you supply your own `modes`): **chat** (no tools, read-only, a short "no tools" prompt), **cowork** (all tools, sandbox unchanged), **code** (all tools, `workspace-write`).

## Configuration

```yaml
- id: modes
  config:
    modes: '{"<id>": {"label": "...", "tools": "all", "sandbox": "inherit", "defaultTier": "", "prompt": ""}}'   # JSON; replaces the built-in three
    defaultMode: cowork       # mode of a session that has not chosen one
    scheduledMode: cowork     # mode of a conversation an Automation task opens (unknown id: the first mode with all tools)
    extraModes: '{}'          # modes other add-ons add (same JSON shape as modes); they come after yours and never replace one
    pruneStaleSessions: true  # drop choices of Sessions that no longer exist
    pinOnFirstTurn: true      # record the mode a Session starts in, so a later defaultMode change (e.g. a Cowork sidebar tab) only affects new Sessions
    sessionWeb: '{}'          # per-Session Search switch (the chat-box button writes it)
    sessionResearch: '{}'     # per-Session Deep research switch (the chat-box button writes it)
    sessionTools: '{}'        # per-Session Tools switch: { sessionId: false } means no tools at all
    # With the Cowork sidebar on: a Session that has not sent a message follows defaultMode (the tab), its first
    # message fixes that mode (replacing any earlier choice), and the chat-box selector is hidden.
    commandName: mode
```

`sessionModes` (`{sessionId: modeId}`) is written by the selector and the command; do not edit it by hand.

## Using it

- **Composer selector**: a drop-down left of Tier's control; it re-reads every 3 seconds so a `/mode` switch shows up.
- **Command**: `/mode` lists modes, `/mode <id>` switches.
- **Service `modes`**: `list()`, `get(sessionId)`, `set(sessionId, modeId)`.
- A switch made during a running turn waits until the Agent is idle, so tools and sandbox never change mid-turn.

## Settings page

Settings > **Modes** edits the mode list without touching YAML: one card per mode (id, label, tools All / None / Only these with a list of tool names, file sandbox, default tier, prompt with a 4,000-character counter), the default mode, add / remove, and "Restore built-in modes". It reads and writes the plugin's own `modes` and `defaultMode` fields through the settings channel (the same one Tier and the composer selector use), in one save, and retries once on a revision conflict. It refuses ids that are not lower-case letters, digits and dashes, duplicate ids, an empty tool list under "Only these", and a default that is not one of the modes. Fields the editor does not know about are kept on save. The default-tier box suggests tier ids when the Tier plugin is loaded. Needs a restart of the app once to load (client half).

Tested in a throwaway web profile: add a mode, validation messages, save (written to the profile patch as the same JSON string), the composer selector picked the new mode within 3 seconds, dark and light. Not tested in the desktop app.

## Limits

- The lists in the Tools panel show what the app registered for the conversation. A tool the app only offers under a condition can be listed as callable and still be left out of a request: `web_search` is offered only while a search backend is ready for the model in use.

- The default tier applies when you switch modes, not when a session is first created (a new session keeps whatever tier it has).
- A conversation opened by an Automation task starts in `scheduledMode`, not in the tab last looked at (which, in Chat, gave it no tools). It is recognised by its first inbox message (`agent/inbox/spliced` with `source.kind: 'schedule'`). There is no Settings control for it yet; a task delivering to an existing conversation keeps that conversation's mode.
- Sub-agents (children) start in `defaultMode`, not in the parent's mode. A chat session cannot spawn them anyway (no tools).
- After a restart, leaving a mode that set the sandbox (for example Chat) does not restore the earlier sandbox mode, because that earlier value is kept in memory only; set the access mode in the composer if needed.
- Changing tools invalidates the model's prompt cache from the first changed tool schema.
- The mode list is edited on the Settings page below; the composer selector itself stays a plain `<select>`.
- Renaming a mode id in the editor leaves sessions that had the old id on the default mode (their stored choice no longer matches).


## Search, Deep research and Tools buttons

Three buttons in the chat box switch tools for **this conversation only**. They apply at the next turn.

- **Search** turns the web tools (`web_search`, `web_fetch`) on or off.
  - Default: on in modes with all tools (Cowork, Code), off in a no-tools mode (Chat).
  - In Chat mode with Search on, the model gets only the web tools, and a note that it may use them.
- **Deep research** makes `deep_research` available, and tells the model to use it for questions that need looking things up. The helper agents it starts do the searching and get the web tools for that, whether or not Search is on.
- **Tools** shows at a glance whether the model has any tools ("Tools on" / "Tools off") and opens a small panel with:
  - one switch for all tools of the conversation. Off means the model is offered no tool at all, so it cannot try to call one and there are no failed attempts to look at; Search and Deep research are greyed out, and the model is told to answer from what it knows. On puts back what the mode allows (in Chat, where the mode has no tools of its own, On switches Search on);
  - the list of tools the model can call and the list it cannot, read from the app for that conversation.

### Helper agents follow their conversation

A helper agent (a sub-agent, a deep-research searcher) has no mode of its own. It takes the mode, the Search switch, the Deep research switch and the Tools switch of the conversation that started it, and it does not get the mode's wording ("answer in one reply, no tools").

Before 0.20 a helper was treated as a new conversation and got the default mode. With the Cowork sidebar on, that is the tab you are on: in the Chat tab, helpers got no tools at all, so Deep research always ended with "found no usable sources". Fixed.

Tool names are passed to the app's restriction as they are. In this dsh version most tools come from the conversation's agent preset and are not listed to plugins, so a name is not checked against a visible list. A name the app refuses is left out, with a warning in the log.

Checked in the throwaway web profile by reading the exact request the model received:

| Case | Tools the model got |
| --- | --- |
| Chat with Search off | no tools |
| Chat with Search on | `web_fetch` only (that lab has no `web_search` backend), plus the note |
| Chat with Deep research on | `deep_research`, plus the research note |
| A deep-research helper of that Chat conversation | `web_fetch` (and `web_search` where a search backend is ready), no Chat wording (0.20; before: no tools) |
| Any conversation with Tools off | no tools, plus the note that tools are off (0.20) |
| Cowork with Search off | all 32 other tools, `web_fetch` removed |

Earlier versions filtered a mode's tool list against the tools visible to plugins. That silently dropped preset tools, for example `read` and `grep` in a custom "Review" mode. Now fixed.

# Notify

Host plugin `@local/dsh-notify` (dsh 0.2.2-rc.1). dsh has no desktop notifications; this runs a command **you list** when something happens. **Nothing is configured by default**: with no rules it does not even listen.

## Configuration

```yaml
- id: notify
  config:
    rules:
      - id: <ID>
        on: turnEnd                       # turnEnd | approval
        reasons: [completed, error]       # turnEnd only: completed | error | aborted | blocked | interrupted
        minSeconds: 0                     # turnEnd only: skip turns shorter than this
        topLevelOnly: true                # ignore sub-agent turns
        minIntervalSeconds: 5             # at least this long between two runs of this rule
        timeoutMs: 5000                   # the command is killed after this
        command: [<PROGRAM>, <ARG>, ...]
    maxPerMinute: 20                      # across all rules
    commandName: notify
```

- `turnEnd` fires when a top-level turn ends. A scheduled run is an ordinary turn, so it is covered. `approval` fires when dsh asks you to approve a tool call (for example one asked by the media-tools gate).
- A rule with a bad or empty `command`, an unknown reason or a duplicate id fails at load.

## The command

It runs **without a shell** (`execFile`): `command[0]` is the program, the rest are its arguments. The message is fixed generic text, for example `Finished in <project folder name>`, `Stopped with an error in <project>`, `Waiting for your approval (<tool name>) in <project>`; **it never contains your prompt, the model's words or the approval reason**.

The command gets these environment variables, which is the safe way to use them (for example in AppleScript through `system attribute`): `DSH_NOTIFY_MESSAGE`, `DSH_NOTIFY_EVENT`, `DSH_NOTIFY_REASON`, `DSH_NOTIFY_TOOL`, `DSH_NOTIFY_PROJECT` (control characters removed, at most 200 characters). Arguments may also contain `{message}`, `{event}`, `{reason}`, `{tool}`, `{project}`; those values are cut to 120 characters of letters, digits and `space . _ : / - ( ) ,` (anything else becomes `?`), so a project folder named with quotes cannot inject into a script. Prefer the environment variables.

macOS example:

```yaml
command: [osascript, -e, 'display notification (system attribute "DSH_NOTIFY_MESSAGE") with title "dsh"']
```

## Safety and behaviour

- Never blocks a turn: the command runs in the background; a failure or timeout is counted and logged, not raised.
- Flood control: `minIntervalSeconds` per rule and `maxPerMinute` overall.
- Events replayed from history (resuming a session) do not notify.
- `/notify` shows rules and counts (started, failed and the last error code, skipped by the rate limit); `/notify test [rule]` runs a rule with a sample event and ignores the rate limits. Service `notify`: `rules`, `test`, `stats`.

## Checked

13 unit tests (helpers, config refusals, no listener without rules, args and environment, reasons, `minSeconds`, sub-agents ignored, approval without the reason text, injection attempt in the project folder and tool name, rate limits, failure and slow command not blocking, replay ignored, `/notify`). Live in a real dsh headless profile with a recording script: a plain turn gave `Finished in <folder>` and the project name came from the session's working folder; an approval asked by the media-tools gate gave `Waiting for your approval (bash) in <folder>` and then the turn end. Not tested: a real macOS banner (the recording script stood in for `osascript`), the app UI, phone notifications.

# DeepSeek Harness Plus

Extra features for the **DeepSeek Harness** desktop app on the Mac: a MindsHub-style sidebar with Chat, Cowork and Code tabs, colour schemes (including MindsHub's navy and teal), work modes, model tiers, a blind model arena, agent swarms, deep research, a usage counter, benchmarks, syncing between Macs and more. Twenty-six add-ons in all, listed in [docs/ADD-ONS.md](docs/ADD-ONS.md).

The add-ons plug into the normal app. Nothing in the app itself is changed, so app updates do not wipe them, and you can remove them at any time.

## What you need

- A Mac with the **DeepSeek Harness** app in your Applications folder, version **0.2.2 or newer, below 0.3**.
- Open the app **once** before installing, so it creates its settings, then quit it.

1. Download the newest **`DS-Harness-Plus-<version>.dmg`** from the [Releases page](https://github.com/BLCKHWK60/DS-Harness-Plus/releases/latest) and double-click it. A window opens with everything in it: all the add-ons, the installer and this guide. (If you use git, clone the project instead; it is the same folder.)
2. In that window, double-click **`Install.command`**.
   - The first time, macOS may say it "cannot be opened because it is from an unidentified developer". If it does, **right-click** the file, choose **Open**, then **Open** again. You only do this once.
3. A Terminal window opens and walks you through it. If the app is open, it asks to quit it. When it says **Done**, open DeepSeek Harness.

Installing copies the add-ons into the app's own data folder (`~/.dsh/addons`), so you can eject the disk image and delete the download afterwards. To remove the add-ons later, open the disk image again and double-click **`Uninstall.command`**.

Before it changes anything, the installer saves your current setup under `~/.dsh/backups/deepseek-harness-plus/`. If any step fails, it puts everything back by itself.

**Terminal instead:** if you prefer, run this from the unpacked folder:

```bash
bash scripts/install.sh
```

## First steps

1. **Add your models.** Go to **Settings → Models** in the app. You can paste an API key for a provider there, or add your own server (for example a model server on another computer). No files to edit.
2. **Look at the new pages.** **Settings** now has **Colours, Model Tiers, Modes, Sampling, Usage, Benchmark, Arena** and **Swarm** pages. The chat box (where you type) gets one **model button** beside the send button, with the model list, an effort slider from Off to Ultra Code, tiers and sampling, and, once set up, a model-health dot.
3. **Switch on what you want.** Some add-ons work right away. The others do nothing until you give them a little setup, for example which models the arena should compare. [docs/ADD-ONS.md](docs/ADD-ONS.md) says which is which and how to set each one up.

### What works the moment you install

- **Cowork sidebar:** Chat, Cowork and Code tabs at the top of the left sidebar. Each tab lists only its own conversations and projects, and has its own sections: Model Arena under Chat, and Automation tasks, Connectors (your MCP servers, with on/off switches) and Skills under Cowork and Code. The start page gets a greeting and suggestion chips. A tab picks the mode of new conversations, so the chat box no longer needs a mode drop-down. To get the normal sidebar back, switch **Cowork sidebar** off on the **Plugins** page.
- **Colours:** pick a colour scheme in **Settings → Colours**: DeepSeek Harness (the stock colours, the default), MindsHub Cowork, Graphite or Forest, each in light and dark.
- **Modes:** Chat, Cowork and Code modes, switchable per conversation, plus **Search** and **Deep research** buttons in the chat box.
- **Model Tiers:** one model button in the chat box: pick any model and drag the effort slider. Five starter tiers (Fast, Balanced, Deep, Creative, Code review) work at once on whatever model you use. No model is preconfigured.
- **Code map:** a compact map of the project a conversation works in, so the assistant looks things up instead of reading whole files. Plus four "reverse engineer" skills. Nothing to install.
- **Privacy:** switches off the app's usage reporting and the upload of a conversation when you rate an answer. `/privacy` shows the state.
- **Usage counter:** counts requests and tokens per day and model (never your text).
- **Deep research** and **Code power:** new tools and skills the assistant can use.

Everything else stays switched off until you set it up.

## Changing an add-on's settings

Some add-ons have their own page in **Settings** (Tiers, Modes, Sampling). The rest are set up in the app's settings file. To edit it:

1. Quit DeepSeek Harness.
2. In Finder press **⌘ Shift G**, paste `~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/` and press Return.
3. Make a copy of **`cordis.patch.yml`** first, as your own backup. Then open the original with TextEdit.
4. Paste in the block for the add-on you want, from its section in [docs/ADD-ONS.md](docs/ADD-ONS.md). Fill in the parts in `<ANGLE BRACKETS>`, save, and open the app.

The file is indentation-sensitive: use spaces, never tabs, and keep the lines lined up as in the example. If the app will not start after an edit, put your copy back.

## Updating

Download the newer version and double-click **`Install.command`** again. It replaces the add-ons and keeps your settings.

## Removing

Double-click **`Uninstall.command`**. It removes all twenty-two add-ons and their files. Your conversations and your models are not touched. Any settings you wrote for the add-ons stay in the settings file and do nothing; if you install again, they come back into effect.

## Using it on a second Mac

1. Install the DeepSeek Harness app on the other Mac and open it once.
2. Run **`Install.command`** there too.
3. Add your models in **Settings → Models**.
4. Optional: to keep the same **settings** on both Macs, use iCloud Drive (below).
5. Optional: to see the same **conversations** on both Macs, set up the **Sync** add-on (see [docs/ADD-ONS.md](docs/ADD-ONS.md#sync)). It needs a private git repository that both Macs can reach. Neither Mac has to be switched on for the other to sync.

### Same settings on both Macs, through iCloud Drive

The **Shared settings** add-on keeps the settings you change in the app's own pages in one file, `settings.json`, in a folder in iCloud Drive. Those settings are Modes, Model Tiers, the Cowork tabs, Sampling presets and Colours. Change something on one Mac and the other Mac picks it up within about a minute. The file never holds secrets: API keys, tokens and passwords stay on each Mac.

1. On the first Mac, double-click **`Install.command`** and answer **y** when it asks *"Share settings through iCloud Drive?"*. It uses the folder **iCloud Drive → DeepSeek Harness Plus**.
2. On the second Mac, do the same. When the app opens there, it takes the settings from the file. Its own earlier settings are kept in `~/.dsh/shared-settings/backups`.

**Good to know:**
- Not shared:
  - which conversation sits in which tab;
  - the tier a conversation uses;
  - which add-ons are switched on;
  - settings written by hand into the settings file rather than in a Settings page.
- If you change the same setting on both Macs at once, the copy in iCloud wins. The other value is kept in the backups folder.
- iCloud sometimes makes a copy such as `settings 2.json` when both Macs write at the same moment. `/shared-settings` tells you if one appears; check it, then delete it.

## Giving it to someone else

Send them the link to this project, https://github.com/BLCKHWK60/DS-Harness-Plus. They follow **Install** above. Nothing in here contains your addresses, keys or personal settings; every add-on starts empty.

## If something goes wrong

- **"DeepSeek Harness is not installed"**: the app must be in `/Applications` or `~/Applications`.
- **"No 'desktop' setup found"**: open the app once, quit it, and run the installer again.
- **"version ... works with version 0.2.2 up to 0.3"**: your app is newer or older than this release supports. Look for a newer DeepSeek Harness Plus.
- **The installer stopped with a problem**: it has already put everything back. The message names a log file; send that file to whoever helps you.
- **The app misbehaves after installing**: run **`Uninstall.command`**. Every install and uninstall also leaves a dated copy of your setup files in `~/.dsh/backups/deepseek-harness-plus/`, in case someone helping you needs them.
- **The app will not start after you edited the settings file**: put back the copy you made before editing.

## What is in this folder

| Folder or file | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `Install.command`, `Uninstall.command` | Double-click to install or remove. |
| `addons/` | The twenty-two add-ons. Each has a `README.md` with its full technical notes. |
| `docs/ADD-ONS.md` | What each add-on does and how to set it up. |
| `docs/HOW-IT-WORKS.md` | For technical readers: how the install works, how to test, how to change an add-on. |
| `templates/` | Optional ready-to-fill examples: model servers, memory, MCP tool servers, backups. |
| `extras/dsh-intel-mcp/` | Optional Python tools (code map, reverse engineering, context store). Needs Python; not installed automatically. |
| `scripts/` | What the `.command` files run. |
| `VERSION` | This release's version number. |
| `LICENSE` | The MIT licence: anyone may use, change and share this. |

## Status

Release 0.29.2 (the version in `VERSION`). Tested so far:

- **Install, update and uninstall:** run on a fresh setup and on a copy of a real, long-used setup.
- **Live start:** the app starts with every add-on loaded.
- **Add-ons:** each has its own automated tests, and each settings page was checked in the app's web version.
- **Not yet tested on another person's Mac.** Each add-on's `README.md` lists what was and was not verified for it.
