# PDF reader

Lets a model read PDF files properly, with a page number for everything. It uses the parts that come with macOS (PDFKit for text and pictures, Vision for text recognition), so there is nothing to install and nothing leaves the Mac. It works the moment it is installed.

## What the model gets

Five tools:

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `pdf_info` | Number of pages, title, the PDF's own contents list with page numbers, and which pages are scans |
| `pdf_read` | The text of a range of pages, each under `--- page N of M ---`. A long range stops at a size limit and says where to continue. `layout: true` keeps columns apart, for tables and forms |
| `pdf_search` | Where a word or phrase appears: page numbers and the words around each hit. Case, line breaks and words split by a hyphen at a line end do not matter |
| `pdf_page_image` | Saves one page as a PNG picture and returns its path, for charts, diagrams, formulas and handwriting. The model then opens it with the app's `read_image` tool, which needs a model that can see images |
| `pdf_ocr` | Recognises the text on a scanned page from its picture, on this Mac |

And one skill, `read-pdf`, loaded only when used. It makes the model look at the facts first, read in page ranges, search for specific facts, re-read tables in layout mode, send scans to text recognition, and put a page after every claim, such as `(p. 12)`. It also tells the model to list any pages it could not read.

## How to use it

- Put a PDF in the conversation's folder and ask about it by name: "Summarise report.pdf with page numbers."
- `/pdf report.pdf` in a chat shows the page count, contents list and which pages are scans.
- **Settings → PDF reader:** the master switch, more folders PDFs may be read from, "Allow any PDF on this Mac" (off by default), and how much text one read returns.

## Where it may read

These tools open files themselves, so they keep their own fence. A PDF can be read when it is:

- in the conversation's own folder (or a sub-folder), or
- in a folder you listed on the settings page, or
- anywhere, only if you switched on "Allow any PDF on this Mac".

Links that point out of an allowed folder are followed and refused. Only files ending in `.pdf` are opened, up to 500 MB.

## What it keeps

- The text of up to four PDFs is held in memory while the app runs, so repeated reads are instant. It is never written to disk.
- Page pictures are saved under the app's data folder (`pdf-reader/pages/`) and removed after a day.

## Limits

- **Tables:** layout mode separates columns by the gaps between words. That reads simple tables well. Merged cells, tables without clear gaps, and tables spread over pages can still come out wrong.
- **Formulas:** as text they lose superscripts and fractions. The skill tells the model to check them on the page picture.
- **Text recognition** can miss small or isolated characters (in one lab test it dropped a lone digit in a table cell). Lines it found hard to read are flagged in the answer.
- **Password-protected PDFs** cannot be read.
- **macOS only.** On another system the tools answer that they need macOS.
- No converter such as Docling or MinerU is used yet; that is a possible later step for complex tables and maths.

## For developers

- `lib/pdfkit.jxa.js`: a JavaScript-for-Automation script run with `/usr/bin/osascript -l JavaScript`. Requests: `load` (all text, outline, facts), `layout` (words with their places), `image`, `ocr`. One JSON request in, one JSON answer out.
- `lib/reader.js`: caching, page ranges, the size limit, search. `lib/layout.js`: columns from word positions, reading order for recognised lines. `lib/access.js`: the fence.
- Service `pdfReader` (apiVersion 1): `info(path, cwd?)`, `read(path, options?, cwd?)`, under the same fence. Meant for other add-ons.
- Route `GET /dsh-pdf/status`. Command `/pdf`.

## Checked

- **Unit tests:** 8 (`test/`): the fence (including links and `..`), page ranges and the size limit, facts, search across line breaks, columns and reading order, every tool refusing politely, settings, the skill, tidying up old pictures. One test builds a real two-page PDF and a scanned copy on this Mac and reads back the text, the table in columns, a page picture and the recognised scan.
- **By hand:** the 158-page Bash manual that ships with macOS: all text in about 0.4 s; layout mode on three pages in 0.6 s.
- **Live, in the throwaway web profile with a test model server:** the five tools and the skill are offered to the model; `pdf_read` with layout returned the table in columns; `pdf_ocr` read a scanned page; `pdf_page_image` saved a picture and the app's `read_image` reached that file; a PDF outside the allowed folders was refused; the settings page saved a folder.
- **Not checked:** a real model following the skill; `read_image` showing a page picture to a model that can see images (the lab model cannot); large scanned documents; PDFs in other scripts than Latin; the Mac desktop app (the lab is the web version).

# Privacy

Plugin `@local/dsh-privacy` (dsh 0.2.2-rc.1). It switches off the app's two reporting channels to its maker, and `/privacy` shows whether they are off. It works at once; there is nothing to set up.

## What it switches off

| Channel | What the app sends by default | How it is switched off |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Conversation upload on feedback** | When you rate an answer (thumbs up or down) or use `/feedback`, the conversation up to that point is uploaded, unredacted, for any model including local ones, with an anonymous install id | The app's `session-telemetry-otel` row is disabled. This is exactly what the app's own `DSH_TELEMETRY_DISABLED` switch does |
| **Usage events** (desktop app only) | An event for each message sent, with the model name, effort, mode, a conversation id, device and account ids, app version, and the Mac's processor, memory and macOS version; also model, mode and plugin changes. No prompts or answers | The app's `product-analytics` setting `enabled` is set to `false`, the app's own off value. With it off the app collects no environment data, reads no identity and accepts no events |

Both are done by this add-on's `cordis.patch.yml`, so they are part of the Plus install and are undone by switching the add-on off on the Plugins page (and restarting the app) or by uninstalling Plus. You can still rate answers; the rating then stays on your Mac.

## What stays on

These are not reporting, and this add-on leaves them alone:

- **Update checks** to the app's download server (app version and platform).
- **Your DeepSeek sign-in** and the balance in the sidebar, while you are signed in. Sign out if you use no DeepSeek cloud models.
- **The plugin list**, fetched from the addresses in your plugin-market setting.
- **Web search and fetch**, when a conversation uses them: the search words and page addresses go to the search service you chose.
- **Any cloud model you pick**: its provider receives the conversation, as with any cloud model.

With a local model, prompts and answers go only to your model server. Conversation titles are written by the conversation's own model.

For certainty about every connection, use a firewall app such as Little Snitch or LuLu.

## `/privacy`

Prints the live state of both channels, read from the app's loaded rows, and lists what stays on. The same check runs three seconds after the app starts and writes one line to the log: information when both are off, a warning otherwise. Service `privacy`: `state()` returns `{feedbackUpload, usageEvents, lines}`.

## Checked

- Unit tests (3): each "off" value is recognised, rows that are on are reported as on, and the bundle patch contains both switches.
- In a throwaway profile, the app's composed setup (`--dump-config`) before and after installing: `session-telemetry-otel` gained `disabled: true` ("patched by @local/dsh-privacy"), and `product-analytics` went from `enabled: true` to `enabled: false`.
- `/privacy` typed in a chat in the web lab reported both channels off.

**Not checked:** the network traffic itself was not captured, so "off" rests on the app's own switches doing what its code says. The usage-events row only runs in the desktop app, and the lab is the web version, so that switch was verified in the composed setup, not on a running desktop app. This was read from app version 0.2.2-rc.1; a later version could add or rename a channel, and `/privacy` would then still say "off" for a row it does not know. Re-check after an app update.

# DeepSeek Harness Plus

Extra features for the **DeepSeek Harness** desktop app on the Mac: a MindsHub-style sidebar with Chat, Cowork and Code tabs, colour schemes (including MindsHub's navy and teal), work modes, model tiers, a blind model arena, agent swarms, deep research, a usage counter, benchmarks, syncing between Macs and more. Twenty-six add-ons in all, listed in [docs/ADD-ONS.md](docs/ADD-ONS.md).

The add-ons plug into the normal app. Nothing in the app itself is changed, so app updates do not wipe them, and you can remove them at any time.

You do not need to know how to code to install or use this.

---

## What you need

- A Mac with the **DeepSeek Harness** app in your Applications folder, version **0.2.2 or newer, below 0.3**.
- Open the app **once** before installing, so it creates its settings, then quit it.

## Install

1. Download the newest **`DS-Harness-Plus-<version>.dmg`** from the [Releases page](https://github.com/BLCKHWK60/DS-Harness-Plus/releases/latest) and double-click it. A window opens with everything in it: all the add-ons, the installer and this guide. (If you use git, clone the project instead; it is the same folder.)
2. In that window, double-click **`Install.command`**.
   - The first time, macOS may say it "cannot be opened because it is from an unidentified developer". If it does, **right-click** the file, choose **Open**, then **Open** again. You only do this once.
3. A Terminal window opens and walks you through it. If the app is open, it asks to quit it. When it says **Done**, open DeepSeek Harness.

Installing copies the add-ons into the app's own data folder (`~/.dsh/addons`), so you can eject the disk image and delete the download afterwards. To remove the add-ons later, open the disk image again and double-click **`Uninstall.command`**.

Before it changes anything, the installer saves your current setup under `~/.dsh/backups/deepseek-harness-plus/`. If any step fails, it puts everything back by itself.

**Terminal instead:** if you prefer, run this from the unpacked folder:

```bash
bash scripts/install.sh
```

## First steps

1. **Add your models.** Go to **Settings → Models** in the app. You can paste an API key for a provider there, or add your own server (for example a model server on another computer). No files to edit.
2. **Look at the new pages.** **Settings** now has **Colours, Model Tiers, Modes, Sampling, Usage, Benchmark, Arena** and **Swarm** pages. The chat box (where you type) gets one **model button** beside the send button, with the model list, an effort slider from Off to Ultra Code, tiers and sampling, and, once set up, a model-health dot.
3. **Switch on what you want.** Some add-ons work right away. The others do nothing until you give them a little setup, for example which models the arena should compare. [docs/ADD-ONS.md](docs/ADD-ONS.md) says which is which and how to set each one up.

### What works the moment you install

- **Cowork sidebar:** Chat, Cowork and Code tabs at the top of the left sidebar. Each tab lists only its own conversations and projects, and has its own sections: Model Arena under Chat, and Automation tasks, Connectors (your MCP servers, with on/off switches) and Skills under Cowork and Code. The start page gets a greeting and suggestion chips. A tab picks the mode of new conversations, so the chat box no longer needs a mode drop-down. To get the normal sidebar back, switch **Cowork sidebar** off on the **Plugins** page.
- **Colours:** pick a colour scheme in **Settings → Colours**: DeepSeek Harness (the stock colours, the default), MindsHub Cowork, Graphite or Forest, each in light and dark.
- **Modes:** Chat, Cowork and Code modes, switchable per conversation, plus **Search** and **Deep research** buttons in the chat box.
- **Model Tiers:** one model button in the chat box: pick any model and drag the effort slider. Five starter tiers (Fast, Balanced, Deep, Creative, Code review) work at once on whatever model you use. No model is preconfigured.
- **Code map:** a compact map of the project a conversation works in, so the assistant looks things up instead of reading whole files. Plus four "reverse engineer" skills. Nothing to install.
- **Privacy:** switches off the app's usage reporting and the upload of a conversation when you rate an answer. `/privacy` shows the state.
- **Usage counter:** counts requests and tokens per day and model (never your text).
- **Deep research** and **Code power:** new tools and skills the assistant can use.

Everything else stays switched off until you set it up.

## Changing an add-on's settings

Some add-ons have their own page in **Settings** (Tiers, Modes, Sampling). The rest are set up in the app's settings file. To edit it:

1. Quit DeepSeek Harness.
2. In Finder press **⌘ Shift G**, paste `~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/` and press Return.
3. Make a copy of **`cordis.patch.yml`** first, as your own backup. Then open the original with TextEdit.
4. Paste in the block for the add-on you want, from its section in [docs/ADD-ONS.md](docs/ADD-ONS.md). Fill in the parts in `<ANGLE BRACKETS>`, save, and open the app.

The file is indentation-sensitive: use spaces, never tabs, and keep the lines lined up as in the example. If the app will not start after an edit, put your copy back.

## Updating

Download the newer version and double-click **`Install.command`** again. It replaces the add-ons and keeps your settings.

## Removing

Double-click **`Uninstall.command`**. It removes all twenty-two add-ons and their files. Your conversations and your models are not touched. Any settings you wrote for the add-ons stay in the settings file and do nothing; if you install again, they come back into effect.

## Using it on a second Mac

1. Install the DeepSeek Harness app on the other Mac and open it once.
2. Run **`Install.command`** there too.
3. Add your models in **Settings → Models**.
4. Optional: to keep the same **settings** on both Macs, use iCloud Drive (below).
5. Optional: to see the same **conversations** on both Macs, set up the **Sync** add-on (see [docs/ADD-ONS.md](docs/ADD-ONS.md#sync)). It needs a private git repository that both Macs can reach. Neither Mac has to be switched on for the other to sync.

### Same settings on both Macs, through iCloud Drive

The **Shared settings** add-on keeps the settings you change in the app's own pages in one file, `settings.json`, in a folder in iCloud Drive. Those settings are Modes, Model Tiers, the Cowork tabs, Sampling presets and Colours. Change something on one Mac and the other Mac picks it up within about a minute. The file never holds secrets: API keys, tokens and passwords stay on each Mac.

1. On the first Mac, double-click **`Install.command`** and answer **y** when it asks *"Share settings through iCloud Drive?"*. It uses the folder **iCloud Drive → DeepSeek Harness Plus**.
2. On the second Mac, do the same. When the app opens there, it takes the settings from the file. Its own earlier settings are kept in `~/.dsh/shared-settings/backups`.

To use another folder, or from Terminal: `bash scripts/install.sh --settings "<folder>"`. To stop sharing on one Mac: `bash scripts/install.sh --no-settings`. Type `/shared-settings` in a conversation to see what is shared and when it last synced.

**Good to know:**
- Not shared:
  - which conversation sits in which tab;
  - the tier a conversation uses;
  - which add-ons are switched on;
  - settings written by hand into the settings file rather than in a Settings page.
- If you change the same setting on both Macs at once, the copy in iCloud wins. The other value is kept in the backups folder.
- iCloud sometimes makes a copy such as `settings 2.json` when both Macs write at the same moment. `/shared-settings` tells you if one appears; check it, then delete it.

## Giving it to someone else

Send them the link to this project, https://github.com/BLCKHWK60/DS-Harness-Plus. They follow **Install** above. Nothing in here contains your addresses, keys or personal settings; every add-on starts empty.

## If something goes wrong

- **"DeepSeek Harness is not installed"**: the app must be in `/Applications` or `~/Applications`.
- **"No 'desktop' setup found"**: open the app once, quit it, and run the installer again.
- **"version ... works with version 0.2.2 up to 0.3"**: your app is newer or older than this release supports. Look for a newer DeepSeek Harness Plus.
- **The installer stopped with a problem**: it has already put everything back. The message names a log file; send that file to whoever helps you.
- **The app misbehaves after installing**: run **`Uninstall.command`**. Every install and uninstall also leaves a dated copy of your setup files in `~/.dsh/backups/deepseek-harness-plus/`, in case someone helping you needs them.
- **The app will not start after you edited the settings file**: put back the copy you made before editing.

## What is in this folder

| Folder or file | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `Install.command`, `Uninstall.command` | Double-click to install or remove. |
| `addons/` | The twenty-two add-ons. Each has a `README.md` with its full technical notes. |
| `docs/ADD-ONS.md` | What each add-on does and how to set it up. |
| `docs/HOW-IT-WORKS.md` | For technical readers: how the install works, how to test, how to change an add-on. |
| `templates/` | Optional ready-to-fill examples: model servers, memory, MCP tool servers, backups. |
| `extras/dsh-intel-mcp/` | Optional Python tools (code map, reverse engineering, context store). Needs Python; not installed automatically. |
| `scripts/` | What the `.command` files run. |
| `VERSION` | This release's version number. |
| `LICENSE` | The MIT licence: anyone may use, change and share this. |

## Status

Release 0.29.2 (the version in `VERSION`). Tested so far:

- **Install, update and uninstall:** run on a fresh setup and on a copy of a real, long-used setup.
- **Live start:** the app starts with every add-on loaded.
- **Add-ons:** each has its own automated tests, and each settings page was checked in the app's web version.
- **Not yet tested on another person's Mac.** Each add-on's `README.md` lists what was and was not verified for it.

# Role prompts

Host plugin `@local/dsh-role-prompts` (dsh 0.2.2-rc.1). It adds instruction sections you write to the system prompt of every Agent, in an order you choose, optionally only on chosen tiers.

**Nothing is configured by default**: `sections` is empty, so installing the plugin changes no prompt. Ready-made texts are in `examples/` (`planning.txt`, `coding.txt`, `routing.txt`); they are examples to copy, not defaults.

## Configuration

```yaml
- id: role-prompts
  config:
    sections:
      <NAME>:
        enabled: true          # false removes the section from the next step on
        order: 60              # ascending; Tier's own section is 70
        appliesToTiers: []     # tier ids; empty = every tier, otherwise only those tiers
        text: |
          <YOUR INSTRUCTIONS>
```

- Each section is a separate prompt section named `role-prompts:<NAME>`. Suggested orders so tier text follows role text: planning 60, coding 65, routing 72 (after Tier at 70).
- `appliesToTiers` needs the Tier plugin (`modelTiers` service); without it a section restricted to tiers is not added.
- The text is inserted literally: `{{...}}` in it is not treated as a prompt variable.
- Prompt text is model-visible and logged with the rest of the system prompt.

## Not implemented

- The spec's `mode: replace` (replacing the whole system prompt). dsh allows only one "complete" section and fails prompt assembly if two exist, so it was left out.
- Measuring the prompt against a token budget (use `token-meter`).
- A Settings page; edit the profile patch.

## Verified (mock setup, rc.1)

Sections appear in the model request in `order` relative to Tier's section; a section restricted to `opus` appears only on that tier; `enabled: false` hides it; `{{not_a_variable}}` stays literal; the three example texts load.

# Route health

Host plugin `@local/dsh-route-health` (dsh 0.2.2-rc.1). It checks that your model routes are reachable and, with the Tier plugin (`plugins/dsh-model-tiers`), moves a Session to its tier's fallback route when a route is down.

**Nothing is configured by default**: `routes` is empty and the plugin does nothing until you add your own (no address, route name or key is baked in).

## Configuration

```yaml
- id: route-health
  config:
    routes:
      <ROUTE_NAME>:            # the provider route id, as in llm-pi-ai `providers`
        probeUrl: <PROBE_URL>  # for example <BASE_URL>/models
        label: <LABEL>
        timeoutMs: 2500        # no answer within this = failed probe
        slowMs: 1000           # answered but slower than this = "slow"
        failureThreshold: 2    # consecutive failed probes before "down"
        reprobeSeconds: 20     # probe interval while down
        intervalSeconds: 30    # probe interval while up
    preemptiveFallback: true   # move Sessions off a down route
    autoReturn: true           # move them back when it recovers
    onlyWhenTierUsesRoute: true
    blockWhenDown: true        # refuse a step on a down route with a clear error
    commandName: routes        # the /routes command
```

Any HTTP answer below 500 counts as reachable, so no credential is needed. A refused connection, a timeout or a 5xx fails the probe.

## Behaviour

- **States:** `unknown`, `up`, `slow`, `down`. A route goes `down` after `failureThreshold` consecutive failed probes and is re-probed every `reprobeSeconds`.
- **Only used routes are probed** (`onlyWhenTierUsesRoute`): a route is probed when a live Session is on it, or on a tier that has it as primary or fallback, or when this plugin moved a Session off it.
- **Pre-emptive fallback:** when a route goes down, each live Session on it is moved to the next usable route of its tier's fallback chain (`modelTiers.advanceFallback`), at a turn boundary, so the next message already goes there. Routes known to be down are skipped.
- **Return:** when the route recovers, Sessions this plugin moved are moved back (`modelTiers.restorePrimary`), at a turn boundary, never mid-turn.
- **Guard:** before a step the plugin refreshes a stale state; if the route is down the step is refused with an error that names the route and the reason, instead of hanging. If a fallback exists, the Session is moved to it and the error tells the user to send the message again.
- **`/routes`** prints each route's state, latency or error, and the time of the last probe.
- **Service `routeHealth`:** `state(route)`, `list()`, `probeNow(route)`, `on('route/health-changed' | 'route/fallback', handler)`.

## Limits

- **UI badge (browser half, `client.js`):** a status dot in the composer, left of the Mode selector. It shows nothing until routes are configured. When every route is up it is a green dot; when one is slow or down the dot turns amber or red and names the route (for example "Closed port"); a click lists every route with its state, latency, last error and age. It reads the host half's read-only route `GET /dsh-route-health/state` (behind dsh's connection fence: login cookie plus Host/Origin check; 405 for any other method; no keys and no probe URLs in the answer) every 10 s while the tab is visible. The request carries `?probe=1`, which probes routes that are unknown or older than 30 s (at most once per 8 s per route), so a route no live Session uses still gets a real state instead of staying "not checked". A page reload after a client change needs the host restarted. A separate banner is not built: the red badge with the route name is the warning.
- Verified in a throwaway web profile (up, slow and closed-port routes; 401 without cookie; the badge, the pop-over and the colours read back from the page). **Not verified:** the desktop app itself (its Electron shell forwards the same authenticated requests, so it should work); the light theme; a route that recovers while the pop-over is open.
- Wake-on-LAN or keeping the host awake is host configuration, not plugin code.
- A route cannot be switched in the middle of a step on rc.1 (the route is fixed per step), so the step in flight when a route dies still ends with the provider error.
- Fallback to a cloud route cannot be forbidden for a private tier yet (spec 6.3 `localOnly`): Tier has no such flag.

# DeepSeek Harness Plus

Extra features for the **DeepSeek Harness** desktop app on the Mac: a MindsHub-style sidebar with Chat, Cowork and Code tabs, colour schemes (including MindsHub's navy and teal), work modes, model tiers, a blind model arena, agent swarms, deep research, a usage counter, benchmarks, syncing between Macs and more. Twenty-six add-ons in all, listed in [docs/ADD-ONS.md](docs/ADD-ONS.md).

The add-ons plug into the normal app. Nothing in the app itself is changed, so app updates do not wipe them, and you can remove them at any time.

You do not need to know how to code to install or use this.

---

## What you need

- A Mac with the **DeepSeek Harness** app in your Applications folder, version **0.2.2 or newer, below 0.3**.
- Open the app **once** before installing, so it creates its settings, then quit it.

## Install

1. Download the newest **`DS-Harness-Plus-<version>.dmg`** from the [Releases page](https://github.com/BLCKHWK60/DS-Harness-Plus/releases/latest) and double-click it. A window opens with everything in it: all the add-ons, the installer and this guide. (If you use git, clone the project instead; it is the same folder.)
2. In that window, double-click **`Install.command`**.
   - The first time, macOS may say it "cannot be opened because it is from an unidentified developer". If it does, **right-click** the file, choose **Open**, then **Open** again. You only do this once.
3. A Terminal window opens and walks you through it. If the app is open, it asks to quit it. When it says **Done**, open DeepSeek Harness.

Installing copies the add-ons into the app's own data folder (`~/.dsh/addons`), so you can eject the disk image and delete the download afterwards. To remove the add-ons later, open the disk image again and double-click **`Uninstall.command`**.

Before it changes anything, the installer saves your current setup under `~/.dsh/backups/deepseek-harness-plus/`. If any step fails, it puts everything back by itself.

**Terminal instead:** if you prefer, run this from the unpacked folder:

```bash
bash scripts/install.sh
```

## First steps

1. **Add your models.** Go to **Settings → Models** in the app. You can paste an API key for a provider there, or add your own server (for example a model server on another computer). No files to edit.
2. **Look at the new pages.** **Settings** now has **Colours, Model Tiers, Modes, Sampling, Usage, Benchmark, Arena** and **Swarm** pages. The chat box (where you type) gets one **model button** beside the send button, with the model list, an effort slider from Off to Ultra Code, tiers and sampling, and, once set up, a model-health dot.
3. **Switch on what you want.** Some add-ons work right away. The others do nothing until you give them a little setup, for example which models the arena should compare. [docs/ADD-ONS.md](docs/ADD-ONS.md) says which is which and how to set each one up.

### What works the moment you install

- **Cowork sidebar:** Chat, Cowork and Code tabs at the top of the left sidebar. Each tab lists only its own conversations and projects, and has its own sections: Model Arena under Chat, and Automation tasks, Connectors (your MCP servers, with on/off switches) and Skills under Cowork and Code. The start page gets a greeting and suggestion chips. A tab picks the mode of new conversations, so the chat box no longer needs a mode drop-down. To get the normal sidebar back, switch **Cowork sidebar** off on the **Plugins** page.
- **Colours:** pick a colour scheme in **Settings → Colours**: DeepSeek Harness (the stock colours, the default), MindsHub Cowork, Graphite or Forest, each in light and dark.
- **Modes:** Chat, Cowork and Code modes, switchable per conversation, plus **Search** and **Deep research** buttons in the chat box.
- **Model Tiers:** one model button in the chat box: pick any model and drag the effort slider. Five starter tiers (Fast, Balanced, Deep, Creative, Code review) work at once on whatever model you use. No model is preconfigured.
- **Code map:** a compact map of the project a conversation works in, so the assistant looks things up instead of reading whole files. Plus four "reverse engineer" skills. Nothing to install.
- **Privacy:** switches off the app's usage reporting and the upload of a conversation when you rate an answer. `/privacy` shows the state.
- **Usage counter:** counts requests and tokens per day and model (never your text).
- **Deep research** and **Code power:** new tools and skills the assistant can use.

Everything else stays switched off until you set it up.

## Changing an add-on's settings

Some add-ons have their own page in **Settings** (Tiers, Modes, Sampling). The rest are set up in the app's settings file. To edit it:

1. Quit DeepSeek Harness.
2. In Finder press **⌘ Shift G**, paste `~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/` and press Return.
3. Make a copy of **`cordis.patch.yml`** first, as your own backup. Then open the original with TextEdit.
4. Paste in the block for the add-on you want, from its section in [docs/ADD-ONS.md](docs/ADD-ONS.md). Fill in the parts in `<ANGLE BRACKETS>`, save, and open the app.

The file is indentation-sensitive: use spaces, never tabs, and keep the lines lined up as in the example. If the app will not start after an edit, put your copy back.

## Updating

Download the newer version and double-click **`Install.command`** again. It replaces the add-ons and keeps your settings.

## Removing

Double-click **`Uninstall.command`**. It removes all twenty-two add-ons and their files. Your conversations and your models are not touched. Any settings you wrote for the add-ons stay in the settings file and do nothing; if you install again, they come back into effect.

## Using it on a second Mac

1. Install the DeepSeek Harness app on the other Mac and open it once.
2. Run **`Install.command`** there too.
3. Add your models in **Settings → Models**.
4. Optional: to keep the same **settings** on both Macs, use iCloud Drive (below).
5. Optional: to see the same **conversations** on both Macs, set up the **Sync** add-on (see [docs/ADD-ONS.md](docs/ADD-ONS.md#sync)). It needs a private git repository that both Macs can reach. Neither Mac has to be switched on for the other to sync.

### Same settings on both Macs, through iCloud Drive

The **Shared settings** add-on keeps the settings you change in the app's own pages in one file, `settings.json`, in a folder in iCloud Drive. Those settings are Modes, Model Tiers, the Cowork tabs, Sampling presets and Colours. Change something on one Mac and the other Mac picks it up within about a minute. The file never holds secrets: API keys, tokens and passwords stay on each Mac.

1. On the first Mac, double-click **`Install.command`** and answer **y** when it asks *"Share settings through iCloud Drive?"*. It uses the folder **iCloud Drive → DeepSeek Harness Plus**.
2. On the second Mac, do the same. When the app opens there, it takes the settings from the file. Its own earlier settings are kept in `~/.dsh/shared-settings/backups`.

To use another folder, or from Terminal: `bash scripts/install.sh --settings "<folder>"`. To stop sharing on one Mac: `bash scripts/install.sh --no-settings`. Type `/shared-settings` in a conversation to see what is shared and when it last synced.

**Good to know:**
- Not shared:
  - which conversation sits in which tab;
  - the tier a conversation uses;
  - which add-ons are switched on;
  - settings written by hand into the settings file rather than in a Settings page.
- If you change the same setting on both Macs at once, the copy in iCloud wins. The other value is kept in the backups folder.
- iCloud sometimes makes a copy such as `settings 2.json` when both Macs write at the same moment. `/shared-settings` tells you if one appears; check it, then delete it.

## Giving it to someone else

Send them the link to this project, https://github.com/BLCKHWK60/DS-Harness-Plus. They follow **Install** above. Nothing in here contains your addresses, keys or personal settings; every add-on starts empty.

## If something goes wrong

- **"DeepSeek Harness is not installed"**: the app must be in `/Applications` or `~/Applications`.
- **"No 'desktop' setup found"**: open the app once, quit it, and run the installer again.
- **"version ... works with version 0.2.2 up to 0.3"**: your app is newer or older than this release supports. Look for a newer DeepSeek Harness Plus.
- **The installer stopped with a problem**: it has already put everything back. The message names a log file; send that file to whoever helps you.
- **The app misbehaves after installing**: run **`Uninstall.command`**. Every install and uninstall also leaves a dated copy of your setup files in `~/.dsh/backups/deepseek-harness-plus/`, in case someone helping you needs them.
- **The app will not start after you edited the settings file**: put back the copy you made before editing.

## What is in this folder

| Folder or file | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `Install.command`, `Uninstall.command` | Double-click to install or remove. |
| `addons/` | The twenty-two add-ons. Each has a `README.md` with its full technical notes. |
| `docs/ADD-ONS.md` | What each add-on does and how to set it up. |
| `docs/HOW-IT-WORKS.md` | For technical readers: how the install works, how to test, how to change an add-on. |
| `templates/` | Optional ready-to-fill examples: model servers, memory, MCP tool servers, backups. |
| `extras/dsh-intel-mcp/` | Optional Python tools (code map, reverse engineering, context store). Needs Python; not installed automatically. |
| `scripts/` | What the `.command` files run. |
| `VERSION` | This release's version number. |
| `LICENSE` | The MIT licence: anyone may use, change and share this. |

## Status

Release 0.29.2 (the version in `VERSION`). Tested so far:

- **Install, update and uninstall:** run on a fresh setup and on a copy of a real, long-used setup.
- **Live start:** the app starts with every add-on loaded.
- **Add-ons:** each has its own automated tests, and each settings page was checked in the app's web version.
- **Not yet tested on another person's Mac.** Each add-on's `README.md` lists what was and was not verified for it.

# Sampling presets

Host plugin `@local/dsh-sampling-presets` (dsh 0.2.2-rc.1). Named sampling presets chosen per **task category**, per **mode** or per **session**. **Nothing is configured by default**: with no presets the plugin does nothing; a config that names something that does not exist fails at load.

## What dsh can and cannot send

dsh sends only `temperature` and `maxTokens` per request. There is no `top_p`, `top_k`, `min_p` or penalty field, and `stop` is refused by the pi-ai adapter (`UNSUPPORTED_OPTION`), so this plugin has no `stop`. Anything else lives in your inference server. Two delivery paths follow from that:

| Strategy | What it does |
|---|---|
| `in-dsh` | the deprecated `agent/request` hook (its only remaining job on rc.1; it keeps provider, model and effort exactly) sets `temperature` and `maxTokens` from the preset |
| `server-alias` | a preset can name a **model alias** (`perModel[<provider>/<model>].aliases[<preset>]`); at a turn boundary the plugin selects that model id with `agent.model.select()`, so your server applies its own sampling settings for that alias. It only moves between the base model and its own listed aliases; a route you choose yourself is never touched |
| `mixed` (default) | both |

Whether your server can hold several sampling profiles for one model (spec question 15) is yours to know: this plugin just switches between model ids you list, and each alias must also exist in your provider config.

## Which preset applies

1. the category: `/sampling <category>` for this session, else the Modes mode through `byMode`, else `defaultCategory`;
2. `categories[<category>]` names the preset;
3. `perModel[<provider>/<model>].allowedPresets`, when non-empty, can forbid it for that model (the model then runs with its normal sampling).

**Precedence with Tier**: a preset overrides Tier's old per-model defaults whichever plugin loads first (tested both orders), but never a temperature or max-token value you set for the Session in the chat box, and (from Plus 0.10) never a value set by the saved model version the Session is on (`modelTiers.sessionSampling` returns both). Checked live in 0.10: a tier's version asked for 0.9, a preset for 0.1, and the request carried 0.9; the preset's max tokens still applied because the version set none. Tier's `modelTiers` service must be the copy with `sessionSampling` (`plugins/dsh-model-tiers`).

## Configuration

```yaml
- id: sampling-presets
  config:
    presets:
      <NAME>: { temperature: <0 to 2>, maxTokens: <TOKENS>, notes: '<WHY>' }
    categories: { <CATEGORY>: <PRESET NAME> }      # for example code, plan, chat, research, summarize
    byMode: { <MODE ID>: <CATEGORY> }              # with the Modes plugin
    defaultCategory: <CATEGORY>
    perModel:
      '<ROUTE>/<MODEL ID>': { allowedPresets: [<NAME>], aliases: { <NAME>: <ALIAS MODEL ID> } }
    strategy: mixed
    commandName: sampling
```

## Use

`/sampling` shows the category, preset, values, alias and strategy for this session; `/sampling <category>` forces a category; `/sampling auto` returns to the mode or default. Service `samplingPresets`: `list()`, `effective(sessionId)`, `setCategory(sessionId, category|null)`.

## Settings page

Settings > **Sampling** edits everything above without YAML: presets (name, temperature 0 to 2, max tokens, note), categories (preset per category), per-mode rules (mode id, category; mode ids suggested from the Modes plugin), the default category, the strategy (In dsh / Server alias / Both) and the optional per-model rules (allowed presets, alias per preset). Renaming a preset or category follows every reference to it. It will not save a name that is empty or duplicated, a temperature outside 0 to 2, max tokens that are not a whole number from 1 to 1,000,000, a reference to a preset or category that does not exist, or a model rule that is not `provider/model`. It writes through the settings channel in one save, so there is no half-saved state.

This needed one change in the host half: `presets`, `categories`, `byMode`, `defaultCategory`, `perModel` and `strategy` are now `.volatile()` (Settings forms only expose volatile fields), so a save applies at once without reloading the plugin. The YAML shape is unchanged and existing config files keep working. Needs a restart of the app once to load.

Tested: in a throwaway web profile (add, rename with cascade, validation message, save written to the profile patch as normal YAML, values still there after a restart, dark and light, 420 px wide) and end to end in a throwaway headless profile: the plugin was loaded with `presets: {}`, a settings edit added a preset, and the first model request carried that temperature and max tokens (0.33 / 1234) with no restart. Not tested in the desktop app.

## Limits

- An alias is a different model id, so Tier no longer recognises the route as its tier unless the alias is also a tier route or variant; the tier prompt and gates are lost while an alias is selected. Prefer `in-dsh` presets when you use tiers heavily.
- A model switch (alias on or off) happens at a turn boundary, never mid-turn, but it still triggers dsh's model-switch handling and may discard the server's KV cache for the session.
- Category changes through the Modes selector are noticed at the end of the next turn (the plugin reconciles when the Agent goes idle).
- Because the six editable fields are now volatile, the plugin no longer exits early when there are no presets (it installs its hooks and does nothing until a preset applies). `validateConfig` still runs at load: a config file that names something that does not exist fails at start. The Settings page checks the same references before it saves, so a save cannot create that state.

## Verified (rc.1, mock model, throwaway home)

Temperature and max tokens reach the request from the preset (0.1 / 1500). A Tier model profile (0.9 / 3000, shown to apply alone) is overridden in either load order. A composer temperature is respected while the preset still sets max tokens. The alias strategy moved the first step to the alias model (with the preset's temperature); `in-dsh` ignores aliases; a forbidden preset leaves normal sampling. Unit checks cover preset picking and the load-time validation.

## Not verified

oMLX behaviour with real aliases (the spec's own acceptance: the server's request log shows the changed sampling); mode-driven category changes in a running session; the `/sampling` command in the web app; multi-session behaviour; the spec's `stop` field (deliberately dropped).

Download the newer version and double-click **`Install.command`** again. It replaces the add-ons and keeps your settings.

## Removing

Double-click **`Uninstall.command`**. It removes all twenty-two add-ons and their files. Your conversations and your models are not touched. Any settings you wrote for the add-ons stay in the settings file and do nothing; if you install again, they come back into effect.

## Using it on a second Mac

1. Install the DeepSeek Harness app on the other Mac and open it once.
2. Run **`Install.command`** there too.
3. Add your models in **Settings → Models**.
4. Optional: to keep the same **settings** on both Macs, use iCloud Drive (below).
5. Optional: to see the same **conversations** on both Macs, set up the **Sync** add-on (see [docs/ADD-ONS.md](docs/ADD-ONS.md#sync)). It needs a private git repository that both Macs can reach. Neither Mac has to be switched on for the other to sync.

### Same settings on both Macs, through iCloud Drive

The **Shared settings** add-on keeps the settings you change in the app's own pages in one file, `settings.json`, in a folder in iCloud Drive. Those settings are Modes, Model Tiers, the Cowork tabs, Sampling presets and Colours. Change something on one Mac and the other Mac picks it up within about a minute. The file never holds secrets: API keys, tokens and passwords stay on each Mac.

1. On the first Mac, double-click **`Install.command`** and answer **y** when it asks *"Share settings through iCloud Drive?"*. It uses the folder **iCloud Drive → DeepSeek Harness Plus**.
2. On the second Mac, do the same. When the app opens there, it takes the settings from the file. Its own earlier settings are kept in `~/.dsh/shared-settings/backups`.

To use another folder, or from Terminal: `bash scripts/install.sh --settings "<folder>"`. To stop sharing on one Mac: `bash scripts/install.sh --no-settings`. Type `/shared-settings` in a conversation to see what is shared and when it last synced.

**Good to know:**
- Not shared:
  - which conversation sits in which tab;
  - the tier a conversation uses;
  - which add-ons are switched on;
  - settings written by hand into the settings file rather than in a Settings page.
- If you change the same setting on both Macs at once, the copy in iCloud wins. The other value is kept in the backups folder.
- iCloud sometimes makes a copy such as `settings 2.json` when both Macs write at the same moment. `/shared-settings` tells you if one appears; check it, then delete it.

## Giving it to someone else

Send them the link to this project, https://github.com/BLCKHWK60/DS-Harness-Plus. They follow **Install** above. Nothing in here contains your addresses, keys or personal settings; every add-on starts empty.

## If something goes wrong

- **"DeepSeek Harness is not installed"**: the app must be in `/Applications` or `~/Applications`.
- **"No 'desktop' setup found"**: open the app once, quit it, and run the installer again.
- **"version ... works with version 0.2.2 up to 0.3"**: your app is newer or older than this release supports. Look for a newer DeepSeek Harness Plus.
- **The installer stopped with a problem**: it has already put everything back. The message names a log file; send that file to whoever helps you.
- **The app misbehaves after installing**: run **`Uninstall.command`**. Every install and uninstall also leaves a dated copy of your setup files in `~/.dsh/backups/deepseek-harness-plus/`, in case someone helping you needs them.
- **The app will not start after you edited the settings file**: put back the copy you made before editing.

## What is in this folder

| Folder or file | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `Install.command`, `Uninstall.command` | Double-click to install or remove. |
| `addons/` | The twenty-two add-ons. Each has a `README.md` with its full technical notes. |
| `docs/ADD-ONS.md` | What each add-on does and how to set it up. |
| `docs/HOW-IT-WORKS.md` | For technical readers: how the install works, how to test, how to change an add-on. |
| `templates/` | Optional ready-to-fill examples: model servers, memory, MCP tool servers, backups. |
| `extras/dsh-intel-mcp/` | Optional Python tools (code map, reverse engineering, context store). Needs Python; not installed automatically. |
| `scripts/` | What the `.command` files run. |
| `VERSION` | This release's version number. |
| `LICENSE` | The MIT licence: anyone may use, change and share this. |

## Status

Release 0.29.2 (the version in `VERSION`). Tested so far:

- **Install, update and uninstall:** run on a fresh setup and on a copy of a real, long-used setup.
- **Live start:** the app starts with every add-on loaded.
- **Add-ons:** each has its own automated tests, and each settings page was checked in the app's web version.
- **Not yet tested on another person's Mac.** Each add-on's `README.md` lists what was and was not verified for it.

# Shared settings

Host plugin `@local/dsh-shared-settings` (dsh 0.2.2-rc.1). It keeps the settings you change in the app's own pages in one file, `settings.json`, in a folder you choose. With the folder in iCloud Drive, two Macs share one setup.

## What is shared

The add-on reads and writes through the app's own settings service (`ctx.get('settings')`: `describe`, `replace` and the `settings/document-updated` event). It therefore sees exactly the settings a Settings page can change, which the app calls *volatile* fields. In Plus 0.9.0 those are:

| Entry | Fields |
| --- | --- |
| `modes` | `modes`, `defaultMode` |
| `model-tiers` | `tiers`, `customTiers`, `modelProfiles`, `projectProfiles`, `fallbackChains`, `roleModels`, `maxSubagents`, `ultraAutoDelegate` |
| `cowork-shell` | `tabs`, `maxTabs` |
| `sampling-presets` | `presets`, `categories`, `byMode`, `defaultCategory`, `perModel`, `strategy` |
| `color-schemes` | `scheme`, `custom`, `opaqueMacSidebar` |

Only values you set are shared, not defaults.

By default every Plus entry (package `@local/dsh-*`) is shared. Two are never shared:
- `dsh-sync`, because it holds paths and keys for one Mac;
- this add-on.

The `include` setting adds other entries, for example the app's own `ui-theme`. The `exclude` setting leaves entries out.

**Never in the file:**
- Fields the app's schema marks as secret.
- Any field whose name looks like a key, token, secret, password, passphrase or credential, at any depth.
- The fields in `skipFields`. By default these are the per-conversation choices:
  - `modes.sessionModes`, `sessionWeb` and `sessionResearch`;
  - `model-tiers.activeTiers`, `sessionProfiles` and `modelProfilesMigrated`.

All of these stay on each Mac and are kept as they are when the file is applied.

**Not shared at all:**
- Settings that no Settings page can change. These are written by hand in `cordis.patch.yml`, for example swarm budgets or notify targets.
- Which add-ons are switched on.

## How it syncs

A sync round compares three versions of each field (top-level key) of each entry:
- this Mac's value;
- the file's value;
- the value at the last sync, kept as digests in `<dsh home>/shared-settings/state.json`.

The outcome:
- **Changed on one side only:** that side wins.
- **Changed on both sides:** the file wins, and the warning lists the field.
- **No sync record yet:** the file wins. This is a new Mac joining.

Before a section is replaced, this Mac's values for it are saved in `<dsh home>/shared-settings/backups`, newest 30 kept. Sections for entries this Mac does not have stay in the file untouched.

A round runs:
- 1.5 s after any Settings change;
- 1 s after the folder changes, through a folder watcher (iCloud replaces files by renaming them);
- every `pollSeconds`;
- on `/shared-settings now`.

Rounds never overlap.

**Writing safely:**
- The file is written to a temporary file in the same folder, then renamed into place.
- Just before writing, the file is read again. If it changed since the round began, the round starts over, up to three times, instead of overwriting.
- A file that is not valid JSON, or was written by a newer format, is never overwritten. The round stops and reports it.

**iCloud:**
- If iCloud has only a placeholder (`.settings.json.icloud`), the add-on asks `brctl download` for the file and waits.
- iCloud conflict copies such as `settings 2.json` are reported. They are not used.

## Configuration

```yaml
- id: shared-settings
  config:
    folder: ''            # absolute path or ~/...; '' = the folder the installer recorded, or off
    include: []           # extra entry ids to share (e.g. ui-theme)
    exclude: []           # entry ids never to share
    skipFields: [...]     # '<entry id>.<field>'; default: the per-conversation fields above
    pollSeconds: 30
    commandName: shared-settings
```

The folder is chosen in one of two ways:
- `Install.command` asks, and uses `iCloud Drive/DeepSeek Harness Plus`.
- `bash scripts/install.sh --settings "<folder>"` uses the folder you name.

Either way, the installer writes it to `<dsh home>/shared-settings/folder.txt`. `--no-settings` removes that file and leaves the shared file alone. A `folder` setting overrides the file. A `folder` that is not absolute switches the add-on off and logs a warning; it does not fall back to the file.

## Use

- `/shared-settings` shows the file, the last round's result, what is shared, and any problem or conflict.
- `/shared-settings now` runs a round straight away.

## Verified

- 13 unit tests, with a stand-in for the app's settings service and two simulated Macs on one folder. They cover:
  - the first Mac writing the file;
  - a second Mac adopting it, keeping its secrets and per-conversation fields, with a backup;
  - edits both ways, including a reset to default;
  - a quiet round that changes nothing;
  - simultaneous edits to different fields and to the same field;
  - a hand edit of the file;
  - a broken file and a newer-format file;
  - a missing folder and an iCloud placeholder;
  - a write racing another Mac;
  - conflict copies;
  - an entry the app refuses;
  - folders with spaces;
  - secret scrubbing.
- In the app's web version, in a throwaway setup:
  - the first round wrote the five sections, with no secrets and no per-conversation fields;
  - a hand edit of `defaultMode` in the file reached the profile within seconds, with a backup, and the per-conversation fields were left alone;
  - choosing the Forest colour scheme in Settings reached the file within seconds;
  - `/shared-settings` answered.

## Not verified

- Two real Macs through real iCloud Drive. The lab used a local folder. iCloud's own timing, placeholders and conflict copies were simulated in the unit tests only.
- The `brctl download` request.

# DeepSeek Harness Plus

Extra features for the **DeepSeek Harness** desktop app on the Mac: a MindsHub-style sidebar with Chat, Cowork and Code tabs, colour schemes (including MindsHub's navy and teal), work modes, model tiers, a blind model arena, agent swarms, deep research, a usage counter, benchmarks, syncing between Macs and more. Twenty-six add-ons in all, listed in [docs/ADD-ONS.md](docs/ADD-ONS.md).

The add-ons plug into the normal app. Nothing in the app itself is changed, so app updates do not wipe them, and you can remove them at any time.

You do not need to know how to code to install or use this.

---

## What you need

- A Mac with the **DeepSeek Harness** app in your Applications folder, version **0.2.2 or newer, below 0.3**.

1. Download the newest **`DS-Harness-Plus-<version>.dmg`** from the [Releases page](https://github.com/BLCKHWK60/DS-Harness-Plus/releases/latest) and double-click it. A window opens with everything in it: all the add-ons, the installer and this guide. (If you use git, clone the project instead; it is the same folder.)
2. In that window, double-click **`Install.command`**.
   - The first time, macOS may say it "cannot be opened because it is from an unidentified developer". If it does, **right-click** the file, choose **Open**, then **Open** again. You only do this once.
3. A Terminal window opens and walks you through it. If the app is open, it asks to quit it. When it says **Done**, open DeepSeek Harness.

Installing copies the add-ons into the app's own data folder (`~/.dsh/addons`), so you can eject the disk image and delete the download afterwards. To remove the add-ons later, open the disk image again and double-click **`Uninstall.command`**.

Before it changes anything, the installer saves your current setup under `~/.dsh/backups/deepseek-harness-plus/`. If any step fails, it puts everything back by itself.

**Terminal instead:** if you prefer, run this from the unpacked folder:

```bash

```

## First steps

1. **Add your models.** Go to **Settings → Models** in the app. You can paste an API key for a provider there, or add your own server (for example a model server on another computer). No files to edit.
2. **Look at the new pages.** **Settings** now has **Colours, Model Tiers, Modes, Sampling, Usage, Benchmark, Arena** and **Swarm** pages. The chat box (where you type) gets one **model button** beside the send button, with the model list, an effort slider from Off to Ultra Code, tiers and sampling, and, once set up, a model-health dot.
3. **Switch on what you want.** Some add-ons work right away. The others do nothing until you give them a little setup, for example which models the arena should compare. [docs/ADD-ONS.md](docs/ADD-ONS.md) says which is which and how to set each one up.

### What works the moment you install

- **Cowork sidebar:** Chat, Cowork and Code tabs at the top of the left sidebar. Each tab lists only its own conversations and projects, and has its own sections: Model Arena under Chat, and Automation tasks, Connectors (your MCP servers, with on/off switches) and Skills under Cowork and Code. The start page gets a greeting and suggestion chips. A tab picks the mode of new conversations, so the chat box no longer needs a mode drop-down. To get the normal sidebar back, switch **Cowork sidebar** off on the **Plugins** page.
- **Colours:** pick a colour scheme in **Settings → Colours**: DeepSeek Harness (the stock colours, the default), MindsHub Cowork, Graphite or Forest, each in light and dark.
- **Modes:** Chat, Cowork and Code modes, switchable per conversation, plus **Search** and **Deep research** buttons in the chat box.
- **Model Tiers:** one model button in the chat box: pick any model and drag the effort slider. Five starter tiers (Fast, Balanced, Deep, Creative, Code review) work at once on whatever model you use. No model is preconfigured.
- **Code map:** a compact map of the project a conversation works in, so the assistant looks things up instead of reading whole files. Plus four "reverse engineer" skills. Nothing to install.
- **Privacy:** switches off the app's usage reporting and the upload of a conversation when you rate an answer. `/privacy` shows the state.
- **Usage counter:** counts requests and tokens per day and model (never your text).
- **Deep research** and **Code power:** new tools and skills the assistant can use.

Everything else stays switched off until you set it up.

## Changing an add-on's settings

Some add-ons have their own page in **Settings** (Tiers, Modes, Sampling). The rest are set up in the app's settings file. To edit it:

1. Quit DeepSeek Harness.
2. In Finder press **⌘ Shift G**, paste `~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/` and press Return.
3. Make a copy of **`cordis.patch.yml`** first, as your own backup. Then open the original with TextEdit.
4. Paste in the block for the add-on you want, from its section in [docs/ADD-ONS.md](docs/ADD-ONS.md). Fill in the parts in `<ANGLE BRACKETS>`, save, and open the app.

Download the newer version and double-click **`Install.command`** again. It replaces the add-ons and keeps your settings.

Double-click **`Uninstall.command`**. It removes all twenty-two add-ons and their files. Your conversations and your models are not touched. Any settings you wrote for the add-ons stay in the settings file and do nothing; if you install again, they come back into effect.

## Giving it to someone else

Send them the link to this project, https://github.com/BLCKHWK60/DS-Harness-Plus. They follow **Install** above. Nothing in here contains your addresses, keys or personal settings; every add-on starts empty.

# dsh-handoff-relay

A dependency-free plugin that watches one or more directories and sends exactly
one notification to each directory's target session when a file in it is
considered finished.

Each entry in `watches` starts its own `fs.watch` and keeps its own
`(size, mtimeMs)` snapshot and marker state, so targets never interfere with
one another.

The name **relay** reflects what the plugin actually does: point-to-point
forwarding of a ready signal to a target session. It deliberately avoids any
wording that suggests builds or commands — a `trigger`-style name would imply
the plugin can start actions, which it cannot.

## What "finished" means

- **Quiet period**: a file that has stopped changing for `stableMs`
  milliseconds (default `5000`) counts as finished. While the file keeps
  being written to, its timer restarts and nothing is sent.
- **Completion rule (per watch)**: each watch may define a `done` rule. When the
  rule matches the last 4 KB of the file, the file is delivered immediately,
  without waiting for the quiet period. If it does not match, the file is still
  delivered once `stableMs` elapses — a `done` hit only accelerates delivery; it
  is never required.

`done` has four states, distinguished by the key/value alone:

| `done` value | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| omitted | default text rule `{ text: '<!-- DONE -->' }` |
| `{ text: '...' }` | deliver early when the text appears in the last 4 KB |
| `{ regex: '...' }` | deliver early when the pattern matches the last 4 KB |
| `null` | completion rule off; deliver only after `stableMs` |

Regex rules are compiled with the `m` flag and only ever see the last 4 KB.
Patterns are capped at 200 characters, and patterns with nested quantifiers
(such as `(a+)+`) are rejected. A pattern that is too long, uses nested
quantifiers, or fails to compile disables the rule **for that watch only** — a
warning naming the watch's `dir` is logged, that watch then delivers on
`stableMs` alone, and other watches are unaffected.

The stability check is exact: on every filesystem event the plugin records
`(size, mtimeMs)` and resets a `stableMs` silence timer. When the timer fires
it stats the file once more and delivers only if **both** values are unchanged.
If either changed, it restarts the timer — no delivery, no queue.

Each file is delivered at most once for the same content snapshot; repeated
filesystem events do not produce duplicate notifications.

## Who gets notified

The session whose id is given by `targetSessionId` receives one user message
containing the file name and the reason (`stable` or `DONE`). If that session
is not loaded, a warning is written and nothing is sent.

## Install

`dsh-handoff-relay` is a plugin bundle for a DSH profile (the host that loads
cordis-based bundles). It has no runtime dependencies, so installing it is just
linking a local directory into a profile.

1. Put this repository in a local directory, for example
   `/srv/dsh-handoff-relay` on macOS/Linux or `C:/plugins/dsh-handoff-relay`
   on Windows (clone it, or copy the checkout there).
2. In the profile directory, add a `file:` dependency pointing at that
   directory in `package.json`, and register the package name in
   `dsh.profile.bundles`. Keep the other entries already present in both
   lists — only add these two:

   ```json
   {
     "dependencies": {
       "dsh-handoff-relay": "file:/srv/dsh-handoff-relay"
     },
     "dsh": {
       "profile": {
         "bundles": ["dsh-handoff-relay"]
       }
     }
   }
   ```

   The `file:` value must be an absolute path to the directory containing this
   package's `package.json`. Use forward slashes on every platform: on Windows
   that means a drive-letter path such as `file:C:/plugins/dsh-handoff-relay`;
   on macOS/Linux a POSIX path such as `file:/srv/dsh-handoff-relay`.
3. Run `pnpm install` in the profile directory (or the equivalent install
   command of your package manager) so the local package is linked into the
   profile's `node_modules`. Re-run it after changing the package's source.
4. Add a row with the same `id` to the profile's `cordis.patch.yml` and set the
   config there. The bundle ships its own patch layer (`dsh.bundle.patch` in
   `package.json`) that inserts the plugin row; the profile patch layer
   overrides that row's config by matching its `id`:

   ```yaml
   - id: dsh-handoff-relay
     name: dsh-handoff-relay
     config:
       watches:
         - dir: '/absolute/path/to/first-outbox'
           targetSessionId: 'session-xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx'
           done: { text: '<!-- DONE -->' }
         - dir: '/absolute/path/to/second-outbox'
           targetSessionId: 'session-yyyyyyyy-yyyy-yyyy-yyyy-yyyyyyyyyyyy'
           done: { regex: '^## 章末' }
         - dir: '/absolute/path/to/third-outbox'
           targetSessionId: 'session-zzzzzzzz-zzzz-zzzz-zzzz-zzzzzzzzzzzz'
           done: null
       stableMs: 5000
   ```

5. Restart the host so the new bundle and its config are loaded.

### Config fields

- `watches` — a non-empty array of watch entries; each entry needs `dir` and
  `targetSessionId`. Each `dir` must be an existing absolute directory. An
  entry missing either field, or whose directory cannot be read, is skipped
  with a warning naming the entry; the remaining watches still start. The
  plugin only reacts to filesystem events; it never polls.
- `stableMs` — silence window in milliseconds, shared by all watches (default
  `5000`). A file counts as finished once `(size, mtimeMs)` has been unchanged
  for this long. Per-entry overrides are not supported.
- `watches[].done` — per-watch completion rule, one of four states:
  - omitted → default text rule `{ text: '<!-- DONE -->' }`;
  - `{ text: '...' }` → text match in the last 4 KB;
  - `{ regex: '...' }` → regex match in the last 4 KB (`m` flag, ≤ 200 chars,
    nested quantifiers rejected; an invalid pattern disables the rule for this
    watch only and logs a warning);
  - `null` → completion rule off, deliver only after `stableMs`.

  `done` is the only completion setting.

At load time each watch's `targetSessionId` is validated: if a session title can
be resolved, the watch starts normally; otherwise a warning naming that watch's
`dir` is logged and the watch still starts, so the remaining watches keep
working.

**`targetSessionId` must point to a session that currently exists. Session ids
change when the host restarts, so re-wire `targetSessionId` after every
restart.**

## Config

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `watches` | Non-empty array of watch entries. Required. |
| `watches[].dir` | Absolute path of the directory to watch. Required. |
| `watches[].targetSessionId` | Id of the session to notify. Required. |
| `stableMs` | Silence window in ms, shared by all watches. Default `5000`. |
| `message` | Optional template; supports `{file}`, `{reason}`, `{size}`, `{mtimeMs}`. |
| `watches[].done` | Per-watch completion rule: omitted = default text, `{ text }`, `{ regex }`, or `null` (off). |

## Test

```
node index.test.mjs
```

Uses real temporary directories and the real silence window; expects every
case to report `PASS` and the summary to end with `RESULT: PASS`.

## License

MIT — see [LICENSE](LICENSE).

# 贴纸相册：聊天页插件弹层示例 [English](README.en.md) 一个放在聊天页「插件」弹层和「全部功能」里的贴纸面板，演示视图 v2 的四样东西：图集（`gallery`）、空状态（`emptyState`）、环形进度（`progress.shape: "ring"`）和趋势线（`metric.trend`），整块跟随用户在 App 里选的主题色（`accent: "app"`）。贴纸是包里自带的四张小图（`assets/stickers/`），不联网。 ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add /绝对路径/dsh-go-example-album ``` 需要主机提供 `dsh-go-bridge`。装好后打开任一对话，输入框上方胶囊行最后多一枚「插件」，点开就是这个面板；「全部功能」里也有一份。 - 点一张贴纸：它的名字放进输入框，不发送。长按任一张：App 的看图页，左右滑看这一组，保存和分享是 App 的动作。 - 「清空」之后是空状态，按钮「放回」把示例贴纸放回来。 - 老 App 不认图集和空状态：用 SDK 的 `adaptView` 能换成图片和提示条（见测试）。 `lib/view.js` 只产生有界 JSON，`lib/index.js` 注册面板并处理三个动作。在仓库内验证： ```sh node --test examples/plugins/dsh-go-example-album/test/*.test.js node sdk/plugin-kit/bin/check.mjs examples/plugins/dsh-go-example-album --load ``` 诊断里的颜色校正是正常提示。组件的写法见[组件目录](../../../docs/plugins/components.md)，弹层见[网页面板](../../../docs/plugins/web-panels.md)。

简体中文 · English

DeepSeek Harness 的 Android 客户端。手机上直接跑，也能遥控你电脑上的 DSH。


Trendshift 全语言日榜 #1 · 2026-10-30


Deepy 和鲸娘，陪你干活

干活时敲代码，做完来个空翻，等你确认会举手。打开「App 外显示」，它们还会跟你到桌面。


下载 DSH Go

从 GitHub Releases 或官网下载页获取最新版 APK，常见手机选 arm64 包。

 

感谢大家对 DSH Go 的支持和喜爱，我将尽快适配 iOS 和鸿蒙！大家 Star 点得越多，我适配得越快哦 hhh

第一次用可以先看使用指南，遇到问题欢迎来论坛和 QQ 群。
手机上装过签名不同的早期测试包时不能直接覆盖安装，需要先卸载旧版；卸载会清空对话、Linux 环境和设置。


本机运行，也能遥控电脑

内置 Linux 环境，免 Root、免 Termux。电脑上的 DSH，也能一键切过去接着用。


插话、打断，过程自动收好

回复中途也能插话，排队的消息随时「立即发送」。做完的过程折叠成一行。


原生界面，也有网页版

和官方网页版一键切换，停在同一段对话，下次打开还是你上次用的那个。


分享卡、对话回放和链接

回复一键做成分享卡。整段对话生成链接，对方在浏览器里回放，链接端到端加密。


横屏与平板

横屏手机和平板重新排版：侧栏常驻，内容居中，弹出键盘也不挤。


主题配色与桌面图标

六套主题色，也能跟随壁纸或自选颜色。四款桌面图标，三种功能图标风格。


中文，也说 English

全部界面支持英文，在设置里切换，默认跟随系统。


手机操控

看屏幕、帮你点，三档确认随你选。敏感操作默认交还给你；放宽应用规则或解除限制前，请先了解风险。


## 可以做什么 DSH Go 提供聊天界面、本机运行环境和远程连接，是基于 [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) 的第三方项目。运行在手机上的是 DSH 引擎；模型请求仍由你配置的模型提供方处理。 - **本机运行**：在 App 内安装 Ubuntu、Node.js 与 DSH 运行环境，无需 Root 或另装 Termux。 - **远程连接**：通过 SSH 或李国宝老师开发的 [DSHarness Remote](https://github.com/liguobao/ds-harness-remote) 使用电脑、服务器上的 DSH。 - **聊天与工具**：切换模型，发送图片、使用语音输入，处理工具审批和提问；支持聊天界面与网页模式。 - **插件界面**：使用适配 DSH Go 的原生工具卡、表单和面板；仓库提供 SDK、教程和示例。 - **手机操控**：在你开启权限后，让本机引擎读取屏幕、点按和输入，并可随时停止。 - **分享与外观**：分享、导出和回放对话，调整主题、图标和桌宠。 功能随主机和连接方式不同。DSHarness Remote 当前只支持图片附件，不能在 App 内打开网页版，插件管理限于开关，且不支持 DS Bot 和对话日志导出。详见[本机引擎与远程主机](docs/guide/zh/03-engine-hosts.md)。 ## 安装 安装要求为 Android 8.0（API 26）及以上。Release 页面上的 **arm64** 安装包适用于常见的 64 位 Android 手机；x86_64 设备和模拟器用的 x64 包在发布说明末尾的「其他版本下载」里。仓库没有 32 位 ARM 构建。 1. 从 [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/ccch1mneyyy/dsh-go/releases/latest) 或[官网下载页](https://go.dshtui.com/download)下载对应架构的 APK，并按系统提示允许该安装来源。 2. 首次启动时，选择在本机安装运行环境，或连接远程主机。 3. 为所选主机配置模型和所需凭据，再开始对话；部分远程渠道需要在主机侧配置。 仅连接远程主机时，不必在手机上安装本机运行环境。手机操控只对正常模式下的本机引擎开放，需要按界面说明开启无障碍等权限；不打扰模式另外要求 Android 14 及以上，以及 Shizuku 或自连 ADB。首次使用可按[使用指南](docs/guide/README.md)逐项配置。 本地引擎默认使用 PRoot 兼容启动。开发者选项中的直接启动默认关闭，开启后的兼容性和回退方式见[常见问题](docs/guide/zh/11-faq.md)。当前 Android 构建以 APK 侧载为目标，不是 Google Play 发布配置。 ## 数据与权限 模型请求会发送给你配置的提供方。开启手机操控后，任务需要的屏幕文字可能发送给模型，支持看图的模型也可能收到截图；请先阅读 App 的权限说明。 “发送匿名使用统计”默认开启，可在首次引导或“设置 → 隐私与分享”关闭。采集范围和关闭后的处理见[常见问题](docs/guide/zh/11-faq.md)。分享内容前，请检查预览；收到链接或文件的人可以保存其中的内容。 ## 风险提示与免责声明 DSH Go 是社区开发的非官方项目，与 DeepSeek 无关联，也不代表 DeepSeek。使用前请了解： - **AI 并非万无一失**：回答、代码和操作可能出错，也可能被网页、消息或文件中的恶意指令误导。请核验重要结果；医疗、法律、投资等高风险决策不应仅依赖 AI 输出。 - **工具会产生真实影响**：本机或远程主机上的命令、文件修改及手机操控可能导致数据丢失、隐私泄露、账号、资金或设备损失。免确认、放宽应用规则或解除限制会减少保护；确认与拦截机制不能保证消除所有风险。建议保留默认保护，只授予必要权限，不在存有支付或银行信息的设备上解除限制。详见[手机操控指南](docs/guide/zh/04-phone-control.md)。 - **第三方服务与费用**：模型、远程主机和插件等按各自条款运行；相关数据处理、服务可用性和费用取决于你选择的服务与配置。本机运行不等于模型离线，也不代表数据不会离开设备。 - **使用前做好防护**：备份重要数据，只连接可信主机、安装可信插件，留意模型用量与费用；不要让 AI 无人值守地处理不可逆或高风险任务。 - **无担保与责任范围**：在适用法律允许的范围内，本软件按“现状”提供，不保证准确性、持续可用性或满足特定用途；相关无担保及责任限制见 [LICENSE](LICENSE) 第 15–17 条。本声明不排除或限制依法不得排除或限制的责任，也不减损你依法享有的权利。 ## 常见问题
和 DeepSeek 官方是什么关系？
没有关系。DSH Go 是社区开发的非官方客户端，基于开源的 [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) 构建。手机上运行的是 DSH 本身；模型请求发给你配置的模型提供方，需要联网，按你在提供方的账户计费。
安全吗？
本机网页版只接受 App 自己的访问。分享链接端到端加密，密钥只在链接里，服务器看不到内容，但获得完整链接的人可以读取并保存内容。手机操控默认保留敏感操作保护；放宽应用规则或开启「解除限制」会减少这些保护。安全机制不能保证零风险，详见[风险提示与免责声明](#风险提示与免责声明)和[手机操控指南](docs/guide/zh/04-phone-control.md)。
切到后台会被杀吗？
部分系统的省电策略会拦住后台。DSH Go 发现后会提醒你，并直达对应的放行设置，vivo、小米、华为、荣耀、OPPO 都有。
对手机有什么要求？
Android 8 及以上。手机直接下载 Release 页面上的安装包即可，模拟器用的 x86_64 版在发布说明末尾的「其他版本下载」里。在手机上运行 DSH 要先准备内置的运行环境，请预留约 1 GB 空间；只连电脑或服务器上的 DSH 可以不装。
开源吗？
开源，代码就在这个仓库，以 [AGPL-3.0](LICENSE) 发布，`sdk/` 和 `examples/` 为 MIT。DSH Go 的名称和标识，以及 Deepy、鲸娘两位吉祥物，不在开源授权范围内，见 [ASSETS.md](ASSETS.md)。再发布和 fork 时的署名要求见[授权范围与再发布](#授权范围与再发布)。
## 从源码构建 以下流程面向 **Linux x86_64**。当前工具链脚本默认安装 JDK 17、Flutter 3.47.7 和 Android SDK/NDK；App 要求 Dart `^3.13.5`。准备 Bash、Git、curl、tar、unzip、xz、Python 3、zstd（Python 未提供 `compression.zstd` 时用于解包 zstd 压缩的 deb）、file 和常见 GNU 命令；重新解析 Ubuntu 软件包锁时还需要 gpgv。 先取得完整源码和项目资源。`app/pubspec.yaml` 声明的字体、图片等都是构建输入，运行时包由下面的脚本生成。 ```bash git clone https://github.com/ccch1mneyyy/dsh-go.git cd dsh-go bash tooling/setup-toolchain.sh source tooling/env.sh flutter --version java -version bash runtime/build-runtime.sh arm64-v8a DSH_BETA_TOKEN_FILE= bash tooling/build-apk.sh -f arm64 --keep-daemon ``` 工具链脚本会下载 SDK/NDK 与模拟器镜像，并执行 Android SDK 许可接受步骤。默认安装到 `~/dev`；可通过 `DEV_ROOT` 指定独立目录。脚本会复用已有安装，构建前请核对版本。 产物为 `app/build/app/outputs/flutter-apk/app-arm64-release.apk`。运行时构建使用仓库固定的版本与校验信息，并需要联网下载依赖。示例中的 `DSH_BETA_TOKEN_FILE=` 不嵌入维护者的内测通道令牌；`--keep-daemon` 保留 Gradle daemon，适合同时开发其他 Android 项目的环境。 构建 x86_64 包时，先生成对应运行时： ```bash bash runtime/build-runtime.sh x86_64 DSH_BETA_TOKEN_FILE= bash tooling/build-apk.sh -f x64 --keep-daemon ``` 未配置 `app/android/key.properties` 时，本地 release 构建使用 debug 签名。它不能直接覆盖不同签名的官方安装包；请在测试设备上安装，保留已有数据，不要为解决签名冲突直接卸载正在使用的 App。发布签名与密钥文件不要提交到仓库。 只查看 APK 构建命令，可运行： ```bash DSH_BETA_TOKEN_FILE= bash tooling/build-apk.sh --dry-run -f all ``` ## 目录 | 路径 | 内容 | | --- | --- | | `app/` | Flutter 界面与 Android Kotlin 平台实现 | | `packages/dsh_client/` | DSH Web API 的 Dart 客户端 | | `packages/dsh_remote/` | DSH Remote 的 Dart 客户端 | | `runtime/` | Linux 运行时打包、引擎补丁与 App 桥接 | | `sdk/plugin-kit/` | 原生插件作者工具包；在仓库中使用，未发布到 npm | | `examples/plugins/` | 插件示例 | | `docs/guide/`、`docs/plugins/` | 用户指南与插件开发文档 | | `docs/assets/` | 本页用到的展示图、桌宠动图和社群二维码 | | `tooling/` | 工具链、APK 构建与诊断脚本 | | `services/`、`site/`、`infra/` | 配套分享服务、网站和部署材料 | ## 参与贡献 问题反馈和改进建议可提交到 [Issues](https://github.com/ccch1mneyyy/dsh-go/issues)。代码、文档和翻译贡献请先看 [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md)。插件作者可以从[插件教程](docs/plugins/README.md)和 [SDK](sdk/plugin-kit/README.md)开始。 安全问题请按 [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) 报告，避免在公开 Issue 中提交漏洞细节或凭据。 ## 社区 - # 文件摘要 在插件面板点「文件」或「图片」，系统选择器允许最多 4 个文件（单个 8 MiB、合计 16 MiB）。内容经当前主机连接上传；插件在选择回调里读取真实字节，显示文件名、实际字节数与 SHA-256。不会自动发消息、调用模型或保留文件副本。面板的摘要随数据订阅生命周期保留；重新订阅后从空状态开始。 本示例仅依赖 NA v1.3 的 `files`，视图全部使用既有 v1 组件，故 F3 可单独应用。完整第二期样式和表单见同批 F1/F2 示例。旧 App 或无能力的连接显示说明文字，无选择按钮。现阶段 Android 适配器及本地/SSH 直连可协商；DSH Remote 中转不可用。 在带本轮桥的主机安装： ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add /absolute/path/to/dsh-go-example-files ``` 开发验证（仓库根目录）： ```sh node sdk/plugin-kit/bin/check.mjs examples/plugins/dsh-go-example-files node --test examples/plugins/dsh-go-example-files/test/*.test.js node --test runtime/tests/native-files.test.mjs ``` 第三个命令通过真实 HTTP/WebSocket、生产桥路由和本示例 handler 验证读取与摘要，不需要 DSH 引擎。系统选择器 UI 和远程设备仍需本机验证，详见[作者文档](../../../docs/plugins/files.md)。 句柄只在被等待的选择回调内有效；长任务需在回调结束前复制或持久化字节。`file.name` 不是路径，MIME 不是内容校验结果。桥接只读交付不等于隔离宿主 Node 插件的沙箱。

简体中文 · English

DeepSeek Harness 的 Android 客户端。手机上直接跑，也能遥控你电脑上的 DSH。


Trendshift 全语言日榜 #1 · 2026-10-30


Deepy 和鲸娘，陪你干活

干活时敲代码，做完来个空翻，等你确认会举手。打开「App 外显示」，它们还会跟你到桌面。


下载 DSH Go

从 GitHub Releases 或官网下载页获取最新版 APK，常见手机选 arm64 包。

 

感谢大家对 DSH Go 的支持和喜爱，我将尽快适配 iOS 和鸿蒙！大家 Star 点得越多，我适配得越快哦 hhh

第一次用可以先看使用指南，遇到问题欢迎来论坛和 QQ 群。
手机上装过签名不同的早期测试包时不能直接覆盖安装，需要先卸载旧版；卸载会清空对话、Linux 环境和设置。


本机运行，也能遥控电脑

内置 Linux 环境，免 Root、免 Termux。电脑上的 DSH，也能一键切过去接着用。


插话、打断，过程自动收好

回复中途也能插话，排队的消息随时「立即发送」。做完的过程折叠成一行。


原生界面，也有网页版

和官方网页版一键切换，停在同一段对话，下次打开还是你上次用的那个。


分享卡、对话回放和链接

回复一键做成分享卡。整段对话生成链接，对方在浏览器里回放，链接端到端加密。


横屏与平板

横屏手机和平板重新排版：侧栏常驻，内容居中，弹出键盘也不挤。


主题配色与桌面图标

六套主题色，也能跟随壁纸或自选颜色。四款桌面图标，三种功能图标风格。


中文，也说 English

全部界面支持英文，在设置里切换，默认跟随系统。


手机操控

看屏幕、帮你点，三档确认随你选。敏感操作默认交还给你；放宽应用规则或解除限制前，请先了解风险。


## 可以做什么 DSH Go 提供聊天界面、本机运行环境和远程连接，是基于 [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) 的第三方项目。运行在手机上的是 DSH 引擎；模型请求仍由你配置的模型提供方处理。 - **本机运行**：在 App 内安装 Ubuntu、Node.js 与 DSH 运行环境，无需 Root 或另装 Termux。 - **远程连接**：通过 SSH 或李国宝老师开发的 [DSHarness Remote](https://github.com/liguobao/ds-harness-remote) 使用电脑、服务器上的 DSH。 - **聊天与工具**：切换模型，发送图片、使用语音输入，处理工具审批和提问；支持聊天界面与网页模式。 - **插件界面**：使用适配 DSH Go 的原生工具卡、表单和面板；仓库提供 SDK、教程和示例。 - **手机操控**：在你开启权限后，让本机引擎读取屏幕、点按和输入，并可随时停止。 - **分享与外观**：分享、导出和回放对话，调整主题、图标和桌宠。 功能随主机和连接方式不同。DSHarness Remote 当前只支持图片附件，不能在 App 内打开网页版，插件管理限于开关，且不支持 DS Bot 和对话日志导出。详见[本机引擎与远程主机](docs/guide/zh/03-engine-hosts.md)。 ## 安装 安装要求为 Android 8.0（API 26）及以上。Release 页面上的 **arm64** 安装包适用于常见的 64 位 Android 手机；x86_64 设备和模拟器用的 x64 包在发布说明末尾的「其他版本下载」里。仓库没有 32 位 ARM 构建。 1. 从 [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/ccch1mneyyy/dsh-go/releases/latest) 或[官网下载页](https://go.dshtui.com/download)下载对应架构的 APK，并按系统提示允许该安装来源。 2. 首次启动时，选择在本机安装运行环境，或连接远程主机。 3. 为所选主机配置模型和所需凭据，再开始对话；部分远程渠道需要在主机侧配置。 仅连接远程主机时，不必在手机上安装本机运行环境。手机操控只对正常模式下的本机引擎开放，需要按界面说明开启无障碍等权限；不打扰模式另外要求 Android 14 及以上，以及 Shizuku 或自连 ADB。首次使用可按[使用指南](docs/guide/README.md)逐项配置。 本地引擎默认使用 PRoot 兼容启动。开发者选项中的直接启动默认关闭，开启后的兼容性和回退方式见[常见问题](docs/guide/zh/11-faq.md)。当前 Android 构建以 APK 侧载为目标，不是 Google Play 发布配置。 ## 数据与权限 模型请求会发送给你配置的提供方。开启手机操控后，任务需要的屏幕文字可能发送给模型，支持看图的模型也可能收到截图；请先阅读 App 的权限说明。 “发送匿名使用统计”默认开启，可在首次引导或“设置 → 隐私与分享”关闭。采集范围和关闭后的处理见[常见问题](docs/guide/zh/11-faq.md)。分享内容前，请检查预览；收到链接或文件的人可以保存其中的内容。 ## 风险提示与免责声明 DSH Go 是社区开发的非官方项目，与 DeepSeek 无关联，也不代表 DeepSeek。使用前请了解： - **AI 并非万无一失**：回答、代码和操作可能出错，也可能被网页、消息或文件中的恶意指令误导。请核验重要结果；医疗、法律、投资等高风险决策不应仅依赖 AI 输出。 - **工具会产生真实影响**：本机或远程主机上的命令、文件修改及手机操控可能导致数据丢失、隐私泄露、账号、资金或设备损失。免确认、放宽应用规则或解除限制会减少保护；确认与拦截机制不能保证消除所有风险。建议保留默认保护，只授予必要权限，不在存有支付或银行信息的设备上解除限制。详见[手机操控指南](docs/guide/zh/04-phone-control.md)。 - **第三方服务与费用**：模型、远程主机和插件等按各自条款运行；相关数据处理、服务可用性和费用取决于你选择的服务与配置。本机运行不等于模型离线，也不代表数据不会离开设备。 - **使用前做好防护**：备份重要数据，只连接可信主机、安装可信插件，留意模型用量与费用；不要让 AI 无人值守地处理不可逆或高风险任务。 - **无担保与责任范围**：在适用法律允许的范围内，本软件按“现状”提供，不保证准确性、持续可用性或满足特定用途；相关无担保及责任限制见 [LICENSE](LICENSE) 第 15–17 条。本声明不排除或限制依法不得排除或限制的责任，也不减损你依法享有的权利。 ## 常见问题
和 DeepSeek 官方是什么关系？
没有关系。DSH Go 是社区开发的非官方客户端，基于开源的 [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) 构建。手机上运行的是 DSH 本身；模型请求发给你配置的模型提供方，需要联网，按你在提供方的账户计费。
安全吗？
本机网页版只接受 App 自己的访问。分享链接端到端加密，密钥只在链接里，服务器看不到内容，但获得完整链接的人可以读取并保存内容。手机操控默认保留敏感操作保护；放宽应用规则或开启「解除限制」会减少这些保护。安全机制不能保证零风险，详见[风险提示与免责声明](#风险提示与免责声明)和[手机操控指南](docs/guide/zh/04-phone-control.md)。
切到后台会被杀吗？
部分系统的省电策略会拦住后台。DSH Go 发现后会提醒你，并直达对应的放行设置，vivo、小米、华为、荣耀、OPPO 都有。
对手机有什么要求？
Android 8 及以上。手机直接下载 Release 页面上的安装包即可，模拟器用的 x86_64 版在发布说明末尾的「其他版本下载」里。在手机上运行 DSH 要先准备内置的运行环境，请预留约 1 GB 空间；只连电脑或服务器上的 DSH 可以不装。
开源吗？
开源，代码就在这个仓库，以 [AGPL-3.0](LICENSE) 发布，`sdk/` 和 `examples/` 为 MIT。DSH Go 的名称和标识，以及 Deepy、鲸娘两位吉祥物，不在开源授权范围内，见 [ASSETS.md](ASSETS.md)。再发布和 fork 时的署名要求见[授权范围与再发布](#授权范围与再发布)。
## 从源码构建 以下流程面向 **Linux x86_64**。当前工具链脚本默认安装 JDK 17、Flutter 3.47.7 和 Android SDK/NDK；App 要求 Dart `^3.13.5`。准备 Bash、Git、curl、tar、unzip、xz、Python 3、zstd（Python 未提供 `compression.zstd` 时用于解包 zstd 压缩的 deb）、file 和常见 GNU 命令；重新解析 Ubuntu 软件包锁时还需要 gpgv。 先取得完整源码和项目资源。`app/pubspec.yaml` 声明的字体、图片等都是构建输入，运行时包由下面的脚本生成。 ```bash git clone https://github.com/ccch1mneyyy/dsh-go.git cd dsh-go bash tooling/setup-toolchain.sh source tooling/env.sh flutter --version java -version bash runtime/build-runtime.sh arm64-v8a DSH_BETA_TOKEN_FILE= bash tooling/build-apk.sh -f arm64 --keep-daemon ``` 工具链脚本会下载 SDK/NDK 与模拟器镜像，并执行 Android SDK 许可接受步骤。默认安装到 `~/dev`；可通过 `DEV_ROOT` 指定独立目录。脚本会复用已有安装，构建前请核对版本。 产物为 `app/build/app/outputs/flutter-apk/app-arm64-release.apk`。运行时构建使用仓库固定的版本与校验信息，并需要联网下载依赖。示例中的 `DSH_BETA_TOKEN_FILE=` 不嵌入维护者的内测通道令牌；`--keep-daemon` 保留 Gradle daemon，适合同时开发其他 Android 项目的环境。 构建 x86_64 包时，先生成对应运行时： ```bash bash runtime/build-runtime.sh x86_64 DSH_BETA_TOKEN_FILE= bash tooling/build-apk.sh -f x64 --keep-daemon ``` 未配置 `app/android/key.properties` 时，本地 release 构建使用 debug 签名。它不能直接覆盖不同签名的官方安装包；请在测试设备上安装，保留已有数据，不要为解决签名冲突直接卸载正在使用的 App。发布签名与密钥文件不要提交到仓库。 只查看 APK 构建命令，可运行： ```bash DSH_BETA_TOKEN_FILE= bash tooling/build-apk.sh --dry-run -f all ``` ## 目录 | 路径 | 内容 | | --- | --- | | `app/` | Flutter 界面与 Android Kotlin 平台实现 | | `packages/dsh_client/` | DSH Web API 的 Dart 客户端 | | `packages/dsh_remote/` | DSH Remote 的 Dart 客户端 | | `runtime/` | Linux 运行时打包、引擎补丁与 App 桥接 | | `sdk/plugin-kit/` | 原生插件作者工具包；在仓库中使用，未发布到 npm | | `examples/plugins/` | 插件示例 | | `docs/guide/`、`docs/plugins/` | 用户指南与插件开发文档 | | `docs/assets/` | 本页用到的展示图、桌宠动图和社群二维码 | | `tooling/` | 工具链、APK 构建与诊断脚本 | | `services/`、`site/`、`infra/` | 配套分享服务、网站和部署材料 | ## 参与贡献 问题反馈和改进建议可提交到 [Issues](https://github.com/ccch1mneyyy/dsh-go/issues)。代码、文档和翻译贡献请先看 [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md)。插件作者可以从[插件教程](docs/plugins/README.md)和 [SDK](sdk/plugin-kit/README.md)开始。 安全问题请按 [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) 报告，避免在公开 Issue 中提交漏洞细节或凭据。 ## 社区 -
