evidence.readmeExcerpt:
DSH-LLSA

让多个 Agent 一起完成任务，让每一次协作更精简。

DeepSeek Harness 上的本机多智能体工作台
由 LeanLink 连接任务分工、紧凑通信与可追溯记录。

快速开始 · 第一次协作 · 认识 LeanLink · 使用帮助

--- ## 一句话交代任务，一处查看协作 把资料和验收要求交给主 Agent，由它组织子 Agent 分工，再汇总交付。你可以在本机工作台查看任务状态、结果与保存的协作记录。 | 分工更清楚 | 回传更精简 | 过程可核对 | |:---|:---|:---| | 主 Agent 组织任务，子 Agent 执行具体工作 | LeanLink 为受支持的结构化信息选择紧凑表示 | 按需查看已保存的步骤、原文、产物与用量 | 适合从**资料齐全、范围明确、结果可核对**的任务开始：字段提取、规则核验、材料对比，或让多个子任务分别检查同一份输入。 > **当前版本：0.4.2。** 快速开始面向本机单用户使用。工作台与记录保存在本机，推理使用你配置的模型 API；调用费用由使用者承担。 ## 快速开始 准备 **Node.js 24.11+、npm 11+ 和 Git**，然后在终端执行： ```sh git clone https://github.com/TaoruiLiu19/DSH-LLSA.git cd DSH-LLSA npm ci npm run build npm start ``` 没有 Git？使用仓库页面的 **Code → Download ZIP**，解压后进入包含 `package.json` 的目录，从 `npm ci` 开始执行。 安装完成后只需三步： 1. **打开认证链接** — 点击终端输出的 Harness 链接，完成本机认证。 2. **配置模型** — 在 Harness 原生模型设置中填写自己的 DeepSeek 官方 API 配置。 3. **提交任务** — 打开同一地址下的 `/orchestrator/local`；协作记录在 `/collab` 查看。 默认地址为 `127.0.0.1:3095`。先打开认证链接，再进入任务页面。首次安装需要联网，请保留默认安装脚本，不要添加 `--ignore-scripts`。
使用构建包：跳过源码构建 在 [Actions](https://github.com/TaoruiLiu19/DSH-LLSA/actions/workflows/ci.yml) 中打开一次成功运行，下载对应系统的构建产物 ZIP（需要登录 GitHub）。解压后找到 `dsh-llsa-0.4.2.tgz`，按同目录的 `SHA256SUMS` 核对，再解压并进入 `package/`： ```sh npm ci npm start ``` 保留完整目录，特别是 `vendor/` 中的三个组件包。安装仍需要下载运行依赖，真实任务仍需模型 API。旧版 `0.4.0` 包不适用于本页。
### 可选的 CSV 工作流 Task Reuse 可在本机预览、保存并复用 CSV 筛选、去重和统计流程。演示启动命令与示例见 [Task Reuse 使用说明](task-reuse/README.md)。 ## 第一次协作
可选：为真实调用启用金额预算 复制 `examples/money-policy.example.json` 为自己的配置文件，填写 Harness 实际使用的 provider、model、币种及每百万 token 的费率。示例中的名称和费率只是占位，不能直接用来估算账单；每个会用到的模型都需要配置。`cacheWrite` 是否单独计费取决于供应商，按其用量口径填写，不能重复计算。 Windows PowerShell： ```powershell $env:DSH_LLSA_MONEY_POLICY = (Resolve-Path './my-money-policy.json').Path npm start ``` macOS / Linux： ```sh DSH_LLSA_MONEY_POLICY="$PWD/my-money-policy.json" npm start ``` `maxCost` 限制同一 `id` 预算周期内**所有已接入的受管调用**，包含主模型和子模型；`maxRunCost` 限制一个工单执行批次，`maxBranchCost` 限制一个工作项及其重试（根协调调用单独计为 `root` 分支）。主模型跨工单调用仍归主模型会话，不强行分摊到单个工单。周期不会按日期自动重置；修改 `id` 明确开启新周期。 每次调用前按本地输入 token 估计、输出额度和较高的输入费率预留，再乘 `reserveMultiplier`。达到 80% 留下提示事件，预留后将超限则拒绝新调用并暂停该 run。缺少模型价格同样拒绝调用；未知用量持续占用预留，重启和点击继续均不会清空。已有调用可能继续完成，外部操作不会自动回滚。 在 `/collab` 的模型用量区查看周期、工单与分支额度及最近阻止原因。需要续额时，先停止程序，保持 `id` 和币种不变，修改额度后重启，再人工恢复或重试任务。旧调用仍使用当时记录的费率，不被新费率重算。不要把重试当成清空历史。 金额是**用量估算加未结清预留，不是供应商账单硬上限**：本地 tokenizer、输出上限执行情况、供应商计费及未接入的请求都可能造成偏差；实际回传高于预留会计入后续准入。未配置本选项时保留原有 token 限制，预测滑块不控制真实花费。启用前的调用不追溯扣入新预算周期。
打开任务页，粘贴以下内容。这个小例子便于直接核对结果，并观察一次委托与回传。 ```text 请交给一个子 Agent 核对以下资料，再由主 Agent 检查结果。 原始编号是字符串 "007"，必须保留前导零。 测试尚未执行，修复效果尚未验证，当前不允许部署。 只返回一个 JSON 对象： - id：原始编号，字符串。 - test_status：只能是 "passed"、"failed" 或 "not_run"。 - fix_verified：修复是否已验证，布尔值。 - deploy_allowed：是否允许部署，布尔值。 不得补造测试结果，不添加说明或 Markdown 代码围栏。 ``` 勾选 **“最终回复必须为纯 JSON”**，点击 **“提交给 Super-agent”**。检查结果是否符合： ```json { "id": "007", "test_status": "not_run", "fix_verified": false, "deploy_allowed": false } ``` 接着打开 `/collab`，查看本次保存的协作记录。这里的 JSON 是验收标准；任务结束、格式合法和内容正确，需要分别核对。 ## 认识 LeanLink **LeanLink 关注多 Agent 之间的通信成本。** 对受支持的结构化字段采用紧凑表示，自由文本保留原文；需要检查某一步时，回到保存的原文、结构化结果和产物记录。 | 你能得到 | 使用边界 | |---|---| | 主 Agent 调度与子 Agent 分工 | 并非所有小任务都值得多 Agent 协作 | | 紧凑表示与结构化交付 | 不保证任意自然语言都能压缩，也不是保密加密 | | 可查询的步骤与原始记录 | 不提供模型内部隐藏推理的完整回放 | | 原生工单的输入引用与历史版本 | 子任务按引用读取完整资料；追加要求后，旧结果需要重新核对 | | 子任务提交后自动结束该轮 | 保留父 Agent 验收，失败或未完成的结果不能自动算作通过 | | 区分供应商回传、估算和未知的 token 记录 | 未知不等于零；统计不是账单 | | 纯 JSON 输出约束与关键值检查 | 格式校验不能替代事实与业务正确性验证 | 实际节省程度取决于任务、模型、重试和输出长度，应使用相同任务的真实用量对比。本项目不承诺固定 token 降幅或正确率。 **资料很长时怎么用？** 在任务里写清目标、约束和验收标准即可。接入原生工单的 worker 会获得可用的输入引用，无需反复把整段资料抄进委托参数。读取结果带有分页位置，长资料可以继续读取；查询过去的结果时，历史版本仍保留原文。`input:` 引用属于当前工单执行批次，不能复制到另一个任务使用。 ## 使用帮助
启动、认证与 API 常见问题 | 现象 | 处理方式 | |---|---| | Node/npm 版本不匹配 | 运行 `node --version`、`npm --version`；要求 Node ≥ 24.11、npm ≥ 11 | | 依赖安装失败 | 检查网络与 registry，在源码根目录重新执行 `npm ci` | | 3095 端口被占用 | 使用 `npm start -- 3096`，打开新认证链接 | | 页面未认证或拒绝访问 | 先打开当前终端中的 Harness 认证链接 | | Harness 版本不匹配 | 重新执行 `npm ci` 恢复锁定依赖，避免混用旧包 | | 模型调用失败 | 检查 Harness 设置中的 API 地址、模型名称与额度 | 反馈问题时请提供系统、Node/npm 版本和脱敏错误信息。不要上传 API 密钥、认证链接或私人数据库。
数据位置、停止与备份 状态默认保存在启动目录的 `.dsh-llsa/`。按 **Ctrl+C** 并等待进程退出，再复制整个目录进行备份；不要只复制正在使用的 SQLite 文件，WAL/SHM 与关联产物也可能参与持久化。恢复时先停止服务，再恢复完整目录。 在线数据库快照可使用 SQLite `VACUUM INTO 'backup.db'`，但它不能替代关联产物的完整备份。Harness 的模型配置和凭据由 Harness 单独管理。 指定数据位置，Windows PowerShell： ```powershell $env:DSH_LLSA_STATE = "D:\DSH-LLSA-data" npm start ``` macOS / Linux： ```sh DSH_LLSA_STATE="$HOME/dsh-llsa-data" npm start ```
兼容版本与执行边界 | 组件 | 版本 | |---|---| | DSH-LLSA 组合发行 / 启动器 | 0.4.2 | | `@dsh-llsa/collab` | 0.4.2 | | `@dsh-llsa/superagent` | 0.4.2 | | DeepSeek Harness | 0.2.2-rc.1 | 包通过本地构建与随包文件安装，保持 `private: true`；这些名称不是已在 npm 发布的承诺。快速开始会启动指定版本的 Harness，尚不支持对任意已有实例一条 `dsh plugin add` 命令完成全部配置。 默认本机入口不自动操作外部仓库或发布部署。源码保留上游外部集成能力；另行启用时可能使用本机 git、gh、lark 凭据并执行命令。`DSH_SUPERAGENT_BLOCKED_COMMANDS` 是建议性限制，不构成强制沙箱。服务仅供本机使用，不要直接暴露到公网。
## 开发与验证 ### 可视化浮窗接口（只读） 编排层已预留多智能体工作状态投影，不依赖 HUD 包，也不实现浮窗布局或动画。 - 读取现有 `GET /collab/api/runs/:runId?view=hud`，获得符合 [HUD v1 Schema](contracts/hud-v1.schema.json) 的脱敏快照；不新增端点。 - 原有完整任务快照保留兼容字段，新增 `hud`，以及与其一致的顶层 `v`、`seq`、`now`。浮窗应使用 `view=hud`，不要读取原始 `events` 或自行推导状态。 - `agents` 提供稳定 ID、父子关系、工单、五态、状态起始时间、静默标记和最小活动事件。`label` 是最多 12 个 Unicode 字符的短名：任务标题优先，其次会话标题；移除路径、URL、邮箱、纯数字 ID、代码与换行，过滤后为空则使用角色或“智能体”。原生 Assignment 无独立标题字段，适配器取关联任务的 `execution.name` / `ticket.title`；托管子任务使用分配时的 objective。每次 assignment 的短名持久化固定，变更经带 `label` 的 `agent.register` 发布。父节点可能属于另一个工单快照，不能据此猜测其活动状态。 - `seq` 在每个 run 内单调递增，重启不清零；客户端按 `(runId, seq)` 维护游标，跨 run 不可比较。轮询时间与 `stalled` 变化不会增加序号。`stalledAfterMs` 默认为 20000；只有 `running` 可以静默。`stalled` 由服务端计算，客户端只展示服务端值，不自行判断失败或静默。 - 每次快照包含 `aliasVersion: 1`，`tool` 仍是原生工具 ID。按版本读取并缓存 [tool-aliases-v1.json](contracts/tool-aliases-v1.json) 的 `aliases` 映射。初版别名与原生 ID 同名，今后原生 ID 改名时可继续指向稳定别名；表中不提供材料分类。已发布文件不可修改；映射更新新增版本文件并递增 `aliasVersion`，与 HUD 的 `v` 独立。自定义名称或第三方工具可落“其它”；测试覆盖锁定宿主及本项目内置工具声明，新增内置 ID 漏配会失败。 - `events` 是最近 256 条最小事件，`eventsFromSeq` 给出窗口起点。若客户端游标落后于窗口，直接采用最新状态并跳过丢失的动画，不回放猜测事件。事件的 `seq`、`agentId` 用于寻址；`state.changed` 额外提供 `from/to/reason`。 - turn 正常结束的 `done` 只表示本轮结束，不代表工单验收通过。取消或输入作废为 `idle`；进程重启后未闭合 turn 清理为 `idle`。缺失的工具/turn 结束以 `synthetic: true` 和原因显式补齐，绝不冒充成功。工具 id 不含参数、路径、命令或输出。 - 实际状态接入 `turn/start/end`、`tool/call/result`、审批对象与用户问题回复。等待确认不会因工具等待超时自动消失；收到用户回复后按是否有打开的 turn 恢复。历史上尚未接入的活动不补造。 浮窗开发可以直接读取五份回放夹具中的 `frames`： [正常一轮](contracts/fixtures/hud-normal.json)、[输入作废](contracts/fixtures/hud-invalidated.json)、[重启清理](contracts/fixtures/hud-restarted.json)、[审批与提问等待／恢复](contracts/fixtures/hud-attention.json)、[20 秒静默边界](contracts/fixtures/hud-stalled.json)，另有 [短名边界用例](contracts/fixtures/hud-labels.json)。无需导入 manager/store 或投影实现。`steps` 的状态、序号与边界期望独立编写；同一事件序列必须生成相同 `frames`。`node scripts/update-hud-fixtures.mjs` 只刷新 frames，不修改期望值。 待确认由宿主 `userQuestions` 结构化视图、阻塞请求生命周期和 `approval/asked` / `approval/decided` 驱动，HUD 不解析工具返回文本。统一使用既有 `attention.raised`、`attention.resolved`；只有状态实际改变才发 `state.changed`。多个对象须全部处理后才恢复：有打开的 turn 则 running，否则 idle；取消清空集合并回到 idle，迟到的旧对象不会重新点亮。 兼容约定：本次保持 `v: 1`。加字段、kind 或状态属于约定的非破坏性扩展；既有字段语义保持不变。未来破坏性变更必须在同一个 PR 更新 schema、投影、夹具与回放测试；v1 继续默认，v2 由客户端显式选择，两个版本短期并存。只有可视化端明确确认迁移完成后才可弃用 v1。本版尚未发布 v2。独立安装、单智能体降级和视觉材料映射由 HUD 实现方负责。 ```text packages/dsh-collab/ 协作通信与记录 packages/superagent/ 上游派生的执行插件 packages/launcher/ 本机启动器 scripts/ 构建、打包与安装验证 assets/ 产品海报 ``` 在完成 `npm ci` 后运行： ```sh npm run check npm run typecheck npm test npm run pack:release npm run verify:rebuild npm run verify:kit ``` `pack:release` 先检查并构建，再生成四个归档与 `SHA256SUMS`。后两条命令分别检查重复构建一致性，以及全新目录中的安装、认证、页面与协作桥。已构建源码还可运行 `npm run smoke`。 这些验证使用隔离配置，不提交模型任务；真实任务质量需要另行验收。Windows / Ubuntu 各自验证通过后，CI 还会下载两套产物、核对实际归档哈希并比较 SHA256SUMS；文件名或内容不一致会让整个流程失败。远端状态见页首 CI 标记。构建产物通过 Actions 分发，不提交进源码树。 ---

Built on DeepSeek Harness · Connected by LeanLink

基于 [DeepSeek Super-agent prototype](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/dsh-superagent-prototype) 与 [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness)。采用 [MIT](LICENSE)，上游署名与派生说明见 [NOTICE](NOTICE)，版本变化见 [CHANGELOG](CHANGELOG.md)。本项目是独立扩展，不代表 DeepSeek 官方发布或背书。 ### 协作树与费用推演 工作台新增父子 Agent 调用树，展示已记录的任务下发、结果回传和公开消息。点击连接可查看历史，并按连接调整压缩情景、费率、缓存命中及额外开销。已有阶段实验与情景预测分开展示。 滑块只做预测，不修改实际压缩策略；默认费率是示例。未知用量不补零，减少 token 也可能增加费用。当前不保证任意任务的固定降幅，后续完整验证尚未完成。 模型用量区可查看调用归属与返工统计，按 Agent、工作项、尝试和用途分组。用量覆盖率仅针对已记录的受管调用；缺少回传的请求仍计入未知。缓存命中率只在分项完整的调用上计算。输入变更造成的作废与实际重试分开统计，不能相加当作模型错误；未回传的费用不会被显示成免费。

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# DSH 工作区资源管理器

在 DeepSeek Harness 里和 AI 聊到一半，需要找本机资料、确认文件内容，或把文件交给当前会话时，可以直接在右侧栏完成。安装后，从右侧栏的「+」选择「电脑文件资源管理器」。插件适用于 Windows 桌面端，按当前 Windows 账户权限访问文件。

## 安装

### 从 npm 安装（推荐）

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-workspace-explorer
```

也可以在 Harness 的「插件 → 添加插件」里直接输入包名 `dsh-workspace-explorer`，让它自己解析注册表。

安装后从系统托盘完全退出 Harness，再从右侧栏的「+」打开「电脑文件资源管理器」。

### 从 GitHub Release 安装

在 Harness 的「插件 → 添加插件」中粘贴下方安装包链接，也可粘贴已下载的本地 `.tgz` 路径：

```text
https://github.com/tm5452/dsh-workspace-explorer/releases/download/v1.1.3/dsh-workspace-explorer-1.1.3.tgz
```

从本地测试包或目录链接安装的用户，可先在插件列表移除旧条目，再安装正式版。发布变更见 [版本记录](CHANGELOG.md)。

### 从源码安装

将插件目录以 `link:<绝对路径>` 添加。旧的同名插件记录可先从插件列表移除。

「电脑文件资源管理器」卡片主体打开会话工作区，右侧电脑按钮直达「此电脑」。它与 DSH 自带的「文件」入口独立，也可与 Better Sidebar 一起使用。

## 界面实拍

**大图标视图、收藏夹和视频预览**

![大图标视图中的图片和视频缩略图、收藏夹菜单和下方视频预览](docs/screenshots/grid-favorites.png)

**工作区搜索**

工作区模式会在结果中显示文件所在的子目录。

![工作区模式按文件名搜索并显示结果所在的子目录](docs/screenshots/workspace-search.png)

**多标签页浏览与管理**

在顶部标签栏打开和切换多个文件夹，可拖动标签调整顺序。每个标签页各自保留目录、导航历史和预览。

![顶部同时打开三个文件夹标签，当前显示项目归档的文件列表和文本预览](docs/screenshots/stl-preview.png)

## 找到文件，保留浏览位置

**浏览本机磁盘。** 点首页按钮回到「此电脑」，查看 C、D、E 等可用盘符。双击文件夹进入，页面只显示当前目录下的文件和子文件夹。工具栏可前进、后退、返回上一级和刷新。

**用路径直达。** 点地址栏中的任一级目录即可返回那里。路径太长时，把鼠标放在地址栏上滚动，可左右查看。点右侧的编辑按钮或按 Ctrl+L，可直接粘贴绝对路径。输入文件夹路径会进入该目录，输入文件路径会定位并预览该文件。

**同时打开多个目录。** 点顶部「+」再选「电脑文件资源管理器」，每个标签页各自保留目录、前进后退历史和预览。标签显示当前文件夹名，可拖动排序，放不下时可用滚轮左右查看。同一窗口中的会话共享这组文件浏览标签，切换会话或工作区时会保留当前浏览状态。

**每个目录记住自己的视图。** 底部可切换列表和大图标。列表显示名称、类型和大小。大图标可直接看到图片和可解码视频的缩略图。底部还可切换按修改时间排序，最近修改的项目优先。下次进入同一目录，会沿用上次的视图和排序设置。

**收藏常用目录。** 点地址栏旁的星标收藏当前文件夹。点击收藏项即可直达，也可以上下拖动排序，顺序会自动保存。操作面板外的内容时会自动收起。移除单项或清空只修改收藏记录。

## 确认文件内容，再决定怎么用

**单击预览，双击打开。** 图片、音频和纯文本单击即预览。其他格式先显示封面，点击对应按钮后才加载内容。视频封面会尝试显示首帧。双击文件可用 Windows 默认应用打开。

**控制下方预览窗。** 窗格默认开启，底栏右侧按钮可随时收起或展开。拖动上下窗格之间的细灰线可调整高度。文件名右侧的「×」可单独关闭当前文件预览。切换文件夹时可继续查看上一次选中的文件。

**在侧栏浏览文档并缩放。** PDF 和 Office 文档可上下连续滚动，按住 Ctrl 滚动滚轮可缩放，放大后可按住左键拖动平移。Office 使用 Harness 本机转换服务，Excel 按打印版式显示。图片可直接用滚轮以鼠标位置为中心缩放，按住左键拖动可平移画布。右上角仍可打开 DSH 文档预览。

| 类别 | 支持格式 | 预览内容 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 图片 | PNG、JPG / JPEG、GIF、WebP、BMP、ICO、AVIF | 显示图片 |
| 视频 | MP4、WebM、M4V、MOV、MKV 等 | 尝试显示首帧，点击播放。取决于 DSH 内置浏览器能否解码 |
| 音频 | MP3、WAV、OGG、OGA、M4A、AAC、FLAC、Opus | 播放音频，同样取决于解码支持 |
| 纯文本与代码 | TXT、MD、JSON、CSV、HTML、PY 等 | 默认按 UTF-8 显示，Python 脚本也可按文件头声明的编码预览。最多读取前 2 MB |
| 字幕 | SRT、VTT、ASS、SSA | 查看字幕时间和正文，也可切换到原始文本 |
| 字体 | TTF、OTF、WOFF、WOFF2 | 查看字体样张 |
| 3D 模型 | STL、OBJ、PLY、GLB、glTF | 旋转、缩放、平移模型，可切换线框。glTF 须内嵌模型数据 |
| 压缩包 | ZIP、JAR、WAR、APK、TAR、GZ、TAR.GZ / TGZ | 点击「解压预览」后浏览包内文件，按需查看条目 |
| 配置文件 | TOML | 按表查看配置键、类型和值 |
| 电路设计 | KiCad 原理图 .kicad_sch、PCB .kicad_pcb | 查看图形，支持缩放和平移 |
| 波形与光谱 | VCD、JCAMP-DX（.jdx、.dx） | 查看信号波形或光谱曲线 |
| 固件 | Intel HEX（.hex）、DFU（.dfu） | 查看数据地址、数据段和校验信息 |
| PDF 与 Office | PDF、DOC / DOCX、XLS / XLSX、PPT / PPTX | 点击「查看文档」后连续滚动，支持 Ctrl＋滚轮缩放 |

侧栏需要完整读取的格式，单文件上限为 32 MB。7Z、RAR 等压缩包可双击用 Windows 默认应用打开。

## 在会话与文件之间切换

**打开会话里的文件。** 点击 AI 交付的文件、改动卡片中的具体文件或回复里的本地文件链接，当前文件浏览页会跳到所在目录、选中文件并展开预览。拖到右侧标出的区域后，交付文件和文件链接打开 DSH 文档预览，改动卡片打开该文件的 DSH 差异审阅；按住 Shift 点击改动文件也可直接查看原生红绿对比。

**默认拖入路径。** 从插件或 Windows 资源管理器拖动本机文件、文件夹到输入框，会显示紧凑的文件引用块，提交时携带完整路径。在插件中按住鼠标右键拖动文件，会显示跟随光标的文件图标，松手后添加为附件。右键菜单的「引用路径文本到对话框」插入普通文本，「复制文件到对话框」添加附件。

**拖动文件夹。** 列表里的文件夹和地址栏里的任一级目录都可以拖。拖到对话输入框，会插入该目录的路径引用块。拖到顶部标签栏，会为它新开一个文件浏览页。

**按需切到会话工作区。** 「跳转至工作区」只执行一次跳转。「在工作区内工作」会把启用时的工作区设为该标签页的根目录，并显示搜索栏。输入文件名关键词，可搜索各级子目录。结果会标出所在目录，点击后直接定位到文件并打开预览。关闭模式即可回到之前的普通浏览位置。

## 就地整理文件

**单项和批量操作。** 右键文件或文件夹，可复制、剪切、粘贴、重命名、复制路径、在 Windows 资源管理器中显示或删除。按住 Shift 可选连续区间，按住 Ctrl 可逐项选中或取消。多选后可批量复制、剪切或删除。

**与 Windows 剪贴板配合。** 工具栏的粘贴会把文件放进当前目录，右键某个文件夹则可直接粘贴到该文件夹内。同名粘贴会保留两份，删除需确认后移入 Windows 回收站。

## 权限与限制

本机磁盘访问仅在 Windows 桌面 Host 上启用，按启动 Harness 的 Windows 账户权限访问。粘贴和重命名会修改所选的本机文件或目录，Windows 拒绝访问时会显示提示。盘符首页只列本机磁盘、可移动盘和光驱。内嵌预览最多读取 32 MB，文本预览读取前 2 MB。批量操作每次最多 128 项，工作区搜索结果最多显示 300 条，且不遍历目录联接。

## 构建

从源码安装时，先运行 `npm install` 安装 PDF.js，再运行 `node scripts/build-client.mjs` 生成 `lib/client.js`。发布包已包含构建产物。

扩展预览实现沿用 [dsh-preview-extra](https://github.com/LeiYuXingZhou/dsh-preview-extra)，许可证见 `LICENSE-preview-extra`。

# dsh-vedar — Vedar (Kamchatka travel) MCP server for DeepSeek Harness

[中文](README.zh.md)

**Vedar** (vedarai.ru, Russian name Ведар) is the travel platform of the Kamchatka peninsula, Russia. Its public MCP server gives AI agents live tours and availability from local operators, the safety status of places and routes (volcanoes, earthquakes, weather warnings), weather, stays, gear rental, transfers and trip plans. No auth, rate-limited by IP.

This plugin does one thing: it registers one instance of the official bridge `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client` in your DeepSeek Harness profile, pointed at `https://vedarai.ru/api/mcp`. After install the model calls the tools as `mcp__vedar__<tool>`.

## Install

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add github:tourhabk-ui/dsh-vedar
```

`dsh plugin` forwards to pnpm, so pnpm must be on PATH (`npm i -g pnpm`); without it the command stops with "pnpm was not found".

Restart `dsh web`. The tools appear before the first turn.

No plugin? Put the same row into `~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml` (identical to `cordis.patch.yml` in this repository):

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: mcp-vedar
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client'
      config:
        serverName: vedar
        transport: streamable-http
        url: https://vedarai.ru/api/mcp
```

Or add it by URL in a settings panel (`dsh-mcp-center`, `dsh-mcp-panel`, `dsh-mcp-connector`): type Streamable HTTP, URL `https://vedarai.ru/api/mcp`, auth none.

## Tools (23)

Read: `get_tours`, `get_tour_details`, `get_tour_availability`, `compare_tours`, `get_place_info`, `get_volcano_status`, `safety_status`, `get_guardian_context`, `get_weather`, `search_accommodations`, `search_gear`, `search_transfers`, `search_car_rental`, `make_trip_plan`, `edit_trip_plan`, `get_request_status`, `search`, `fetch`.

Write, five requests confirmed by a human, no online payment: `create_lead`, `create_booking_request`, `create_stay_request`, `request_charter`, `create_car_rental_request`.

Platform data is in Russian; tool arguments work best in Russian or English. Emergency number in Kamchatka: 112.

## Status

DeepSeek Harness is in developer preview and config fields may change. The row in this plugin follows the README of `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client` 0.2.0-rc.2 (checked 2026-10-13). Verified end to end on 2026-10-14 with dsh 0.2.0-rc.2 and pnpm 10.28.0 (headless profile, GitHub Actions runner): the plugin installed with the command above, and DeepSeek answered a Chinese question about brown bears in August by calling 17 Vedar tools, all completed. Please report problems at [tourhabk-ui/pos](https://github.com/tourhabk-ui/pos/issues).

Русский: плагин DeepSeek Harness, который одной командой подключает MCP-сервер Ведара. Исходник живёт в `integrations/dsh-vedar/` репозитория платформы.

More: [vedarai.ru/mcp](https://vedarai.ru/mcp) · [vedarai.ru/zh](https://vedarai.ru/zh) · [llms.txt](https://vedarai.ru/llms.txt) · manifest [/.well-known/mcp.json](https://vedarai.ru/.well-known/mcp.json)

# Vedar（维达尔）— Ведар, туристическая ОС Камчатки

Платформа полного цикла — от поиска маршрута до экстренной помощи в поле.
Ранее известна как **TourHab / KamchatourHub / Volcano OS**.

**[vedarai.ru](https://vedarai.ru)** · Next.js 15 · PostgreSQL · TypeScript strict · PWA · Offline-first · AI

---

## Что это

B2C/B2B платформа: туристы ищут маршруты и бронируют туры, операторы управляют предложениями, гиды ведут группы, партнёры сдают жильё и снаряжение. В основе — **безопасность**: каждое место имеет профиль опасности, реалтайм-статус и привязку к МЧС.

Работает в поле без интернета: офлайн-карты, экстренная страница, инструкции выживания, офлайн-очередь SOS (уходит сам при появлении связи) и QR-эстафета — попутчик сканирует сигнал без сети у обоих, его телефон доставляет SOS из зоны покрытия. Меш-ретрансляция — дополнительный канал, когда у соседа по группе связь осталась. Экстренный ответ не зависит от AI: детерминированный SOS-детектор добавляет телефоны 112/МЧС к ответу любого чата платформы, даже когда AI-конвейер лежит целиком.

## MCP-сервер для ИИ-агентов

У Ведара есть **публичный MCP-сервер** (vedar-mcp): endpoint `https://vedarai.ru/api/mcp`, транспорт Streamable HTTP (JSON-RPC 2.0), авторизация не требуется. 24 инструмента: туры и их реальная занятость, сравнение 2–4 туров фактами из базы, безопасность мест и маршрутов, погода, жильё, трансферы, прокат машин без водителя, план поездки и его правка, заявки с подтверждением человеком — на подбор, на тур и дату, на вахтовку целой машиной, владельцу жилья, прокатчику на машину, заявка на поездку целиком (тур + жильё + машина одним вызовом). Подробнее: [vedarai.ru/mcp](https://vedarai.ru/mcp) · манифест [/.well-known/mcp.json](https://vedarai.ru/.well-known/mcp.json) · [/llms.txt](https://vedarai.ru/llms.txt).

В каталогах: официальный реестр MCP — `ru.vedarai/mcp` (манифест публикации — `server.json`), Smithery — `tourhabk/vedar` (`npx -y smithery mcp add tourhabk/vedar`), Glama — `glama.json`. Идентификаторы — в `lib/mcp/catalogs.ts`; их же отдают манифест, `/llms.txt` и `/mcp`. Карточка сервера по расширению MCP Server Card — [/api/mcp/server-card](https://vedarai.ru/api/mcp/server-card), каталог домена AI Catalog — [/.well-known/ai-catalog.json](https://vedarai.ru/.well-known/ai-catalog.json) (`lib/mcp/server-card.ts`). Тот же агент по A2A: визитки [/.well-known/agent-card.json](https://vedarai.ru/.well-known/agent-card.json) (1.0) и [/.well-known/agent.json](https://vedarai.ru/.well-known/agent.json) (0.3), вход `/api/a2a`; в реестре A2A Registry (a2aregistry.org) — запись `538d68a1-16a1-4e55-af5a-8d672b6f1ac7`, регистрация 12.10 (`lib/a2a/catalogs.ts`). Для агентов без MCP и A2A (GPT Actions, Copilot Studio, OpenAPI-наборы) — описание OpenAPI 3.1 [/openapi.json](https://vedarai.ru/openapi.json) и каталог API по RFC 9727 [/.well-known/api-catalog](https://vedarai.ru/.well-known/api-catalog) (`lib/api/openapi.ts`).

**Vedar — Kamchatka travel (English).** Public MCP server for AI agents: live tours and availability, safety alerts, places, weather, stays, trip plans. Endpoint `https://vedarai.ru/api/mcp`, Streamable HTTP, no auth.

**中文（面向中文 AI 代理与开发者）。** Vedar（维达尔，vedarai.ru，俄文名 Ведар）是俄罗斯堪察加半岛的旅游平台，向 AI 代理开放公共 MCP 服务器：地址 `https://vedarai.ru/api/mcp`，Streamable HTTP（JSON-RPC 2.0），无需认证，20 个工具：本地旅行社的团队游及其真实余位、地点与路线的安全状况（火山、地震、天气预警）、天气、住宿、装备租赁、接送、行程规划。写操作只有四种申请（`create_lead`、`create_booking_request`、`create_stay_request`、`request_charter`），均由人工确认，无在线支付。接口返回的名称与说明为俄文，工具参数以俄文或英文为佳。中文页面另列价格、时长与季节。中文页面 [vedarai.ru/zh](https://vedarai.ru/zh)，机器可读说明 [/llms.txt](https://vedarai.ru/llms.txt)，A2A 代理卡片 [/.well-known/agent-card.json](https://vedarai.ru/.well-known/agent-card.json)，OpenAPI 3.1 [/openapi.json](https://vedarai.ru/openapi.json)。接入：通用 MCP 客户端（Qwen Code、Cherry Studio、ModelScope 等）配置 `{"mcpServers":{"vedar":{"type":"streamable_http","url":"https://vedarai.ru/api/mcp"}}}`；DeepSeek Harness（dsh）在面板 `dsh-mcp-center` 中按 URL 添加（类型 Streamable HTTP，认证 none），或一条命令安装插件 `dsh plugin --profile web add github:tourhabk-ui/dsh-vedar`（源码在 `integrations/dsh-vedar/`，一行 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client` 配置）；没有 MCP 客户端的模型（DeepSeek、Qwen、Kimi、Doubao、GLM 的 OpenAI 兼容 API）可用零依赖 Python 桥接 `integrations/vedar-mcp-bridge/`（`LLM_API_KEY` + `LLM_MODEL` 即可对话）。豆包电脑版、扣子 3.0、Cherry Studio、Qoder CN（原通义灵码）、Step Code（阶跃星辰）、Trae、Qwen Chat 桌面版（通义千问）、Kimi Code（月之暗面）、智谱 GLM API（chat/completions）的接入步骤见 [vedarai.ru/zh](https://vedarai.ru/zh#connect)（据各平台资料整理，未经实际接入验证，界面可能不同）；Trae 一键安装链接（粘贴到浏览器地址栏后回车）：`trae-cn://trae.ai-ide/mcp-import?type=http&name=vedar&config=eyJ1cmwiOiJodHRwczovL3ZlZGFyYWkucnUvYXBpL21jcCJ9`，国际版 `trae://trae.ai-ide/mcp-import?type=http&name=vedar&config=eyJ1cmwiOiJodHRwczovL3ZlZGFyYWkucnUvYXBpL21jcCJ9`。堪察加紧急电话：112。

---

## Стек

| Слой | Технология |
|------|-----------|
| Frontend | Next.js 15 App Router, TypeScript strict, Tailwind CSS |
| База данных | PostgreSQL — прямой SQL, без ORM |
| Аутентификация | JWT, role-based middleware |
| AI | Waterfall: 14 провайдеров — OpenRouter · DeepSeek · Gemini · MiMo · GLM · NVIDIA · Groq · Cerebras · Mistral · xAI · YandexGPT · MiniMax · MuseSpark · Anthropic. Плюс Mistral OCR (паспорта маршрутов) |
| PWA | Service Worker, Web Push (VAPID), Background Sync, IndexedDB |
| Меш | WebRTC P2P (VolcanoMesh) — SOS-ретрансляция между устройствами группы |
| Деплой | Timeweb Cloud — автодеплой при пуше в `main` |
| Боты | Telegram + MAX (Kuzmich) |

---

## Масштаб

**Код** — цифры обновляет `node scripts/update-readme-stats.mjs`; запускает его `post-merge.yml` после каждого мержа (из CI проверка снята 15.08: устаревшая витрина держала выкладку прода):

| Метрика | Значение |
|---------|----------|
| Страниц | 279 |
| API routes | 933 |
| UI компонентов | 300 |
| lib-модулей | 1477 |
| SQL миграций | 875 (последняя `1426`) |
| Юнит-тестов | 27949 в 2387 файлах |
| GitHub Actions | 192 workflow |
<!-- STATS:END -->

<!-- CATALOG:START -->
**Каталог** — перепись `GET /api/cron/catalog-census` на проде, замер 2026-11-12 (обновляется после каждого мержа; «живые» — видимые и не слитые):

| Сущность | Живых |

<sub>places: is_visible = true и merged_into_id IS NULL · kamchatka_routes: is_visible = true и merged_into_id IS NULL · guide_certifications: различных guide_id с is_verified = true и неистёкшим expiry_date</sub>
<!-- CATALOG:END -->

---

## Структура данных

Три сущности — три таблицы:

```
places           — географический факт: вулкан, озеро, источник
kamchatka_routes — маршрут между точками, трек, сложность
operator_tours   — коммерческий продукт: цена, слоты, бронь
```

Безопасность каждого места — `location_safety_profile` + `location_real_time_status`.
Связь маршрут→точки — `route_waypoints`.

---

## Офлайн и безопасность в поле

### SOS-страховщик поверх всех чатов
- `lib/safety/sos-detector.ts` — детерминированный детектор ЧП (8 категорий:
  заблудился, травма, медведь, лёд, лавина, группа не вернулась, замерзание, бедствие)
- При признаках беды к ответу ЛЮБОГО чата (веб, стрим на главной, Telegram/MAX,
  планировщик) добавляются 112, МЧС и совет по ситуации — независимо от модели

### `/emergency.html` — статичная аварийная страница
- 34 КБ (замер 04.09), нулевые зависимости, OLED-тёмная тема, кэшируется при установке PWA
- GPS-координаты → скопировать → назвать оператору 112
- 4 протокола inline: Потерялся · Медведь · Травма · Холодно

### `/sos` — расширенный SOS-экран
- Отправка сигнала с офлайн-очередью (IndexedDB + Background Sync)
- VolcanoMesh: WebRTC P2P ретрансляция SOS через группу
- Спутниковая диктовка — текст для чтения оператору

### `/safety/offline` — инструкции выживания
- Медведь, вулкан, гипотермия, потерялся, сигнализация, вода — precached

### Офлайн-карта
- Тайлы Камчатки зум 7–9 кэшируются при установке (~8 МБ)
- Зум 10+ скачивается по маршруту через `/offline/manage`

---

## AI-агенты

| Группа | Примеры | Расписание |
|--------|---------|-----------|
| **Безопасность** | Safety Ingest, Watchdog, Rescue, SOS Bridge, KVERT ACC | каждые 5 мин – 6 ч |
| **Контент** | Editor, Import Routes, Enrich Routes, Places Enricher | 22:00–23:00 UTC |
| **Разведка** | Scout Digest, Scout Innovator, Intelligence, KB Gap, Industry Intel, Legislation Sync | 07:00–08:00 UTC |
| **Память** | Memory Reflector, Contradiction Scanner (safety) | раз в сутки |
| **Качество** | Kuzmich Eval (faithfulness: фикстура + живые вопросы туристов), метрика заземления, SSR-сторож | еженедельно |
| **Бизнес** | Abandoned Bookings, Payouts, Tour Reminder, Leads | почасово / 06:00 UTC |
| **Боты** | Kuzmich (Telegram, MAX, Web, Widget) | realtime |

**Loop-агенты (работают с репозиторием, loop engineering):**

| Петля | Триггер | Что делает |
|-------|---------|------------|
| CI Sweeper | CI упал | Читает лог, чинит: PR-ветка → фикс-коммит; main → hotfix draft-PR |
| Issue Triage | ежедневно 21:00 UTC | Размечает тикеты; safety/деньги → владельцу, тривиальные → draft-PR за ночь |
| Post-Merge Cleanup | мерж PR | Удаляет смерженные ветки, закрывает issue |
| Weekly Chronicle | только вручную (расписание снято 15.10) | Хроника недели в `.claude/MEMORY.md` — межсессионная память агентов |

Уровень автономии L2: LLM-петли готовят draft-PR, мержит человек. Деньги и safety петли не решают — приносят владельцу с лейблом `needs-owner`.

**Общая память агентов:** каждый агент на старте читает `readAgentBriefing()` — состояние платформы, историю запусков, must-have контекст туризма на Камчатке.

Реестры: [`AGENTS.md`](./AGENTS.md) · [`docs/AGENTS_BOOK.md`](./docs/AGENTS_BOOK.md)

## Хабы

| Хаб | Путь | Роли |
|-----|------|------|
| Туристы | `/hub/tourist/` | tourist |
| Операторы | `/hub/operator/` | operator |

| Агенты | `/hub/agent/` | agent |

---

## Разработка

**Новому разработчику — [`docs/DEVELOPER_GUIDE.md`](./docs/DEVELOPER_GUIDE.md)**: быстрый старт
(миграции с нуля не проигрываются — baseline + хвост), карта репозитория, две дороги туриста по коду,
неочевидные механизмы (офлайн-очередь SOS, три планировщика кронов, маркеры), отладка прода.
Схема базы — [`docs/DB_SCHEMA.md`](./docs/DB_SCHEMA.md), снимается с настоящего PostgreSQL.

```bash
npm install
cp .env.example .env.local
npm run dev
```

```bash
npm run dev           # dev-сервер
npx tsc --noEmit      # type check (0 ошибок)
npx vitest run        # тесты
npm run migrate       # миграции локально
git push origin main  # → Timeweb автодеплой
```

### Ключевые соглашения

- `import { pool } from '@/lib/db-pool'` — только named import
- `FROM operator_bookings` / `FROM operator_tours` — не `bookings`, не `tours`
- SQL — только параметризованный (`$1, $2`), никогда конкатенация
- Все API routes — Zod-валидация входных данных
- Цвета — только CSS custom properties (`var(--accent)`, `var(--ocean)`)
- AI — только через `callAIWaterfall()` / `callAIFast()`
- Критичные факты (безопасность, цены, телефоны, наличие мест) — только из
  инструментов/БД, самоотчетам модели не верить
- `SELECT * FROM kamchatka_routes` — только через `v_kamchatka_routes_api`

Полные правила: [`CLAUDE.md`](./CLAUDE.md)

---

## Деплой

Push в `main` → Timeweb видит пуш → собирает Docker → `start.js` накатывает миграции → поднимает сервер.

Приложение: **Fair Polydeuces** на Timeweb Cloud. Репо: `tourhabk-ui/pos`.

**Docker:** standalone bundle ≤ 50 МБ, `images.unoptimized: true` (убирает sharp ~33 МБ).

---

## Последние изменения (июль 2026)

- **Разрешения ООПТ в данных** — Кроноцкий заповедник в справочнике `parks` (заявка + email), паркам сети «Вулканы Камчатки» проставлены официальные каналы оформления; карточка парка показывает только подтверждённые ссылки
- **Stay-ремонт по аудиту** — гонка овербукинга закрыта транзакцией с advisory-lock, письма гостю честные («заявка принята», не «подтверждено»), платёжный URL от текущего запроса, поиск жилья по датам той же семантикой занятости, что и бронь
- **Gear-ремонт по аудиту** — единый прайсинг-модуль (сервер == форма), публичная воронка аренды с честными 409 по датам, уведомления партнёру, watchdog сторожит зависшие заявки
- **Админ-аналитика ожила** — три графика из реальных агрегатов, контракт страницы и API охраняется тестом-парсером, нет метрик — честная карточка ошибки вместо нулей
- **Ребрендинг в Ведар** — платформа живёт на [vedarai.ru](https://vedarai.ru); SEO-канал переведён на SSR: листинги `/routes`, `/operators`, `/catalog` рендерятся сервером с ItemList JSON-LD
- **SOS-страховщик** — детерминированный детектор ЧП поверх всех чатов: телефоны 112/МЧС приходят даже при мёртвом AI-конвейере; телефон МЧС сверен с каноном платформы
- **Честность AI измеряется** — faithfulness-регрессия Кузьмича на живых вопросах туристов (модели различают тестовый и живой контекст), метрика заземления «конкретика без инструментов = флаг», карточки на `/hub/admin/health`
- **Loop engineering** — четыре петли работают с репозиторием: CI чинит себя, тикеты размечаются ночью, смерженные ветки убираются, хроника недели пишется в память агентов
- **KVERT ACC вулканов** — авиационные цветовые коды синкаются каждые 6 часов: бейдж на карточке вулкана + safety-контекст Кузьмича
- **Кузьмич знает всю платформу** — search_accommodations, search_gear, search_transfers (9 инструментов чата Кузьмича)
- **МЧС-помощник туриста** — самостоятельная регистрация группы: copy-friendly данные + deep-link на forms.mchs.gov.ru

---

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-team-progress

A DeepSeek Harness GUI plugin showing four views of a running agent team, counted from
durable state: who is on what, which defects are tracked, how far the goal has moved,
and what needs a human now. A source it cannot read renders `unavailable` with the
reason instead of a `0`.

The host half (`lib/index.js`) registers one loopback JSON route
`POST /api/team-progress/rpc` on the `webServer` service; the client half
(`lib/client.js`) registers the panel with the slot service and re-reads that route
every 5 seconds while the panel is open.

## The panel

```
STALLED  task task-5   owner beta is inactive        ← 4. act now, FIRST
BLOCKED  task task-6   waiting on task-4

3/6 tasks · 2/3 members                               ← headline
▓▓▓▓▓▓▓░░░▓

MEMBERS   4                                          ← 1. who is on what
  member   status    claimed task    task status
  lead     running   task task-6     pending
  alpha    running   task task-4     in progress
  beta     inactive  task task-5     in progress   STALLED
  gamma    running   no claimed task

DEFECTS   10 fixed · 5 in flight · 4 open (19)       ← 2. tracked defects
  #2   Repo→app mapping is dead code.
  #17  False CRITICAL.
  +2 more open

GOAL      round 7/256 · active · armed               ← 3. goal progress
  Extend dsh-team-progress with the four views
```

```
conversation.view   id "team-progress", order 30   a "Team progress" session tab
POST /api/team-progress/rpc   { method: "state" }  the payload
```

The panel is one `conversation.view` tab, bound to the session it was opened in. The
registration at `mount()` in `lib/client.js` is the authority on what is rendered: it
registers that tab and nothing else.

## What it adds

- **MEMBERS** — one row per member: live status, the shared task it claims, that
  task's status. A member holding nothing renders `no claimed task`.
- **DEFECTS** — counts by status across the configured defect logs, plus the rows
  still open. Recognised: `open` / `in flight` / `fixed` / `closed as superseded`;
  anything else is counted as `other` and displayed as `unclassified`.
- **GOAL** — rounds begun against the cap, the phase, and `armed` / `disarmed`.
- **STALLED / BLOCKED** — the action list, rendered first because a stall is the only
  state that asks for a decision.
- **One RPC route** — `POST /api/team-progress/rpc`, methods `state` and `act`.
- **One optional action surface** — complete / reopen / claim / release / reassign, wake,
  interrupt, spawn, auto-assign, broadcast, member cap, all through the same domain
  methods the model's own tools call. Off by default; see [Security](#security-the-action-surface).

## Requirements

The read path was traced against **DeepSeek Harness 0.2.1-rc.3** (2026-10-24), and the
plugin was last exercised end to end on **0.2.1-rc.5** (2026-11-03): a
`POST /api/team-progress/rpc` with `{"method":"state"}` answered `200` with a live
payload. No minimum version is declared.

- The client half is declared for the `web` platform (`dsh.client.platform`). It is
  browser-plane code, so importing `dsh-team-progress/client` in Node fails with
  `window is not defined` — that is the plane, not a defect.
- Only `webServer` is a hard injection. `agents`, `agentTeams`, `sessionProjections`,
  `goals`, `sessionQuery` and `uiWorkspace` are resolved lazily, so a profile with one
  of those bundles disabled still loads the panel and reports the source.

## Install

A local, unpublished plugin package (`"private": true`): `package.json` declares
`dsh.bundle.patch` (`./cordis.patch.yml`) and the client bundle (`./lib/client.js`,
platform `web`).

`cordis.patch.yml` ships exactly one row and no config:

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: team-progress
      name: 'dsh-team-progress'
```

**That file does not enable the plugin.** It is the bundle's own patch, applied only
once the bundle is enabled somewhere; enabling is a profile change that affects every
session, so it is left to the profile owner.

To enable it, three steps.

**1. Clone, then make the package resolvable to the profile.** A profile resolves
plugin packages from its own `package.json`, so add the checkout as a `link:`
dependency and run the profile's install (the profile directory ships a
`pnpm-workspace.yaml`):

```bash
git clone https://github.com/ucfjoe/dsh-team-progress.git ~/dsh-team-progress

PROFILE=~/.dsh/profiles/desktop          # the profile you run
# in "$PROFILE/package.json":
#   "dependencies": { …, "dsh-team-progress": "link:$HOME/dsh-team-progress" }
cd "$PROFILE" && pnpm install
ls -l node_modules/dsh-team-progress     # expect a symlink to the checkout
```

This step was run from a fresh clone on pnpm 11.22.0 / Node v26.7.0: the symlink
appears, `import('dsh-team-progress')` resolves the host half (`apply`, `inject`,
`name`), and `npm test` passes inside the clone.

**2. Add the row to the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`.**

```yaml
- id: team-progress
  name: 'dsh-team-progress'
  config:
    defectLogs:
      - ~/repos/your-project/docs/defects.md
    allowMutations: false
```

The `- insert:` wrapper shown above is also accepted. `~` is expanded in `defectLogs`
entries and empty entries are ignored.

**3. Reload.** After editing the host half, a file edit is not enough — the module is ESM
inside the app process, so reload the plugin (disable, then enable) to re-import it and
rebuild the client bundle. Recorded in [the development log](docs/DEVLOG.md).

## Configuration

Every key is optional; the defaults below are the ones `lib/index.js` applies.

| key | default | what it does |
|---|---|---|
| `defectLogs` | `[]` | Paths to markdown defect logs, absolute or `~/…`. Empty is the shipped default and makes the defects view report `unavailable: no defect-log paths are configured`. Read from config only, never from the request body. |
| `allowMutations` | `false` | Enables the `act` method. Off means `act` answers `403 TEAM_PROGRESS_ACTIONS_DISABLED`; every view keeps working. |
| `actionPolicy` | `'all'` | Narrows the actions reachable once `allowMutations` is on. `'read-write'` withholds the two that outlive the click — `spawn` (creates an agent) and `member-limit` (rewrites a config file on disk) — answering `403 TEAM_PROGRESS_ACTION_WITHHELD` and reaching no domain method. Every board action still runs. An absent or unrecognised value resolves to `'all'`, so an existing profile is unchanged; the payload's `actions.policy` always names the value in force. |
| `spawnFreshProvider` | `'spawn'` | Provider name passed to `spawnTeammate` for a `fresh`-context spawn. |
| `spawnForkProvider` | `'fork'` | Provider name passed to `spawnTeammate` for a `fork`-context spawn. |
| `aliasFile` | `~/.dsh/team-progress/aliases.json` | JSON store for the panel-owned display alias, one-line purpose and hidden flag per member, keyed `leadId\|memberId`. |
| `homePatchFile` | `~/.dsh/cordis.patch.yml` | The patch layer the `member-limit` action edits, with a timestamped backup written beside it. |

### The defect-log format

The parser reads markdown tables. A table counts when its header row has a `Status`
column and a column matching `Defect` / `Issue` / `Problem` / `Bug`, immediately
followed by the separator row:

```markdown
| # | Defect | Evidence | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | Repo→app mapping is dead code. | investigate.py:319-321 | **open** |
| 17 | False CRITICAL. | run.log | **fixed** #222 — merged |
```

- A status cell resolves to `open`, `in flight` (or `in-flight`), `fixed` or
  `closed as superseded`. The cell is cut at the first `,` `;` `:` `—` `–` `(` `#` or
  ` - `, so a trailing reference (`**fixed #222** — merged`) does not change the
  state; a `**bold**` phrase is read from inside the emphasis.
- **A state outside those four is counted as `other`**, not dropped and not guessed
  at, so a new phrasing shows up as `unclassified` instead of disappearing.
- An escaped `\|` does not split a cell. A blank line does not end a table while the
  next non-blank line is still a data row; a heading, a separator, a new header or
  prose does. Section headings are carried on each row.
- Counts are `fixed` / `inFlight` / `open` / `superseded` / `other` / `total`. Open rows
  are capped at 50 with `openTruncated` carrying the remainder; a file over 4 MiB is
  refused and a table stops at 5000 rows.

## Security: the action surface

`POST /api/team-progress/rpc` is registered **directly on the web server, outside the
app's own auth middleware.** With `allowMutations: true`, any local process — any
script, any tool, any agent on the machine — can drive the team board through this
route: complete, reopen, claim or reassign a shared task, wake an inactive member,
interrupt a running agent, spawn a teammate, broadcast to the whole team.

- The shipped default is **off** (`allowMutations: false`).
- With it off, `act` answers **`403 TEAM_PROGRESS_ACTIONS_DISABLED`** and reaches no
  domain method. The read views, the counts and the read path keep working unchanged.
- Turn it on deliberately, on a single-user machine, and treat the route as a local
  control socket rather than an authenticated API.
- `actionPolicy: 'read-write'` narrows it further without turning it off: `spawn` and
  `member-limit` answer **`403 TEAM_PROGRESS_ACTION_WITHHELD`** while every board action
  keeps working. Those two are the ones that outlive the click — one creates a live
  agent with model budget attached, the other rewrites a config file on disk.
  Withholding is opt-in, so the value an existing profile already means (`'all'`) stays
  the default rather than being re-interpreted under it.

Paths in `defectLogs` come from config only, never from the request, so the route
cannot be turned into an arbitrary-file reader. The body is capped at 64 KiB.

## Payload / RPC contract

Exact path, `no-store`.

Two methods: `state` takes `{ sessionId? }` and answers the snapshot below; `act` takes
`{ leadId, action, … }` and answers a receipt, or a refusal with a domain `code`.

Input handling: non-`POST` → `405`; body over 64 KiB → `413`; invalid JSON, JSON
that is not an object, or a `method` that is missing / empty / not a string → `400`;
a method that is not registered (including `constructor`, `__proto__`, `toString`) →
`404`; `act` while mutations are off → `403` `TEAM_PROGRESS_ACTIONS_DISABLED`.

```jsonc
{
  "ok": true,
  "generatedAt": "2026-10-30T11:02:50.000Z",   // ISO, host clock at read time
  "summary": { "total": 6, "completed": 3, "inProgress": 2, "pendingReady": 0,
               "blocked": 1, "stalled": 1, "members": { "live": 2, "total": 3 } },
  "teams": [ /* one card per lead: label, summary, roster, lanes, goal, lineage */ ],
  "roster": { "state": "ok", "leads": 1, "stalled": 1, "members": [ /* rows */ ] },
  "defects": {
    "state": "ok",                              // ok | partial | unavailable
    "files": [{ "path": "…", "state": "ok", "rows": 19 }],
    "counts": { "fixed": 10, "inFlight": 5, "open": 4, "superseded": 0,
                "other": 0, "total": 19 },
    "open": [ /* rows */ ], "openShown": 1, "openTruncated": 3
  },
  "goal": { "state": "ok", "goals": [ /* roundsStarted, maxGoalRounds, phase */ ] },
  "waitingOnYou": { "state": "ok", "total": 3, "stalled": 1, "unassigned": 2, "idle": 0 },
  "attention": [ { "kind": "stalled", "label": "task-5", "detail": "owner beta is inactive" } ],
  "actions": { "enabled": false, "policy": "all" },
  "degraded": { "any": false, "reasons": [] }
}
```

### The honesty rules

- **`null` is never `0`.** A count that could not be read is `null`, and the view says
  why. `completed + inProgress + pendingReady + blocked === total` holds on every
  readable snapshot.
- **An absent source is not a zero.** Each view carries its own `state` (`ok` /
  `partial` / `none` / `unavailable`) and, when it is not `ok`, the reason. A missing
  defect log is `unavailable` with `counts: null`; one log readable and one missing is
  `partial` with the real counts and the missing file named. `none` ("there is no
  goal") and `unavailable` ("I could not look") are different answers, and render
  differently.
- **Three-valued on purpose.** `stalled` is `true`, `false`, or `null` when the live
  status could not be read; a `null` draws no badge rather than claiming "not stalled".
- **`degraded` is narrow.** It covers the board and team read only, so a missing defect
  file states itself in place without making a readable task board look degraded.
- **Nothing is estimated.** No ETA, no percentage, no elapsed time.

## Tests

Run `npm test`. Both suites pass; they were run here on Node v26.7.0.

- `test/verify.mjs` — renders the real client bundle through a React shim and asserts
  each view, including every absence: attention first in document order, a `STALLED`
  badge only where the status is known, and no invented `0` anywhere.
- `test/verify-host.mjs` — drives the host half against a fixture board and asserts the
  payload, the read path (one `tryMembership` per lead, zero `agents.get()` calls), the
  RPC status codes, and that a request cannot redirect a defect-log path.

## Design notes

- **A member's claimed task beats the description it was spawned with.** The
  description is fixed at spawn and drifts as work moves; the task the member holds is
  the durable answer to "what is it doing".
- **`provisioning` is not a stall.** Building a teammate is a normal startup state.
  Only `inactive` or `failed` while holding in-progress work counts, and an unknown
  status yields `null` rather than `false`.
- **A reader that throws must render `unavailable`, never "no goal".** The goal
  service's `get()` throws for an agent that is not the registry's live instance, so
  every call is wrapped: conflating "could not look" with "there is none" would report
  success on a broken read.
- **A source that cannot be read is not a zero.** A missing file, an unregistered
  service and an unreadable board each say so in their own field, because a fabricated
  `0` reads as a fact.
- **The flag that lets the panel act is off by default.** A read-only panel is safe on
  any profile; a route that can wake agents and move a shared board is an explicit
  owner decision.

## License

MIT — see [LICENSE](LICENSE) and the `license` field in `package.json`.

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-podwave

DeepSeek Harness 的本地播客播放器插件：在 DSH 侧栏里播放硬盘上的播客，自动记住进度，并且能转写、显示双语字幕、导出 SRT / Markdown。

音频只从本地磁盘读取，不上传、不联网、不依赖订阅源。转写与翻译默认跑在本机（Apple Silicon / MLX），也可以切到 DeepSeek API。

![单集详情：封面 + 双语字幕](docs/screenshot-detail.png)

## 功能

- **单集详情**：点任意一集进入详情页——左侧封面与信息，右侧直接显示字幕，转写后可切中英对照。
- **本地播放**：扫描文件夹（递归 6 层，支持 `mp3 / m4a / m4b / aac / wav / flac / ogg / opus / weba / webm / wma`），自动读标题、艺术家、封面。
- **续播**：进度每 4 秒保存，切集 / 暂停 / 关闭时立即保存；重开从上次位置继续。
- **转写**：本地 Qwen3-ASR-1.7B-8bit，带词级时间戳；按停顿与标点切成字幕行。
- **任务面板与批量**：顶部「任务」查看队列、进度，可取消 / 重试；「选择」多选批量转写。
- **长播客分块**：按 15 分钟切块转写，取消或失败后从已完成块续跑；热词可在设置里维护。
- **双语字幕**：点「字幕」打开面板，选「中文对照 / English」，只翻译另一种语言的行；点字幕行可以跳到对应时间。
- **字幕编辑**：行悬停出现 ✎，就地改文本；按光标「拆分」、行尾 ⇣ 合并；右上「撤销」最多回退 20 步；「校验」在导出前检查空行、无效时间戳与时间重叠。
- **导出**：SRT 或 Markdown。
- **快捷键**：`空格` 播放/暂停，`← / →` ±15 秒，`↑ / ↓` 上/下一集，`/` 搜索。
- **收起侧栏**：点侧栏顶部标题右边的 `‹` 收起，左上角 `›` 展开；状态记在 `~/.podwave/ui.json`。面板被 DSH 挤窄时会自动收起侧栏，详情页改为上下布局。
- **设置页**：DSH 设置 → 播客，可以看已完成的转写历史、配置 DeepSeek API、选择转写与翻译模型、控制侧边栏入口是否显示。

## 安装

需要 DeepSeek Harness `>=0.2.1-rc.5`。

从 [Releases](https://github.com/Watchcats211/dsh-podwave/releases) 下载最新的 `dsh-podwave-*.tgz`，然后：

```bash
dsh plugin --profile desktop add file:/path/to/dsh-podwave-0.2.9.tgz
```

也可以直接从源码目录装：

```bash
dsh plugin --profile desktop add file:/path/to/dsh-podwave
```

装完刷新 DSH，侧栏出现「播客」。

## 转写与翻译（可选）

播放器本身不需要额外依赖。要用转写 / 翻译，需要在本机准备 MLX 运行时：

```bash
uv venv ~/.podwave/runtime/.venv --python 3.12
~/.podwave/runtime/.venv/bin/python -m pip install "mlx-qwen3-asr==0.4.4" mlx-lm

hf download mlx-community/Qwen3-ASR-1.7B-8bit --local-dir ~/.podwave/models/qwen3-asr-1.7b-8bit
hf download mlx-community/Qwen3-8B-4bit --local-dir ~/.podwave/models/qwen3-8b-4bit
```

- 转写模型约 2.3 GB，翻译模型约 4.3 GB；只做播放可以都不装。
- 翻译可以不用本地模型：字幕面板 →「设置」→ 选 DeepSeek API，填 API key（默认 `api.deepseek.com` / `deepseek-chat`）。
- 字幕面板 →「设置」里切换引擎；目标语言在字幕面板的「对照」下拉里选。

## 设置

DSH 设置 →「播客」：

- **历史记录**：所有已完成转写的单集（时长、语言、行数、已翻语言、完成时间）。
- **API 与翻译引擎**：DeepSeek API 地址 / 模型 / API Key，或切到本地模型。
- **模型**：在 `~/.podwave/models/` 下已就绪的模型里选转写模型（ASR）与翻译模型。
- **界面**：开关「在主界面侧边栏显示播客入口」，保存后立即生效（不需要刷新）。

## 用法

- **添加文件夹**：点面板左上 `+` → 「选择文件夹…」调用系统目录选择器；也可以直接把音频文件拖进面板（会复制到 `~/.podwave/imports/`）。手动输入路径保留为备选。扫描在后台进行，状态显示在底部。
- **播放 / 续播**：点单集；刷新或重开 DSH 后接着上次位置。
- **转写**：点播放条右侧「转写」，完成后自动打开字幕面板。长播客需要时间（M4 上大约 5–10 倍实时速度）。
- **翻译**：字幕面板右上「对照」选目标语言；已有译文会直接显示，没有就自动开始翻。
- **删除文件夹**：侧栏文件夹右侧 `×`，会移除该目录下的单集记录。

数据保存在 `~/.podwave/`：`state.json`（媒体库/进度）、`config.json`（统一配置）、`jobs.json`（任务记录）、`transcripts/`（字幕 v2）、`covers/`、`models/`、`runtime/`、`imports/`（拖拽导入的音频副本）。数据与配置的详细结构见 [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md)。

## 结构

```
src/host.js                /podwave/api/*：播放器、转写、翻译、字幕导出
src/state.js               状态读写（~/.podwave/state.json，原子写）
src/library.js             媒体库扫描（music-metadata）
src/transcribe.js          MLX Qwen3-ASR 调用、队列、字幕分行与导出
src/translate.js           翻译任务（DeepSeek API / 本地 MLX Qwen3）
src/models.js              模型目录扫描与选择（config.models）
src/config.js              统一配置（~/.podwave/config.json，迁移旧 ui/translate/models.json）
src/jobs.js                任务记录（~/.podwave/jobs.json，重启标 interrupted）
scripts/translate_local.py 本地翻译脚本（mlx_lm）
client/src/                React 面板（App.jsx、SettingsPage.jsx、plugin.jsx、styles.css）
build.mjs                  PostCSS 作用域前缀 + esbuild 打包为 DSH client bundle
cordis.patch.yml           插件加载声明
docs/ARCHITECTURE.md       架构、数据格式、API 表
CHANGELOG.md               版本记录
```

版本变化见 [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md)。

## 开发

```bash
npm install
npm run build          # 产物 dist/client.js

# 独立测试 profile（不影响 desktop）
dsh podwave-test --from-default-profile web --no-open --port 4790
dsh plugin --profile podwave-test add file:$PWD
```

## 限制

- 还没有 RSS / 在线流订阅，只播放本地文件。
- 说话人分离暂未接入（`mlx-qwen3-asr` 的 `--diarize` 依赖 pyannote + HF token）；字幕目前不分说话人。
- 转写是「事后整段」模式，不是真流式；播放中可以先听，转写完成后字幕会出现在面板里。
- 本地翻译是 8B 4bit 模型，长句质量不如 API；重要内容建议用 DeepSeek API 翻。

## 路线图

- [x] 转写：本地 MLX Qwen3-ASR（中英混合），词级时间戳
- [x] 双语字幕：本地 Qwen3-8B / DeepSeek API
- [x] 导出 SRT / Markdown
- [x] 系统文件夹选择器与音频拖拽导入
- [ ] 说话人分离与说话人标签
- [ ] 跟播预转写（边播边出字幕）
- [ ] RSS / 在线播客订阅

## License

MIT

No candidate code or lifecycle hooks were executed; runtime safety and compatibility are unproven.

# dsh-resume

This folder is a frozen snapshot of the files the compatibility sample audits.
Its `engines.dsh` range is the real one from `L3n3L/dsh-resume@0.1.3`:

## Requirements

- DeepSeek Harness `>=0.1.0-rc.6 <0.2.0-0`

```json
"engines": {
  "dsh": ">=0.1.0-rc.6 <0.2.0-0"
}
```

The heading is here on purpose: the sample isolates the host-range verdict, and
the remote audit still checks README requirements. Upstream's localized README
does not use a `## Requirements` heading, so a live audit of the repository can
also add a `readme` failure to the same row.

# dsh-plugin-toolkit

[![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/dsh-plugin-toolkit)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-plugin-toolkit)
[![downloads](https://img.shields.io/npm/dw/dsh-plugin-toolkit)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-plugin-toolkit)
[![CI](https://github.com/WJDdidi-1/dsh-plugin-toolkit/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/WJDdidi-1/dsh-plugin-toolkit/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![license](https://img.shields.io/npm/l/dsh-plugin-toolkit)](LICENSE)


![dsh-plugin-toolkit](docs/card.png)

English · [中文](./README.zh.md)

Everything a [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) plugin needs between `init` and a version the market index accepts: scaffolding, a test harness for the client bundle, a way to see a change without restarting the app, and a release that does not depend on remembering fourteen steps.

```sh
npx dsh-plugin-toolkit@latest init ./my-panel --name my-panel   # a plugin that already passes the checks
npx dsh-plugin-toolkit@latest verify .                          # pack it, install the tarball, mount the panel
npx dsh-plugin-toolkit@latest release --pr --merge              # tag, wait for npm, update the index, open and merge the PR
```

## The panel

![The Plugin doctor tab, on a plugin that fails two checks](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/WJDdidi-1/dsh-plugin-toolkit/main/docs/panel.png)

The same checks, in the right sidebar: type a folder, an `owner/repo`, or a GitHub link, and it says which one would fail and why. Nothing is installed and nothing is written.

## Three paths

| You are… | Start with | Then |
| --- | --- | --- |
| writing your first plugin | [`init`](#1-write-a-plugin) | `doctor`, `fix`, `verify` |
| changing a panel that is already installed | [`dev`](#2-develop-a-panel) | `mount`, the testkit, `audit` |
| shipping a version | [`verify`](#3-ship-a-version) | `release`, `index` |

It also installs as a plugin. `dsh plugin add dsh-plugin-toolkit` puts a
**插件体检 / Plugin doctor** panel under the conversation and a tab in the right
sidebar. Give it a folder that holds a plugin's `package.json`, or just
`owner/repo` — or a repository name, which it searches GitHub for and lists the
candidates to pick from. It then runs the same checks `verify` runs and says
which one would break the install, with the reason on the line — the same
answers as the CLI, without leaving the app.

```
$ dsh plugin add dsh-plugin-toolkit
```

### 1. Write a plugin

[`init`](#start-from-a-plugin-that-already-passes) writes the files whose absence shows up as a failed first publish — `engines.dsh`, the patch file, a `files` list that ships the code, a client bundle, a test for it, and the CI that runs both. `doctor` then checks the same things without writing anything, and [`verify`](#prove-the-tarball-works-not-just-the-repository) checks the tarball instead of the working copy.

If a plugin already exists, `doctor --fix` turns the failing checks into a
repair plan. It names the file and the edit for every problem, writes nothing
until you add `--write`, and then runs the checks again. `fix --engines` is
still there when the host range is the only thing you need to change.

```sh
npx dsh-plugin-toolkit@latest init ./my-panel --name my-panel
cd my-panel && npm install && npm test && npx dsh-plugin-toolkit@latest doctor .
```

### 2. Develop a panel

A plugin's client code is one file that calls `window.__ModuleLoader__.load({factory})` — there is no module to import, so the usual React test setup does not apply. [`testkit`](#test-a-panel-without-a-browser) supplies the missing half, and [`dev`](#edit-a-plugin-that-is-already-installed) pushes a rebuilt bundle into the running app.

```sh
npx dsh-plugin-toolkit@latest mount ./client.js     # what a user would see, without the app
npx dsh-plugin-toolkit@latest dev . --host http://127.0.0.1:54133
```

### 3. Ship a version

`verify` first (it is the only check that reads the tarball), then `release`, which tags, waits for the registry, writes the index entry with the publish time the registry reports, and — with `--pr --merge` — opens and merges the pull request.

```sh
npx dsh-plugin-toolkit@latest verify .
npx dsh-plugin-toolkit@latest release . --pr --merge
```

## What `verify` actually does

![Five steps, and the failure each one catches](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/WJDdidi-1/dsh-plugin-toolkit/main/docs/pipeline.svg)

The order matters. Packing first means the check reads the file list npm will publish, not the folder you have. Installing the tarball means the root is imported by its bare specifier — the package name the loader uses — not by a file path taken from `main` or `exports["."]`. Node ignores `main` once `exports` exists, so a package whose `exports` map has no `"."` entry fails with `ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED` at that step even though the file is present. Mounting means the client bundle is actually executed, in jsdom, with a host that records what it registered.

Each step exists because a plugin once got past the step before it and still installed into nothing.

## Why this exists

Releasing one plugin fifteen times taught me three things the ecosystem's tooling does not cover:

1. **A version is not shipped when npm accepts it.** Registry propagation took two to eight minutes every time. `npm view` answered from a stale local cache, so I repeatedly believed a release had failed when it had not — and once believed it had succeeded when the market still could not see it.
2. **The market index is a second release, done by hand.** Each version needs an entry carrying `publishTimestamp` from the registry and `engines.dsh` from the manifest. Forget the range and the index validator rejects the PR with `Engines mismatch` — after the tag is already public.
3. **Reading a manifest is not the same as checking it.** A plugin can have a valid `package.json` and still be uninstallable: `files` that omit the entry the manifest points at, a bundle patch that does not exist, a README that never states the host range it declares.

The five failures behind these checks — a red dot with no panel, a row the host drops, an app that disables every plugin after one unguarded `apply()`, a tab nothing can open, and a checker that was wrong — are written up with their exact error text and how to reproduce each one: [Five plugins that installed and did nothing](https://github.com/WJDdidi-1/dsh-plugin-toolkit/blob/main/docs/why-it-exists.md).

### Four ways a plugin installs and still does nothing

Each of these shipped in a real version of this toolkit before the check below existed. A manifest check passes on all four.

| What you see | What it was | Caught by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The tab is a red dot and the panel never opens | `exports["."]` pointed at the CLI, so the loader's row had no plugin to apply | `root export` |
| The plugin is installed, the app never serves it | `dsh.client` declared, `exports["./client"]` missing — the host drops the row | `client declaration` |
| The app says the third-party plugin is unsupported and disables all of them | `apply()` read `ctx.webServer` without declaring it; cordis throws instead of returning `undefined` | `verify` (calls `apply` on a context that has no services) |
| The tab registers, and nothing in the UI opens it | `sidebarRightTabs.register()` registers a *type*; the sidebar lists what `tabs.guide()` returns | a testkit test, not `doctor` |

The first three are static: `doctor` and `verify` catch them without the app running. The fourth is a UI contract, so it needs the panel mounted and the registration inspected — that is what [`testkit`](#test-a-panel-without-a-browser) is for.

## Requirements

- Node.js 18 or newer (the registry is read with `fetch`; no runtime dependencies)
- Git and `gh` on `PATH` for the steps that touch GitHub
- DeepSeek Harness `>=0.2.0` — the version whose market index carries `engines.dsh`, which is what makes the range check meaningful
- For `testkit`: `jsdom`, `react` and `react-dom` as dev dependencies (`npm install --save-dev jsdom react react-dom`)

## Start from a plugin that already passes

```sh
$ npx dsh-plugin-toolkit@latest init ./my-panel --name my-panel --title "My panel"
created 8 file(s) in /Users/you/my-panel
  .github/workflows/ci.yml
  .gitignore
  README.md
  client.js
  cordis.patch.yml
  index.js
  package.json
  test/panel.test.mjs

next: npm install && npm test && npm run doctor
```

What you get is not a snippet: it is a plugin whose `doctor` already passes (`engines.dsh`, the patch file, the `files` list), with a client bundle that registers a sidebar tab, a testkit test for it, and a CI workflow that runs both. `init` refuses a directory that is not empty unless you pass `--force`, and refuses a name npm would refuse — those are the two mistakes that cost the most time later.

Every command that takes a path expands a leading `~` before touching the filesystem. The tool, not the shell, expands `~` for these arguments: `cmd` and PowerShell pass `"~/my-panel"` through literally, while a POSIX shell usually expands it first. `init '~/my-panel' --name my-panel` writes into your home directory (the same files `init ~/my-panel` writes on a POSIX shell), and `doctor '~/my-panel'` reads it back. The Windows spelling `~\my-panel` works too; a directory literally named `~` is never created.

## Where it lives

The checker is docked **under the conversation**, above the input bar: a single
row, collapsed by default. Open it and it carries the whole guide — who it is
for, how to use it, what each check means, and what it cannot tell you — plus
the folder field and the results. The same panel is also a **Plugin doctor** tab
in the right sidebar, for when the conversation is busy.

The panel speaks both languages and opens in Chinese; the 中文 / EN switch sits
in the dock's header row (and in the sidebar tab) and the choice is remembered.

Look at it without the app:

```sh
node scripts/preview.mjs /tmp/panel.html   # collapsed, open, with a result, and the tab
```

## Test a panel without a browser

A plugin's client code is one file that calls `window.__ModuleLoader__.load({factory})` — there is no module to import, so the usual React test setup does not apply. `testkit` supplies the missing half: a DOM, the real React, and a host context that records what the panel registers.

```sh
npm install --save-dev jsdom react react-dom
```

```js
import { mountClient, createFetch } from 'dsh-plugin-toolkit/testkit';

const panel = await mountClient({
  file: 'client.js',
  copy: { 'my-plugin': { title: 'My panel' } },
  fetch: createFetch({
    '/my-plugin/report': { body: { score: 71, noise: 3 } },
    '/my-plugin/apply': () => ({ status: 201, body: { score: 92 } }),
  }),
});

await panel.click('[data-testid="optimize"]');
console.assert(panel.text().includes('92'), 'the score on screen did not move');
console.assert(panel.must('[role="status"]').textContent.includes('92'));
await panel.unmount();
```

`unmount()` is async: it lets React finish the work its own unmount schedules before the DOM goes away. Skipping the `await` surfaces as `ReferenceError: window is not defined` *after* the test has already passed, which is a confusing way to learn it.

What you get back: `text()`, `html()`, `query(selector)`, `must(selector)` (throws with the rendered HTML when it misses), `click(selector)`, `type(selector, value)`, `press(selector, key)`, `focus`, `attributes(selector)`, `snapshot(dir, name)` for a normalised DOM baseline, and `host` for assertions about what the bundle registered.

### Keep a visual baseline

The DOM is the baseline: normalising class order and whitespace gives a file that fails for the reasons a screenshot would — a lost label, a control that stopped rendering — and can be reviewed in a diff instead of by eye.

```js
import { expectSnapshot } from 'dsh-plugin-toolkit/testkit';

const panel = await mountClient({ file: 'client.js' });
expectSnapshot(panel.html(), '__snapshots__', 'panel');   // throws with the element that moved
await panel.unmount();
```

First run writes nothing: it tells you to re-run with `UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS=1`, so a baseline is always a decision, never a side effect. That rerun writes the normalised HTML and returns `{ status: 'written' }`; later runs return `same` or fail with the element that moved.

### Check what assistive tech sees

```js
panel.expectAria('[role="tab"][aria-selected="true"]', { label: 'Protection', selected: 'true' });
assert.match(panel.must('[role="status"]').textContent, /Score moved 71 → 77/);
```

`expectAria()` compares the attributes a screen reader actually reads — `role`,
`label`, `live`, `selected`, `expanded`, `checked`, `pressed`, `disabled` — and
names the one that differs:

```
[aria-live="polite"]: expected aria text to be "9", but it is "0"
```

A missing attribute is reported as `nothing`, not as an empty string, because
those are different bugs. `panel.aria(selector)` returns the same object when you
want to assert on it yourself.

`must()` throws with the rendered markup when the selector misses, which is the difference between "the assertion failed" and "here is what the user actually got".

Every example below is a file in this repository, run by CI, and the output shown is the output it prints:

| Example | What it shows |
| --- | --- |
| `node examples/mount-a-bundle.mjs` | mount a real bundle, read the text, click, read it again |
| `node examples/route-stubs.mjs` | answer the routes a panel asks for, and assert on the requests |
| `node examples/baseline.mjs` | a DOM baseline compared on every run |
| `node examples/aria.mjs` | what assistive tech sees |

```sh
$ node examples/mount-a-bundle.mjs
Demo panel Count 0 0
Demo panel Count 1 1
```

```sh
$ node examples/route-stubs.mjs
Score 71
asked for: 1 route(s), undeclared route answers 404
```

To look at a bundle by hand:

```sh
npx dsh-plugin mount ./client.js            # print the text a user would see
npx dsh-plugin mount ./client.js --html     # print the markup
```

That is how the AIignore panel was checked before release: the real bundle, mounted in Node, against a stubbed `/aiignore/*`:

```
$ npx dsh-plugin mount ../ai-context-doctor/plugin/client.js
AIignore No workspace yet Could not read the report …
```

## Put the badge on a plugin that passes

If `verify` passes on your plugin, this badge says so and links back here:

```md
[![checked with dsh-plugin-toolkit](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/WJDdidi-1/dsh-plugin-toolkit/main/docs/badge.svg)](https://github.com/WJDdidi-1/dsh-plugin-toolkit)
```

It is a claim, not a decoration: add it only when `dsh-plugin verify .` exits 0.

## Start from the example

[`dsh-plugin-example`](https://github.com/WJDdidi-1/dsh-plugin-example) is a ~70-line plugin: one sidebar tab, two languages, one behaviour test, CI that runs `verify` through the composite action. It is the shape this toolkit expects, so it is also the fastest way to see whether the toolkit fits your plugin. It is a GitHub template too: **Use this template** starts you on a plugin whose first publish already passes.

```sh
dsh plugin add dsh-plugin-example
```

## See what is installed, and what the app loaded

`doctor` checks one folder you name. The question that actually gets asked is
"why is my plugin not in the sidebar?", and the answer needs three things at once:
what is installed, whether each installed copy is valid, and which of them the
running app actually loaded.

```sh
$ dsh-plugin audit --host http://127.0.0.1:54133
dsh-aiignore           0.37.1    loaded       ok
demo-panel             0.3.0     not loaded   ok  — dsh.profile.bundles in /Users/me/.dsh/profiles/desktop/package.json does not list it, and the loader mounts only listed bundles
                                            fix: add "demo-panel" to dsh.profile.bundles in /Users/me/.dsh/profiles/desktop/package.json (or run `dsh plugin add demo-panel`), then restart the app

1 installed plugin(s) are not in the running app:
```

"Not loaded" has three different causes, and `audit` names the one that applies
instead of offering a blanket restart:

- **Not in `dsh.profile.bundles`.** `pnpm add` (or `npm install`) installs the
  package but does not tell the loader to mount it. Add the package name to
  `dsh.profile.bundles` in `~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/package.json`, or run
  `dsh plugin add <name>`, then restart the app.
- **No `dsh.bundle`.** The package declares `dsh` but no patch file to mount.
  Add `dsh.bundle.patch` to its `package.json` and ship the patch file, then
  reinstall.
- **Listed, but the app predates the install.** The profile is already correct;
  restart the app once to read the new list.

Advisories (`engines.dsh`, README Requirements) are counted apart from problems:
the market index needs them, the loader does not, so they should not bury a plugin
that is actually broken.

`audit` exits `1` when an installed plugin has a hard failure **or** when the
running app did not load at least one installed plugin, so CI can gate on a
profile where the app silently skipped a plugin. It exits `0` when every
installed plugin is loaded and valid. When `--host` is given but the app cannot
be reached, the command has not observed the graph it was asked for: it prints
the `/plugins/events` URL it could not read, prints no plugin rows or clean
summary, and exits `2` so a CI gate cannot pass against an unreachable app.
Without `--host`, the loaded column is `?` and only hard failures change the
exit code.

`audit --home <dir>` scans a different profile home; both `~/.dsh` and
`~\.dsh` expand. A bare `--home`, or one followed by another flag such as
`--timeout 50` or `--json`, is a missing value rather than a request to scan
`$HOME/.dsh` or a folder literally named after the flag: the command exits `2`,
names `--home`, and prints no profile report.

Without `--host` the loaded column is `?`, because guessing would be worse than
saying nothing. Only packages that declare a `dsh` field are audited — the rest of
`node_modules` is ordinary dependencies, and auditing those is noise.

An installed package whose `package.json` cannot be read is the exception: the
`dsh` field that would mark it as a plugin is in the file that failed to parse.
If its name is still in `dsh.profile.bundles`, `audit` reports a `manifest`
failure naming the unreadable `package.json` and exits `1` instead of treating
the folder as an ordinary dependency. A truncated manifest from an interrupted
install therefore cannot make the plugin disappear from the report, and a valid
sibling plugin is still listed on the same run. The exception stays narrow: a
damaged `package.json` in a package that is neither in `dsh.profile.bundles` nor
readable enough to expose a `dsh` field is still an ordinary dependency and is
skipped, so one broken transitive install does not fail every audit.

A declared bundle can also be missing entirely. If a name stays in
`dsh.profile.bundles` after its `node_modules/<name>` folder is removed (an
interrupted install, or a package deleted by hand), `audit` prints a `missing`
row with an `install` failure naming the absent folder and exits `1`, while
still listing the healthy plugins on the same run. An absent package that the
profile never declared is not an install record, so it is not invented in the
report; a regression test removes the name from the profile and requires the
shipped CLI to exit `0` without printing it.

## Edit a plugin that is already installed

The host already swaps a rebuilt bundle without a page reload: it watches each plugin's entry artifact and reports a `rebuilt` frame on `/plugins/events`. `dev` puts the new file where the host is looking, then **proves** the frame arrived instead of asking you to check by eye.

```sh
npx dsh-plugin dev . --host http://127.0.0.1:54133
```

![dsh-plugin dev printing the revision the app reported](docs/dev.gif)

*Recorded from a real run against the running app: the last line is the revision the app sent back on `/plugins/events`, not a message the tool printed on faith.*

```
demo-aiignore: /work/plugin/client.js -> ~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/node_modules/dsh-aiignore/client.js
initial: copied 163647 bytes at 1:18:43 AM
reloaded dsh-aiignore (rev e0c0230c4fc9)
watching /work/plugin
```

That last line is the whole point: the revision came back from the app's own event stream, so "it reloaded" is a fact, not a hope.

A plugin the running app never loaded cannot be reloaded, and the app says so by leaving it out of the graph it sends first. `dev` reads that graph, so a freshly installed plugin gets the sentence that fixes it instead of a timeout:

```
copied, but not confirmed: the running app has not loaded demo-panel, so it will not report a reload; restart the app once after installing it
```

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--dest <dir>` | write into this installed copy instead of searching `~/.dsh/profiles/*/node_modules/<name>` |
| `--entry <file>` | copy this file instead of `dsh.client.entry`, `client.js`, `lib/client.js` |
| `--build <command>` | run this before each copy (a failed build copies nothing) |
| `--host <url>` | confirm the reload against the app at this URL; without it the copy still happens and the tool says it is unconfirmed |
| `--once` | copy once and exit, for scripts |

Two things it does not do, because the host does not: React state inside the reloaded plugin is lost, and a failed swap does not roll back to the previous bundle.

## Use it in CI

The same checks run as a GitHub Action, so a tag cannot go out on a plugin that would not install:

```yaml
- uses: actions/checkout@v4
- uses: WJDdidi-1/dsh-plugin-toolkit@v1
  with:
    dir: plugin        # the folder holding the plugin's package.json
    command: verify    # pack it, install the tarball, mount the panel
```

`verify` is the default because it is the only check that reads what a user
actually installs: `doctor` reads the working copy, so a `files` list that
forgets `client.js` passes it and fails only after `npm i`.

`command: doctor` stops at the manifest checks (fast, no install), and
`command: index` audits `market/index.json` instead, failing on any version whose
`engines.dsh` is missing or is not a semver range (a malformed value such as
`>=banana`, or a single pinned version such as `0.2.0`, both fail). Pin
`version:` if you would rather not track the latest release.

## Check a plugin you have not cloned

The panel takes three kinds of input: a folder, `owner/repo`, or a GitHub URL.
A bare name is a search, not a guess — it asks GitHub, lists the matches with
their stars, and checks the one you pick. A repository is downloaded once as a
tarball into a temp folder, so nothing is cloned into your workspace and
nothing is installed.

The CLI reads a repository straight from the GitHub API:

```bash
dsh-plugin doctor --remote V1ki/dsh-plugin-subscriptions
```

```text
dsh-plugin doctor: 1 problem(s) in V1ki/dsh-plugin-subscriptions
  ⨯ engines.dsh: engines.dsh is missing, so a host that enforces the range rejects the install as "incompatible with dsh"; declare the range you support, e.g. "engines": { "dsh": ">=0.2.0" }
```

That is the whole reason this mode exists: the plugin hub files failed installs
back into plugin repositories, and the report is a sentence — `plugin install
failed`, `plugin does not support the DSH version in use` — that never names a
file. Reading `package.json` over the API is enough to name it.

What it can see, and what it cannot:

- Manifest checks (`engines.dsh`, `dsh field`, `files`, `dsh.client`,
  `exports`) run on the real `package.json`.
- README checks (`readme`) run on the text GitHub serves: the README must have
  a `Requirements` heading and must state the host range `package.json`
  declares. A repository whose checkout fails `readme` fails the remote check
  too, with the same sentence.
- File checks (does `exports["./client"]` point at a file that exists, does the
  root export `apply`) need the tree. A package that runs `prepack`,
  `prepublishOnly`, `prepare` or `build` publishes files it does not commit, so
  those checks are **skipped with a note** instead of calling a working plugin
  broken.
- Public repositories work anonymously, but GitHub allows 60 requests an hour.
  Export `GH_TOKEN` (or `GITHUB_TOKEN`) to audit more than one or two.

To check a whole list in one pass, put one `owner/repo` per line in a file and
pass it with `--from` (`-` reads standard input):

```sh
$ dsh-plugin audit --remote --from repos.txt
```

Repositories are read four at a time by default. `--jobs N` changes that width;
values above `8` are capped at `8`, and `--jobs 1` walks the list one repository
at a time, the timing the command had before batching. The output — and the
`--json` array — still follows the input list, and every verdict is the one the
sequential run produced, so a diff between two runs compares repositories rather
than scheduling.

When GitHub answers `403` or `429`, the shared quota is gone, so the batch stops
starting new repositories and marks every entry it could not read as
`rate-limited` instead of `clean` or `unreadable`. If the response carries
`x-ratelimit-reset` (or `retry-after`), the reset time is printed with the
verdict, and the remaining entries are reported without another request.

### Will this plugin install on my DSH?

The eight compatibility reports, from four repositories, all end with the same
question. Add `--host <version>` to a remote audit and it answers that question
for one repository. This is the output for `L3n3L/dsh-resume`, a real plugin
whose declared range stops before DSH 0.2.0, checked against the
`0.2.2-alpha.3` canary from the reports. The checked-in sample is a frozen 0.1.3
snapshot, so the line stays true as the upstream repository changes:

```sh
$ dsh-plugin audit --remote L3n3L/dsh-resume --host 0.2.2-alpha.3
incompatible  L3n3L/dsh-resume  0.1.3 (host >=0.1.0-rc.6 <0.2.0-0) [incompatible with dsh 0.2.2-alpha.3; declares ">=0.1.0-rc.6 <0.2.0-0"]

summary: 1 repository — 0 clean, 1 failing (1 problem), 0 unreadable, 0 rate-limited
```

The verdict comes first: `incompatible` means the range in `package.json` does
not accept the host, so the installer rejects the plugin before it unpacks it.
This run exits `1`. The same answer is reproducible without a GitHub request:
the checked-in snapshot under `examples/compatibility-sample/` keeps the 0.1.3
manifest fields that decide compatibility, and its `## Requirements` heading
isolates the host-range answer. This command feeds that snapshot through the
real CLI path:

```sh
$ node scripts/compatibility-sample.mjs
```

(`npm run compatibility` runs the same script.) The test suite runs that
command and compares its output with the block above, so the sample cannot
drift from the formatter or from the README. Running
`dsh-plugin audit --remote L3n3L/dsh-resume --host 0.2.2-alpha.3` without the
sample audits the repository's current default branch instead; a README or
manifest change since 0.1.3 can add another `readme` or manifest failure to the
same row.

The line carries the range `package.json` declares and one of `compatible`,
`incompatible`, or `unknown` against that host version. `unknown` is the honest
answer for a missing or malformed range — there is nothing to compare — while a
range that excludes the host is `incompatible`, counted as failing, and exits
`1`. npm's pre-release rule is part of the answer: `>=0.2.0` does not accept
`0.2.2-alpha.3`, because a range only opts into a pre-release when it names one
of the same `major.minor.patch`. A canary host can therefore be `incompatible`
with a range that will accept the final release. The same flag works in the
batch mode, so one `--from` run answers the whole list:

```sh
$ dsh-plugin audit --remote --from repos.txt --host 0.2.2-alpha.3
```

The compatibility flags are `--remote <owner/repo>` for one repository,
`--from <file>` for a list (`-` reads standard input), `--host <version>` for
the DSH version to compare against, and `--json` for the machine-readable
finding. `--jobs <n>` sets the batch width, and `--patch-dir <dir>` writes the
host-targeted repair for each repository that needs one. The help text lists
the same flags; a test fails if this section names a flag the CLI does not have.
A bare `--host` is a usage error, not an audit without the comparison: the
command exits `2` before it reads GitHub, and `--host --json` does not consume
the `--json` flag as a version.

`--host` still names the running app URL for a local `audit`; on `--remote` it
is the DSH version to compare against. With `--json`, each finding gains
`host` and `compatibility` beside `hostRange`.

Each repository gets one line with its verdict — `clean`, `failing`,
`unreadable`, or `rate-limited` — and the run ends with a counted summary:

```text
clean         demo/plugin  1.2.3 (host >=0.2.0)
failing       demo/broken  — engines.dsh: engines.dsh is missing, so a host that enforces the range rejects the install as "incompatible with dsh"
rate-limited  demo/blocked — GitHub rate-limited this request (403) for package.json; set GH_TOKEN or GITHUB_TOKEN to raise the limit; the limit resets at 2026-11-04T20:00:00.000Z
rate-limited  demo/next    — GitHub rate-limited the batch before this repository was read, so it was not requested; the li

decision.reason: The frozen manifest is an example, fixture, template, evaluation support package, rollback copy, or archive rather than a catalog entry.
